question_text: Are you supposed to stop before the white line or after?
answer_text_a: After
answer_text_b: There's no need to stop
answer_text_c: Before
correct_answer: C. Before
answer_information_text: A stop line tells you where the vehicle must come to a complete stop. Stop before the line, then proceed only when it is safe and you have complied with any applicable robot, sign or traffic-officer instruction.

question_text: Are you allowed to drive a car alone if you only have your learner's licence?
answer_text_a: Yes
answer_text_b: No
answer_text_c: Only if you are older than 21
correct_answer: B. No
answer_information_text: A learner may ride a motorcycle alone, but a learner driving a car must have a licensed accompanying driver.

question_text: Which of the following is true?
answer_text_a: You are not allowed to drive bakkies on weekends
answer_text_b: Your vehicle can not have a radio
answer_text_c: You must always use your indicator before changing lanes
correct_answer: C. You must always use your indicator before changing lanes
answer_information_text: You must signal before changing lanes so other road users are warned of your intended movement. Check that it is safe, signal in good time and move only when you will not endanger or obstruct another road user.

question_text: Are you allowed to drive a motor vehicle that requires number plates on a public road without them if no valid permit or lawful exemption allows this?
answer_text_a: Yes, if you are only making a short trip.
answer_text_b: No.
answer_text_c: Yes, if the vehicle displays a valid licence disc.
correct_answer: B. No.
answer_information_text: A motor vehicle must display its required number plates when used on a public road unless a valid permit or lawful exemption allows otherwise. A valid licence disc alone does not excuse missing number plates.

question_text: What should you do if a traffic officer instructs you to disobey a road sign?
answer_text_a: Leave the area immediately
answer_text_b: Do exactly what he/she says
answer_text_c: Ignore whatever they say
correct_answer: B. Do exactly what he/she says
answer_information_text: A traffic officer's lawful instruction takes priority over a road sign. Follow the instruction promptly and safely because an officer may temporarily control traffic differently from the normal sign or robot.

question_text: What should you do if your phone rings while you are driving?
answer_text_a: You can only answer it if you are in a red car
answer_text_b: Answer it and tell your boss to call you back later
answer_text_c: When it is safe, pull off to the side of the road and answer the call
correct_answer: C. When it is safe, pull off to the side of the road and answer the call
answer_information_text: When it is safe, pull off the road in a suitable place, stop, and then answer the call without creating a danger or obstruction.

question_text: Are you allowed to use your hooter to greet your friend?
answer_text_a: No
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: Only if you haven't seen them for a while
correct_answer: A. No
answer_information_text: A hooter may be used only when necessary for safety, such as warning another road user of danger. Greeting a friend is not a safety reason, so it is not a lawful use of the hooter.

question_text: What should you do if an ambulance approaches from behind sounding its siren or displaying its emergency identification lamp?
answer_text_a: Continue at the same speed and leave it to find a way past.
answer_text_b: Give it immediate and absolute right of way, safely making room for it to pass.
answer_text_c: Give way only if both its siren and emergency identification lamp are operating.
correct_answer: B. Give it immediate and absolute right of way, safely making room for it to pass.
answer_information_text: An ambulance sounding its siren or displaying its emergency identification lamp must be given immediate and absolute right of way. Make room safely, changing lanes only if necessary and safe.

question_text: Except for bus-trains and twin-steer four-axle rigid goods vehicles, what is the maximum permitted turning radius for a motor vehicle operated on a public road?
answer_text_a: 13.1 metres
answer_text_b: 17.5 metres
answer_text_c: 8.5 metres
correct_answer: A. 13.1 metres
answer_information_text: The general maximum permitted turning radius is 13.1 metres. Bus-trains and twin-steer four-axle rigid goods vehicles may have a turning radius of up to 17.5 metres.

question_text: Are you allowed to drive your vehicle on a public road if your brake lights are not working?
answer_text_a: No
answer_text_b: only during the day
answer_text_c: Yes
correct_answer: A. No
answer_information_text: A vehicle may not be driven on a public road if its brake lights are not working. Stop lamps must be fitted, visible and maintained in good working order so following traffic is warned when you brake.

question_text: Are you allowed to drive with only your park lights on?
answer_text_a: Only during the day
answer_text_b: No
answer_text_c: Yes
correct_answer: B. No
answer_information_text: Parking lights may be on with the required headlamps, but you may not drive with only the parking lights lit.

question_text: How far ahead should your main-beams brighten the road ahead?
answer_text_a: 40 metres
answer_text_b: 220 metres
answer_text_c: 100 metres
correct_answer: C. 100 metres
answer_information_text: Main-beam headlights must illuminate far enough ahead for the driver to see a person, vehicle or substantial object at least 100 metres away. This gives the driver enough distance to identify hazards and react safely.

question_text: Are you allowed to tow a vehicle on a freeway with a minimum speed of more than 30 km/h without a solid tow bar?
answer_text_a: No
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: Only if you are towing a truck
correct_answer: A. No
answer_information_text: A tow rope or chain may not be used above 30 km/h without a solid tow-bar, so a freeway with a higher minimum speed requires one.

question_text: Are you allowed to stop on a public road if a traffic officer instructs you to do so?
answer_text_a: Only if you are driving a truck
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: No
correct_answer: B. Yes
answer_information_text: A traffic officer may direct a driver to stop, and that instruction must be obeyed. Stop in a controlled and safe manner where the officer directs you, even if normal road rules would otherwise restrict stopping there.

question_text: Is an ambulance allowed to park on the road if they are carrying out their duties?
answer_text_a: Only on weekdays
answer_text_b: No, they have to follow the rules of the road
answer_text_c: Yes, if necessary for their duties, provided it does not create unnecessary danger or confusion and the prescribed identification lamps are displayed
correct_answer: C. Yes, if necessary for their duties, provided it does not create unnecessary danger or confusion and the prescribed identification lamps are displayed
answer_information_text: An ambulance may stop or park where its duties make it necessary, but it must not create unnecessary danger or confusion and must display its prescribed identification lamps.

question_text: Which of the following may happen if you are illegally parked?
answer_text_a: You will automatically be arrested
answer_text_b: You may be fined or your vehicle may be removed and impounded
answer_text_c: Your driving licence will automatically be cancelled
correct_answer: B. You may be fined or your vehicle may be removed and impounded
answer_information_text: Illegal parking can result in a fine. A traffic officer may also remove and impound an illegally parked vehicle.

question_text: You are not allowed to park your vehicle in a place where...
answer_text_a: In your garage
answer_text_b: It will obstruct vehicles passing by
answer_text_c: You are allowed to
correct_answer: B. It will obstruct vehicles passing by
answer_information_text: Parking must not hinder the free and proper passage of traffic. A vehicle may not be left where it obstructs vehicles passing on the road or blocks a lawful entrance.

question_text: You are not allowed to...
answer_text_a: Have a sunroof in your vehicle
answer_text_b: Talk to your passengers while driving
answer_text_c: Break the speed limit when you are overtaking
correct_answer: C. Break the speed limit when you are overtaking
answer_information_text: The speed limit remains binding while overtaking. Overtaking must be completed only when safe and within the applicable posted or general speed limit; needing to go faster is not a legal exception.

question_text: What is the speed limit within urban areas?
answer_text_a: 60 km/h
answer_text_b: 80 km/h
answer_text_c: 25 km/h
correct_answer: A. 60 km/h
answer_information_text: The general speed limit on a public road within an urban area is 60 km/h unless a different limit is displayed. A lower signed limit must also be obeyed.

question_text: What is the general speed limit on a freeway?
answer_text_a: 80 km/h
answer_text_b: 120 km/h
answer_text_c: 100 km/h
correct_answer: B. 120 km/h
answer_information_text: The general speed limit on a freeway is 120 km/h unless a lower limit is displayed for that section or for a particular class of vehicle. Road, weather, traffic and visibility conditions may require you to drive below the maximum.

question_text: Your vehicle must be fitted with...
answer_text_a: Water-filled tyres
answer_text_b: Sand-filled tyres
answer_text_c: Pneumatic tyres
correct_answer: C. Pneumatic tyres
answer_information_text: A vehicle operated on a public road must be fitted with pneumatic tyres. The tyres must also be in safe condition, with a visible tread pattern and no dangerous damage.

question_text: For a car fitted with pneumatic tyres without tread-depth indicators, what is the minimum legal tread depth?
answer_text_a: 0.1 millimetre
answer_text_b: 1 millimetre
answer_text_c: 0.5 millimetre
correct_answer: B. 1 millimetre
answer_information_text: Each tyre must have a tread depth of at least 1 millimetre. Its tread pattern must also be clearly visible across the tyre's full width and all the way around it.

question_text: Are you allowed to immediately stop your vehicle if you've been involved in an accident?
answer_text_a: No
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: Only if it's the weekend
correct_answer: B. Yes
answer_information_text: You must stop immediately after being involved in an accident. This allows you to check for injuries, exchange details and comply with the police and accident-reporting requirements.

question_text: You were the driver in an accident causing injury or property damage. May you drink alcohol to calm down before completing the required reporting and any medical examination required by a traffic officer, if no medical practitioner has instructed or administered it for injury or shock?
answer_text_a: Yes, if you will not drive again that day.
answer_text_b: Yes, if you have exchanged details with the other driver.
answer_text_c: No.
correct_answer: C. No.
answer_information_text: A driver involved in such an accident must not drink alcohol until the applicable reporting requirements and any medical examination required by a traffic officer are completed. The exception is alcohol instructed or administered by a medical practitioner for injury or shock.

question_text: You are NOT allowed to drive your vehicle on a public road if...
answer_text_a: You drive in a reckless manner
answer_text_b: If you have 20 inch wheels
answer_text_c: It does not have a radio
correct_answer: A. You drive in a reckless manner
answer_information_text: Driving in a reckless or negligent manner is an offence under the National Road Traffic Act, whatever you are driving. The size of your wheels and whether the vehicle has a radio have nothing to do with whether it may legally be driven.

question_text: If you are not a professional driver, you may not drive a motor vehicle on a public road when your blood-alcohol concentration is equal to or greater than...
answer_text_a: 0.005 grams per 100 ml of blood
answer_text_b: 0.0005 grams per 100 ml of blood
answer_text_c: 0.05 grams per 100 ml of blood
correct_answer: C. 0.05 grams per 100 ml of blood
answer_information_text: For a non-professional driver, driving on a public road with a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.05 grams per 100 ml or more is prohibited. For professional drivers, the threshold is 0.02 grams per 100 ml.

question_text: Which of the following is true?
answer_text_a: You can only drive a red vehicle on a freeway
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to listen to your radio on the weekend
answer_text_c: You are not allowed to turn at an intersection if it will cause harm to other road users
correct_answer: C. You are not allowed to turn at an intersection if it will cause harm to other road users
answer_information_text: You must not turn at an intersection if your turn will cause harm or danger to other road users. Before turning, check the traffic and wait until the movement can be completed safely.

question_text: Are you allowed to drive on the shoulder of the road beyond the left yellow line?
answer_text_a: Yes, but only during daylight, while another vehicle is overtaking you, on a road with one lane in each direction, when it is safe and visibility is at least 150 metres
answer_text_b: No
answer_text_c: Yes
correct_answer: A. Yes, but only during daylight, while another vehicle is overtaking you, on a road with one lane in each direction, when it is safe and visibility is at least 150 metres
answer_information_text: Normally you must stay off the shoulder. A limited daytime exception applies on a two-way road when another vehicle is overtaking you and it is safe with 150 metres of visibility.

question_text: Are you allowed to cross a single solid white no-overtaking line to overtake a moving vehicle?
answer_text_a: Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
answer_text_b: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is moving slowly.
answer_text_c: No.
correct_answer: C. No.
answer_information_text: You may not cross a single solid white no-overtaking line to overtake a moving vehicle. You may cross it to access property or pass a stationary obstruction, provided it is safe to do so.

question_text: What is the maximum speed limit on non-urban roads for a goods vehicle with a gross vehicle mass exceeding 9 000 kg, where no lower speed limit applies?
answer_text_a: 120 km/h
answer_text_b: 80 km/h
answer_text_c: 100 km/h
correct_answer: B. 80 km/h
answer_information_text: A goods vehicle with a gross vehicle mass exceeding 9 000 kg is subject to an 80 km/h speed limit. A lower speed limit must be obeyed wherever it applies.

question_text: When should you increase your following distance?
answer_text_a: When travelling in wet conditions
answer_text_b: Only when your radio is on
answer_text_c: If you are driving on a Monday
correct_answer: A. When travelling in wet conditions
answer_information_text: Increase your following distance in wet conditions because the road is less grippy and your vehicle takes longer to stop. The extra space also gives you more time to react if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly.

question_text: Where should you keep your driver's licence?
answer_text_a: On you while driving
answer_text_b: At work in a safe cupboard
answer_text_c: At home when you go out
correct_answer: A. On you while driving
answer_information_text: You must carry your driver's licence with you whenever you drive. A traffic officer may require you to produce it during a roadside inspection.

question_text: Before signalling to move forward from a parked position, what should you do?
answer_text_a: Release the parking brake before checking for traffic.
answer_text_b: Check your mirrors and the appropriate blind spot for surrounding traffic.
answer_text_c: Begin moving forward, then check your mirrors.
correct_answer: B. Check your mirrors and the appropriate blind spot for surrounding traffic.
answer_information_text: Check your mirrors and the appropriate blind spot before signalling your intention to move off. Observe again before moving, and proceed only when it is safe.

question_text: What colour warning lights does a fire-fighting vehicle have?
answer_text_a: Red
answer_text_b: Blue
answer_text_c: Green
correct_answer: A. Red
answer_information_text: A fire-fighting vehicle carries a red identification lamp. Regulation 176 of the National Road Traffic Regulations, 2000 keeps blue lamps for the police, traffic officers and similar law-enforcement vehicles, so blue on the road means enforcement, not fire or rescue.

question_text: What are you supposed to do if you are driving in heavy rain?
answer_text_a: Increase your speed
answer_text_b: Increase your following distance
answer_text_c: Decrease your following distance
correct_answer: B. Increase your following distance
answer_information_text: Heavy rain reduces visibility and makes the road slippery, so you need more time and distance to react and stop. Increase your following distance and reduce speed when conditions require it.

question_text: What is the speed limit for buses?
answer_text_a: 150 km/h
answer_text_b: 275 km/h
answer_text_c: 100 km/h
correct_answer: C. 100 km/h
answer_information_text: A bus has a maximum speed limit of 100 km/h where that limit applies. This lower limit allows for the bus’s size, weight and passenger-carrying responsibility.

question_text: Are you allowed to park in a disabled parking if you are conveying elderly people?
answer_text_a: No
answer_text_b: Only if you are over 65
answer_text_c: Yes
correct_answer: A. No
answer_information_text: A disabled parking bay is reserved for an authorised disabled person and vehicle displaying the required identification. Carrying elderly passengers does not give you permission to park there.

question_text: What are you supposed to do if there are pedestrians crossing the road?
answer_text_a: Don't stop as you have the right of way
answer_text_b: Drive around them
answer_text_c: Stop your vehicle and let them cross
correct_answer: C. Stop your vehicle and let them cross
answer_information_text: Pedestrians are vulnerable road users, especially while crossing. Slow down and stop when necessary to let them cross safely, particularly at a pedestrian crossing.

question_text: Can you carry a load on your vehicle if it will obscure the drivers view?
answer_text_a: No
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: Only if you are carrying wood
correct_answer: A. No
answer_information_text: A load must not block the driver’s view through the windscreen, side windows or mirrors. The driver must be able to see traffic and keep complete control of the vehicle.

question_text: Excluding a motorcycle sidecar headlamp, what is the minimum distance ahead at which dipped-beam headlights must enable you to see a person, vehicle or substantial object?
answer_text_a: 45 metres
answer_text_b: 100 metres
answer_text_c: 10 metres
correct_answer: A. 45 metres
answer_information_text: Dipped-beam headlights must enable the driver to see a person, vehicle or substantial object at least 45 metres ahead. This requirement does not apply to a dipped-beam headlamp fitted to a motorcycle sidecar.

question_text: Are you allowed to use your vehicle on a public road if it does not have an effective fuel cap?
answer_text_a: Only if you drive a Toyota
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: No
correct_answer: C. No
answer_information_text: No. An effective fuel cap is required to prevent fuel from spilling and vapour from escaping, which could create a fire and safety hazard. A vehicle without one may not be operated on a public road.

question_text: What should you do if there are animals crossing the road?
answer_text_a: Stop your vehicle
answer_text_b: Continue as you have right of way
answer_text_c: Only stop if horses are crossing
correct_answer: A. Stop your vehicle
answer_information_text: You must stop and wait when animals are crossing the road, and may only move off once they are all across and it is safe. Animals are unpredictable and cannot be expected to give way, so right of way does not apply to them.

question_text: Are you allowed to enter a public road if an obstruction ahead prevents you from entering safely?
answer_text_a: No.
answer_text_b: Yes, if you enter slowly.
answer_text_c: Yes, if you sound your hooter first.
correct_answer: A. No.
answer_information_text: You may enter a public road only when you can do so safely for yourself and other traffic.

question_text: Can you stop on a freeway shoulder, outside an area designated by a road sign for stopping or parking, solely to drink water?
answer_text_a: No
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: Only for 15 minutes
correct_answer: A. No
answer_information_text: You may not stop on an ordinary freeway shoulder solely to drink water. You may stop for refreshments in an area reserved for stopping or parking by an appropriate road traffic sign.

question_text: Which of the following is true?
answer_text_a: Under the ordinary height limits, a motor vehicle other than a double-deck bus, including its load, may not exceed 4.3 metres in overall height on a public road.
answer_text_b: The maximum permitted mass of every motor vehicle on a public road is 4.3 tonnes.
answer_text_c: A vehicle's load is excluded when measuring its overall height.
correct_answer: A. Under the ordinary height limits, a motor vehicle other than a double-deck bus, including its load, may not exceed 4.3 metres in overall height on a public road.
answer_information_text: The ordinary maximum overall height, including the load, is 4.3 metres for motor vehicles other than double-deck buses. For double-deck buses, it is 4.65 metres.

question_text: When are you not allowed to overtake a vehicle?
answer_text_a: When approaching a curve with a clear view ahead, enough room to pass safely and no overtaking restriction.
answer_text_b: When approaching a blind curve on a two-way road where passing requires entering the right-hand side of the roadway and restricted visibility could endanger oncoming traffic.
answer_text_c: When on a one-way road with enough room to pass safely and no overtaking restriction.
correct_answer: B. When approaching a blind curve on a two-way road where passing requires entering the right-hand side of the roadway and restricted visibility could endanger oncoming traffic.
answer_information_text: You must not overtake when approaching a curve if restricted visibility could make passing hazardous to oncoming traffic. This restriction does not apply if you can pass without entering the right-hand side of the roadway or if the roadway carries traffic in only one direction.

question_text: Illuminated brake lights normally indicate that...
answer_text_a: The vehicle’s service brake is being applied.
answer_text_b: The vehicle is turning left.
answer_text_c: The vehicle is accelerating.
correct_answer: A. The vehicle’s service brake is being applied.
answer_information_text: Brake lights indicate that the vehicle’s service brake is being applied. The vehicle may already be stationary.

question_text: Your friend borrows your vehicle and is stopped and identified by a traffic officer for exceeding the speed limit on a public road. Who is responsible for that speeding offence?
answer_text_a: Your friend (the driver)
answer_text_b: You (the owner)
answer_text_c: You and your friend equally
correct_answer: A. Your friend (the driver)
answer_information_text: Your friend is responsible for the speeding offence because they were driving. The presumption that the owner was driving is rebutted by evidence identifying your friend as the driver.

question_text: How long are you allowed to drive your vehicle on a public road if your vehicle's licence disc has expired?
answer_text_a: 40 days
answer_text_b: 21 days
answer_text_c: 1 week
correct_answer: B. 21 days
answer_information_text: The regulations allow a vehicle to be driven on a public road for 21 days after its licence becomes due for renewal, provided the licence number and previous licence disc are displayed as prescribed. This is a limited period to renew the licence, not a permanent extension of the licence disc.

question_text: Are you allowed to drive your vehicle on a public road if its licence disc expired more than 21 days ago?
answer_text_a: Yes
answer_text_b: You are only allowed to drive on weekends
answer_text_c: No
correct_answer: C. No
answer_information_text: A vehicle may be driven for up to 21 days after its licence disc expires, with the old disc displayed as required. After that period, it may not be driven on a public road.

question_text: What colour warning lights does a traffic officer's vehicle have?
answer_text_a: Blue
answer_text_b: Red
answer_text_c: Green
correct_answer: A. Blue
answer_information_text: A traffic officer’s vehicle uses a blue warning light to identify it as an official traffic-control vehicle. Drivers must respond safely to the officer’s directions and give way when required.

question_text: What colour warning lights does an ambulance have?
answer_text_a: Green
answer_text_b: Red
answer_text_c: Blue
correct_answer: B. Red
answer_information_text: An ambulance uses a red warning light to identify it as an emergency vehicle. Give way safely when it approaches with its warning light or siren operating, without creating another danger.

question_text: What is the general rule about which side of the roadway to drive on in South Africa?
answer_text_a: Drive on the left side, except where legally permitted or directed otherwise
answer_text_b: Drive on the right side, except when overtaking
answer_text_c: Drive on either side whenever there is no oncoming traffic
correct_answer: A. Drive on the left side, except where legally permitted or directed otherwise
answer_information_text: On a two-way public road, drive on the left side of the roadway, subject to lawful exceptions and directions from traffic officers or road signs. This rule does not apply to one-way roads.

question_text: What are you not allowed to do on a public road?
answer_text_a: Cause a vehicle's wheels to drag or spin on the roadway, except in an emergency
answer_text_b: Overtake another vehicle where overtaking is permitted and safe
answer_text_c: Park in a marked parking bay where parking is permitted
correct_answer: A. Cause a vehicle's wheels to drag or spin on the roadway, except in an emergency
answer_information_text: On a public road, you may not cause any vehicle wheel to drag or spin on the roadway surface, except in an emergency.

question_text: Which statement correctly describes the rule for driving on a public road while under the influence of intoxicating liquor?
answer_text_a: Driving a vehicle is prohibited at any speed.
answer_text_b: Driving is prohibited only when making a U-turn.
answer_text_c: Driving is prohibited only when travelling over 90 km/h.
correct_answer: A. Driving a vehicle is prohibited at any speed.
answer_information_text: You may not drive a vehicle on a public road while under the influence of intoxicating liquor. This prohibition applies regardless of your speed or manoeuvre.

question_text: You should not drive...
answer_text_a: With both hands on the steering wheel
answer_text_b: With your headlights switched on during the day
answer_text_c: Recklessly or while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
correct_answer: C. Recklessly or while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
answer_information_text: Reckless driving and driving while intoxicated are both prohibited because each creates a serious danger to other road users. You must be fit to drive and operate the vehicle with proper care and control.

question_text: What should you always do when driving on a public road?
answer_text_a: Have consideration for other road users
answer_text_b: Drive beyond on the yellow line on freeways
answer_text_c: Have your radio off when driving
correct_answer: A. Have consideration for other road users
answer_information_text: Every driver must show consideration for other road users by driving courteously, safely and without unnecessarily obstructing or endangering them. The yellow line marks the shoulder, which has limited permitted uses, and switching off the radio is not a general legal requirement.

question_text: What should a load that projects more than 150mm to the side, or more than 300mm to the rear be marked by?
answer_text_a: A purple triangle
answer_text_b: A red flag during the day
answer_text_c: A yellow flag at night
correct_answer: B. A red flag during the day
answer_information_text: A projecting load must be clearly marked so that other road users can see its extra width or length. During the day, a load projecting more than 150 mm to the side or more than 300 mm to the rear must be marked with a red flag.

question_text: What must a light or heavy motor vehicle be fitted with at the rear?
answer_text_a: Carbon fiber car parts
answer_text_b: A sound system
answer_text_c: The rear of the vehicle must be fitted with two retro-reflectors
correct_answer: C. The rear of the vehicle must be fitted with two retro-reflectors
answer_information_text: Light and heavy motor vehicles must have two red retro-reflectors at the rear. Motorcycles have a separate requirement for one rear red retro-reflector.

question_text: Your vehicle will not be allowed on a public road if...
answer_text_a: It does not have an efficient exhaust silencer
answer_text_b: It does not have chrome mags
answer_text_c: If it does not have a panoramic sunroof
correct_answer: A. It does not have an efficient exhaust silencer
answer_information_text: An efficient exhaust silencer or muffling device is required to control exhaust noise and keep the vehicle safe and roadworthy. A vehicle without one may not be used on a public road.

question_text: Is it compulsory for a motor car to have a service brake and a parking brake?
answer_text_a: It is only compulsory on trucks
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: No
correct_answer: B. Yes
answer_information_text: A motor car must have two independent braking systems: a service brake to slow and stop it while driving, and a parking brake to hold it still once stopped. Both are a legal requirement, not an optional extra.

question_text: What can the maximum width of a bus be?
answer_text_a: 2 metres
answer_text_b: 1.75 metres
answer_text_c: 2.6 metres
correct_answer: C. 2.6 metres
answer_information_text: The maximum permitted overall width of a bus is 2.6 metres. Keeping within this limit helps buses pass safely and prevents them from taking up excessive road space.

question_text: What is the maximum permitted overall height, including any load, of a motor vehicle other than a double-deck bus on a public road?
answer_text_a: 4.65 metres
answer_text_b: 4.3 metres
answer_text_c: 3.4 metres
correct_answer: B. 4.3 metres
answer_information_text: The overall height of a motor vehicle other than a double-deck bus, including any load, may not exceed 4.3 metres on a public road.

question_text: What can the maximum height of a double-deck bus be?
answer_text_a: 3.5 metres
answer_text_b: 4.65 metres
answer_text_c: 2.5 metres
correct_answer: B. 4.65 metres
answer_information_text: A double-deck bus, including its load, may not be higher than 4.65 metres. The greater limit recognises the design of these buses while still protecting them from overhead obstructions.

question_text: For a trailer with a GVM exceeding 12 000 kg, which is neither a semi-trailer nor a trailer with only one axle or one axle unit, what is the maximum overall length, excluding any drawbar or coupling?
answer_text_a: 11.3 metres
answer_text_b: 8 metres
answer_text_c: 12.5 metres
correct_answer: C. 12.5 metres
answer_information_text: The maximum overall length for this category of trailer is 12.5 metres, excluding any drawbar or coupling. A trailer with only one axle or one axle unit and a GVM exceeding 12 000 kg has a limit of 11.3 metres.

question_text: If a trailer other than a semi-trailer has one axle and a GVM not exceeding 12 000 kg, its overall length, excluding any drawbar or coupling, must not exceed...
answer_text_a: 8 metres
answer_text_b: 3 metres
answer_text_c: 5 metres
correct_answer: A. 8 metres
answer_information_text: For a trailer other than a semi-trailer with one axle and a GVM of 12 000 kg or less, the maximum permitted length is 8 metres. Any drawbar or coupling is excluded from this measurement.

question_text: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum distance at which your motor vehicle’s hooter must be clearly audible to a person of normal hearing?
answer_text_a: 90 metres
answer_text_b: 100 metres
answer_text_c: 25 metres
correct_answer: A. 90 metres
answer_information_text: Under normal conditions, a motor vehicle’s hooter must be clearly audible to a person of normal hearing from at least 90 metres.

question_text: May you stop in a freeway traffic lane or on its shoulder solely to pick up an ordinary civilian hitchhiker, outside a signposted stopping or parking area?
answer_text_a: No.
answer_text_b: Yes, if you stop only briefly.
answer_text_c: Yes, if you switch on your hazard warning lights.
correct_answer: A. No.
answer_information_text: Stopping solely to pick up an ordinary civilian hitchhiker is not permitted on a freeway outside an area designated by a road traffic sign for stopping or parking. A brief stop or hazard warning lights do not make it lawful.

question_text: Are you allowed to stop on the freeway and reverse if you miss an exit?
answer_text_a: Yes
answer_text_b: No
answer_text_c: Only if you miss the exit by 10 metres
correct_answer: B. No
answer_information_text: You may not stop and reverse on a freeway after missing an exit. Continue to the next exit and return safely, because reversing creates a serious danger to fast-moving traffic.

question_text: Are elderly people exempt from using a seat belt?
answer_text_a: Only if they are over 65
answer_text_b: Yes
answer_text_c: No
correct_answer: C. No
answer_information_text: Old age does not exempt anyone from wearing a seat belt. Occupants must wear a seat belt while the vehicle is moving unless a specific legal exemption, such as a valid medical exemption, applies.

question_text: Are you allowed to tow a vehicle on a public road if the length of the tow rope is less than 1 metre?
answer_text_a: Yes
answer_text_b: No, the tow rope must be exactly 3.5 metres long
answer_text_c: No, a rope may never be used to tow a vehicle
correct_answer: A. Yes
answer_information_text: Regulation 330 of the National Road Traffic Regulations, 2000 sets a maximum of 3,5 metres between the two vehicles, not a required length, so a shorter rope is allowed. Remember that towing faster than 30 km/h needs a rigid tow-bar rather than a rope.

question_text: If a traffic officer instructs you to stop on a freeway. What should you do?
answer_text_a: Carry on driving
answer_text_b: Stop your vehicle
answer_text_c: You can only stop if a traffic sign instructs you to do so
correct_answer: B. Stop your vehicle
answer_information_text: You must stop when a traffic officer instructs you to stop, including on a freeway. A lawful instruction from a traffic officer must be obeyed even when no traffic sign requires you to stop.

question_text: What is the general speed limit on a freeway, unless a road sign or a vehicle-specific restriction sets a lower limit?
answer_text_a: 80 km/h
answer_text_b: 100 km/h
answer_text_c: 120 km/h
correct_answer: C. 120 km/h
answer_information_text: The general speed limit on a freeway is 120 km/h. You must obey any lower posted limit or lower limit applicable to your vehicle.

question_text: What is the minimum blood alcohol concentration at which a professional driver is prohibited from driving on a public road?
answer_text_a: 0.20 grams per 100 ml of blood
answer_text_b: 0.02 grams per 100 ml of blood
answer_text_c: 0.05 grams per 100 ml of blood
correct_answer: B. 0.02 grams per 100 ml of blood
answer_information_text: A professional driver is prohibited from driving on a public road with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 grams per 100 ml or more.

question_text: Are you allowed to drive in a manner that will disregard the safety of the other road users as well as your own safety?
answer_text_a: You can only do this on weekends
answer_text_b: Yes, you can drive your car however you want to
answer_text_c: No, as it will put you and other road users in danger
correct_answer: C. No, as it will put you and other road users in danger
answer_information_text: You may not drive in a way that disregards your own safety or the safety of other road users. Safe driving requires you to control the vehicle responsibly and avoid conduct that creates danger.

question_text: What should you do immediately if someone is killed in a road accident involving your vehicle?
answer_text_a: Stop and call the police and emergency services.
answer_text_b: Phone your insurance company before seeking emergency assistance.
answer_text_c: Drive away without reporting the accident.
correct_answer: A. Stop and call the police and emergency services.
answer_information_text: Stop immediately and summon the police and emergency services. Unless already reported to a police or traffic officer at the scene, the accident must be reported as soon as reasonably practicable and within 24 hours, unless your injuries prevent you from doing so.

question_text: What should you immediately do if you have an accident?
answer_text_a: Have an alcoholic drink to recover from the shock
answer_text_b: Stop your vehicle immediately
answer_text_c: Phone your boss and let him know immediately
correct_answer: B. Stop your vehicle immediately
answer_information_text: After an accident involving a vehicle, person, animal or property, the driver’s immediate duty is to stop the vehicle. Stopping allows the driver to assess the situation, assist injured people and comply with the further accident-reporting duties.

question_text: When overtaking, which of the following are you allowed to do?
answer_text_a: Exceed the speed limit.
answer_text_b: Pass a vehicle stopped at a stop sign and cross the stop line that applies to your lane without stopping yourself.
answer_text_c: Pass on the left on a one-way roadway in an urban area that is divided into traffic lanes, when it is safe to do so
correct_answer: C. Pass on the left on a one-way roadway in an urban area that is divided into traffic lanes, when it is safe to do so
answer_information_text: You may pass safely on the left on an urban one-way roadway wide enough for two or more lines of moving vehicles, without using the shoulder or verge. Overtaking does not allow you to exceed the speed limit or ignore a stop sign that applies to you.

question_text: When another vehicle is overtaking you, you must:
answer_text_a: Drive on the shoulder of the road
answer_text_b: Keep as far left as possible
answer_text_c: Slow down so the other vehicle may overtake you
correct_answer: B. Keep as far left as possible
answer_information_text: When being overtaken, keep as far left as possible to give the overtaking vehicle room. Do not accelerate.

question_text: You should never overtake when:
answer_text_a: You are travelling above 60 km/h.
answer_text_b: You are on a straight road with clear visibility.
answer_text_c: Overtaking could endanger other road users, including where restricted visibility at a curve or blind rise makes it unsafe.
correct_answer: C. Overtaking could endanger other road users, including where restricted visibility at a curve or blind rise makes it unsafe.
answer_information_text: Never overtake if doing so could endanger other road users. A curve or blind rise alone does not automatically prohibit overtaking.

question_text: You can overtake on the left of a vehicle if:
answer_text_a: The vehicle ahead is driving slowly, allowing you to use the shoulder to pass
answer_text_b: The vehicle ahead is turning right or has signalled its intention to turn right, and you can pass safely without driving on the shoulder or verge
answer_text_c: You need to pass quickly to avoid being late
correct_answer: B. The vehicle ahead is turning right or has signalled its intention to turn right, and you can pass safely without driving on the shoulder or verge
answer_information_text: You may pass on the left when the vehicle ahead is turning right or has signalled a right turn, provided you can do so safely. You must not use the shoulder or verge for this manoeuvre.

question_text: When driving on a road with traffic lanes, you should NOT:
answer_text_a: Keep in your designated lane
answer_text_b: Straddle from side to side between lanes
answer_text_c: Change lanes when safe to do so
correct_answer: B. Straddle from side to side between lanes
answer_information_text: You must stay in your designated lane and not weave from side to side. Lane changes must be done safely with indication.

question_text: At a pedestrian crossing without traffic signals, you must:
answer_text_a: Sound your horn to warn pedestrians
answer_text_b: Yield to pedestrians crossing on your half of the roadway, or approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger, slowing down or stopping as necessary
answer_text_c: Reduce speed and continue as you have right of way
correct_answer: B. Yield to pedestrians crossing on your half of the roadway, or approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger, slowing down or stopping as necessary
answer_information_text: At a pedestrian crossing without traffic signals, yield to pedestrians on your half of the roadway or approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger. Slow down or stop as necessary to let them cross safely.

question_text: You are turning at an intersection and see pedestrians crossing the road you are turning into. You must:
answer_text_a: Sound your horn to warn them
answer_text_b: Swerve around them
answer_text_c: Give way to the pedestrians
correct_answer: C. Give way to the pedestrians
answer_information_text: Pedestrians crossing at an intersection have right of way. You must give way to them.

question_text: You must obey signals given by a traffic officer:
answer_text_a: Always
answer_text_b: Only at an accident scene
answer_text_c: Only at a road block
correct_answer: A. Always
answer_information_text: You must always obey a traffic officer, even if their signal contradicts a road sign or traffic light.

question_text: Which of the following is a no-stopping area?
answer_text_a: In a marked parking bay in a parking lot
answer_text_b: In a designated parking area next to a shopping centre
answer_text_c: On the roadway of a public road within the railway reserve at a level crossing
correct_answer: C. On the roadway of a public road within the railway reserve at a level crossing
answer_information_text: You may not stop on the roadway of a public road within the railway reserve at a level crossing. Exceptions apply when stopping to avoid an accident, obey a road traffic sign or a traffic officer's direction, or for a cause beyond your control.

question_text: Except when stopping to avoid an accident, comply with a road traffic sign or a traffic officer's direction, or for a cause beyond your control, how close before a marked pedestrian crossing may you stop on the roadway of a public road?
answer_text_a: Not within 7 metres
answer_text_b: Not within 9 metres
answer_text_c: Not within 12 metres
correct_answer: B. Not within 9 metres
answer_information_text: Unless a stated exception applies, you may not stop within 9 metres on the approaching side of a pedestrian crossing demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs.

question_text: Which hand signals can you use on a freeway?
answer_text_a: Hand signals are prohibited, except for a cause beyond your control
answer_text_b: Turning signals only
answer_text_c: Stopping signal only
correct_answer: A. Hand signals are prohibited, except for a cause beyond your control
answer_information_text: When driving a motor vehicle on a freeway, you may give a hand signal only for a cause beyond your control.

question_text: Which vehicles are NOT allowed on the freeway?
answer_text_a: Heavy trucks
answer_text_b: Motorcycles under 50cc
answer_text_c: Buses
correct_answer: B. Motorcycles under 50cc
answer_information_text: Motorcycles under 50cc, bicycles, animal-drawn vehicles, and pedestrians are not allowed on freeways.

question_text: Headlights must be switched on:
answer_text_a: Only at night
answer_text_b: Only when it is raining
answer_text_c: Between sunset and sunrise or when visibility is not clear
correct_answer: C. Between sunset and sunrise or when visibility is not clear
answer_information_text: Headlights must be on between sunset and sunrise, and whenever visibility is reduced.

question_text: When towing a vehicle, the distance between the two vehicles must not be greater than:
answer_text_a: 3.5 metres
answer_text_b: 3 metres
answer_text_c: 4.5 metres
correct_answer: A. 3.5 metres
answer_information_text: The maximum distance between a towing and towed vehicle is 3.5 metres.

question_text: Assuming all other legal requirements are met, passengers may be carried in a vehicle being towed on a public road, other than a semi-trailer, only if:
answer_text_a: The driver gives permission, regardless of the towing speed
answer_text_b: The towing speed does not exceed 60 km/h when a solid tow bar is used
answer_text_c: The towing speed does not exceed 30 km/h
correct_answer: C. The towing speed does not exceed 30 km/h
answer_information_text: A towed vehicle carrying persons may not be towed faster than 30 km/h unless it is a semi-trailer. A solid tow bar does not remove this limit.

question_text: What is the first thing you must do as the driver if your vehicle is involved in or contributes to a collision causing injury or damage?
answer_text_a: Continue driving and report later
answer_text_b: Call the police first
answer_text_c: Stop your vehicle immediately
correct_answer: C. Stop your vehicle immediately
answer_information_text: You must immediately stop your vehicle if it is involved in or contributes to a collision in which someone is killed or injured, or property or an animal is damaged.

question_text: If someone is killed or injured in a collision involving your vehicle, you have not reported it to a police or traffic officer at the scene, and your injuries do not prevent reporting, how soon must you report it to the police?
answer_text_a: As soon as reasonably practicable, and within 24 hours after the collision.
answer_text_b: As soon as reasonably practicable, and within 72 hours after the collision.
answer_text_c: As soon as reasonably practicable, and within 12 hours after the collision.
correct_answer: A. As soon as reasonably practicable, and within 24 hours after the collision.
answer_information_text: In these circumstances, you must report the collision as soon as reasonably practicable and within 24 hours after it occurred.

question_text: If someone is fatally injured in a collision, when can you move the vehicles?
answer_text_a: When authorised by a traffic officer; otherwise, only if the collision completely obstructs the roadway, after clearly marking the vehicles’ positions on the road, and only far enough to allow traffic to pass.
answer_text_b: Once you have noted all details.
answer_text_c: Whenever they obstruct traffic, even if their positions have not been marked.
correct_answer: A. When authorised by a traffic officer; otherwise, only if the collision completely obstructs the roadway, after clearly marking the vehicles’ positions on the road, and only far enough to allow traffic to pass.
answer_information_text: Vehicles involved in a fatal collision may be moved when a traffic officer authorises it. Without that authorisation, the collision must completely obstruct the roadway, each vehicle’s position must first be clearly marked on the road by the person moving it, and movement must be limited to allowing traffic to pass.

question_text: Emergency vehicles always have right of way when:
answer_text_a: Only in hospital zones
answer_text_b: At all times regardless
answer_text_c: Their sirens or flashing lights are activated
correct_answer: C. Their sirens or flashing lights are activated
answer_information_text: Emergency vehicles have right of way only when their sirens or flashing lights are activated.

question_text: A vehicle is considered abandoned if it is left:
answer_text_a: For more than 24 hours in the same place on a public road outside an urban area, or for more than 7 days in the same place on a public road within an urban area
answer_text_b: Overnight in a parking lot
answer_text_c: For 24 hours on a highway
correct_answer: A. For more than 24 hours in the same place on a public road outside an urban area, or for more than 7 days in the same place on a public road within an urban area
answer_information_text: A vehicle may be deemed abandoned after more than 24 hours outside an urban area or more than 7 days within an urban area, subject to the road rules.

question_text: How close to a fire hydrant are you allowed to park?
answer_text_a: Not within 3 metres
answer_text_b: Not within 1.5 metres
answer_text_c: Not within 5 metres
correct_answer: B. Not within 1.5 metres
answer_information_text: You may not park within 1.5 metres of a fire hydrant.

question_text: Which of these is a permitted reason for a driver to extend an arm from a vehicle moving on a public road?
answer_text_a: When giving a hand signal required or authorised by the road traffic regulations.
answer_text_b: It is never permitted.
answer_text_c: When greeting someone.
correct_answer: A. When giving a hand signal required or authorised by the road traffic regulations.
answer_information_text: A driver may extend an arm to give a legally required or authorised hand signal while the vehicle is moving on a public road. There are also exceptions for examining, testing or parking the vehicle.

question_text: When turning right at an intersection from a two-way road, you must:
answer_text_a: Indicate only after you have turned
answer_text_b: Indicate before turning, approach immediately left of the centre of the road as circumstances permit, and yield to oncoming traffic that has right of way
answer_text_c: Turn as wide as possible
correct_answer: B. Indicate before turning, approach immediately left of the centre of the road as circumstances permit, and yield to oncoming traffic that has right of way
answer_information_text: Indicate before turning right and approach immediately left of the centre of a two-way road as circumstances permit. Yield to oncoming traffic that has right of way and turn only when you can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic.

question_text: When approaching an oncoming vehicle at night, when must you switch your headlights from high beam to low beam?
answer_text_a: Only when the oncoming vehicle is within 300 metres.
answer_text_b: Only when the oncoming vehicle is within 50 metres.
answer_text_c: Whenever high beam could cause dangerous glare to oncoming traffic.
correct_answer: C. Whenever high beam could cause dangerous glare to oncoming traffic.
answer_information_text: You must dip your headlights whenever high beam could cause dangerous glare to oncoming traffic. The rule specifies no fixed distance.

question_text: When driving a light motor vehicle in good road, weather and visibility conditions, which rule determines the minimum recommended following distance?
answer_text_a: A distance determined by means of the two-second rule
answer_text_b: A driver may drive as close as possible so that overtaking will be easier
answer_text_c: Five metres at 100 km/h
correct_answer: A. A distance determined by means of the two-second rule
answer_information_text: Maintain at least a two-second following gap when driving a light motor vehicle in good conditions. Increase the gap whenever conditions require it to remain reasonable and prudent.

question_text: The driver of a vehicle shall not cross a public road unless ...
answer_text_a: There is a traffic officer directing traffic
answer_text_b: The road is clear of moving traffic for a sufficient distance to allow him/her to cross the road without obstructing or endangering any traffic
answer_text_c: The road is a one-way road
correct_answer: B. The road is clear of moving traffic for a sufficient distance to allow him/her to cross the road without obstructing or endangering any traffic
answer_information_text: Before crossing a public road, you must make sure moving traffic is clear for a sufficient distance. This ensures that you can cross without obstructing or endangering other road users.

question_text: When a vehicle is left unattended on a public road, what must be done to prevent it from moving?
answer_text_a: Leave the vehicle in neutral only
answer_text_b: Switch off the engine only
answer_text_c: Set its brake or use another method that effectively prevents it from moving
correct_answer: C. Set its brake or use another method that effectively prevents it from moving
answer_information_text: An unattended vehicle on a public road must be secured against movement by setting its brake or using another effective method. Selecting neutral or switching off the engine alone does not ensure that it cannot roll.

question_text: On which side may a driver encroach on a two-way roadway of sufficient width, and under what conditions?
answer_text_a: A driver may never encroach onto the right-hand half of a two-way roadway.
answer_text_b: Onto the right-hand half for any distance, provided there is no oncoming traffic.
answer_text_c: Onto the right-hand half, if traffic or property there is not obstructed or endangered, for only as long and as far as necessary and prudent, and if no road traffic sign prohibits it; or as directed by a traffic officer or road traffic sign.
correct_answer: C. Onto the right-hand half, if traffic or property there is not obstructed or endangered, for only as long and as far as necessary and prudent, and if no road traffic sign prohibits it; or as directed by a traffic officer or road traffic sign.
answer_information_text: Drivers must keep left, but may encroach onto the right-hand half without obstructing or endangering traffic or property, only as long and as far as necessary and prudent, and if no sign prohibits it. Encroachment is also permitted when directed by a traffic officer or road traffic sign.

question_text: When moving off from a stationary position at the side of the road, what is the responsibility of the driver?
answer_text_a: The driver must switch on hazard lights before moving off
answer_text_b: The driver must ensure that it is safe and that he/she will not interfere with traffic approaching from any direction
answer_text_c: The driver must hoot to warn other road users
correct_answer: B. The driver must ensure that it is safe and that he/she will not interfere with traffic approaching from any direction
answer_information_text: Before moving off from the side of the road, you must check that it is safe and that you will not interfere with traffic approaching from any direction. Use the correct observation and signalling procedure; hooting or hazard lights do not replace this responsibility.

question_text: Which of the following statements regarding a silencer is correct?
answer_text_a: A silencer with a small hole is acceptable
answer_text_b: A silencer need not be fitted
answer_text_c: A silencer must be fitted to a vehicle to restrict engine noise to acceptable levels
correct_answer: C. A silencer must be fitted to a vehicle to restrict engine noise to acceptable levels
answer_information_text: A vehicle must have a properly fitted silencer to keep engine noise within acceptable limits. A missing or damaged silencer can make the vehicle excessively noisy and means it is not compliant for use on a public road.

question_text: Whilst the vehicle is in motion a driver may ...
answer_text_a: Hold a cell phone provided the driver keeps at least one hand on the steering wheel
answer_text_b: Not hold a cell phone with any part of the body
answer_text_c: Type an SMS
correct_answer: B. Not hold a cell phone with any part of the body
answer_information_text: While driving, a driver may not hold a cell phone with any part of the body. Keeping one hand on the steering wheel does not make holding the phone legal, and typing an SMS is also prohibited.

question_text: Which of the following vehicles is not allowed on a freeway?
answer_text_a: A minibus taxi
answer_text_b: A motorcycle with a sidecar
answer_text_c: A tractor, except when it is used in connection with construction or maintenance of the freeway
correct_answer: C. A tractor, except when it is used in connection with construction or maintenance of the freeway
answer_information_text: A tractor may not be used on a freeway unless it is being used for construction or maintenance of that freeway. A motorcycle with a sidecar and a minibus taxi are not prohibited by this freeway rule.

question_text: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding pedal cycles?
answer_text_a: Pedal cycles are not permitted on a freeway
answer_text_b: Racing cycles may be ridden on a freeway during the day only
answer_text_c: Pedal cycles may only be ridden on the shoulder of the freeway
correct_answer: A. Pedal cycles are not permitted on a freeway
answer_information_text: Pedal cycles are not allowed on a freeway because they are unsuitable for freeway traffic and create a safety risk. This applies during the day and at night, and riding on the shoulder does not create an exception.

question_text: What is the duty of a driver when re-filling the fuel tank with petrol or inflammable fuel?
answer_text_a: He/she may start the engine to check if the fuel tank is full
answer_text_b: The driver may not cause or allow the engine to run whilst petrol or other inflammable fuel is being transferred to the fuel tank
answer_text_c: He/she may only allow the engine to run if diesel is being transferred
correct_answer: B. The driver may not cause or allow the engine to run whilst petrol or other inflammable fuel is being transferred to the fuel tank
answer_information_text: The engine must not be running while petrol or another inflammable fuel is being transferred into the fuel tank. Keeping the engine off reduces the risk of igniting fuel vapour during refuelling.

question_text: What is the minimum distance along the roadway behind a stationary motor vehicle at which a warning triangle must be placed to warn traffic approaching from behind?
correct_answer: A. 45 m
answer_information_text: When a warning triangle is required, it must be placed at least 45 metres from the stationary motor vehicle along the roadway towards approaching traffic. Its reflective side must face approaching traffic.

question_text: On a public road, any person under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a drug having a narcotic effect ...
answer_text_a: May occupy the driver's seat of a motor vehicle whose engine is running, as long as the vehicle is stationary
answer_text_b: May not occupy the driver's seat of a motor vehicle whose engine is running
answer_text_c: May sleep in the driver's seat of a motor vehicle while the engine is running
correct_answer: B. May not occupy the driver's seat of a motor vehicle whose engine is running
answer_information_text: On a public road, a person under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a drug having a narcotic effect may not occupy the driver's seat of a motor vehicle while its engine is running. This applies even when the vehicle is stationary.

question_text: When is overtaking prohibited?
answer_text_a: When passing a school
answer_text_b: When driving at night
answer_text_c: When approaching any place where passing could cause a hazard to traffic approaching from the opposite direction
correct_answer: C. When approaching any place where passing could cause a hazard to traffic approaching from the opposite direction
answer_information_text: Overtaking is prohibited when the road or visibility is such that passing could create a hazard for traffic approaching from the opposite direction. This includes places such as a rise, curve or any restricted-view section where the driver cannot pass safely.

question_text: Which parking rule applies on a public road outside an urban area?
answer_text_a: You may park on the roadway provided your vehicle is no more than 1 m from its left edge.
answer_text_b: You may park on the roadway provided your left-hand wheels are no more than 450 mm from its left edge.
answer_text_c: Parking is prohibited on the roadway (excluding shoulders) or where any part of the vehicle is within 1 m of its edge, unless an appropriate road traffic sign demarcates a parking place.
correct_answer: C. Parking is prohibited on the roadway (excluding shoulders) or where any part of the vehicle is within 1 m of its edge, unless an appropriate road traffic sign demarcates a parking place.
answer_information_text: Outside an urban area, parking is prohibited on the roadway, excluding shoulders, and any part of a parked vehicle must stay at least 1 m clear of the roadway edge. A parking place demarcated by an appropriate road traffic sign is the exception.

question_text: When flags have to be used to indicate projections ...
answer_text_a: They must be any size red flag
answer_text_b: They must be red, and at least 300 mm × 300 mm
answer_text_c: They may be any colour as long as they are visible
correct_answer: B. They must be red, and at least 300 mm × 300 mm
answer_information_text: A red flag or red cloth is required to make a projecting load visible to other road users. It must be at least 300 mm by 300 mm and must be attached in the prescribed position on the projection.

question_text: Is it permissible to drive a motor vehicle, other than a motorcycle or other cycle, on a public road with its engine uncovered?
answer_text_a: The engine must be so covered as not to be a source of danger
answer_text_b: The engine may be uncovered provided it is not noisy
answer_text_c: The engine may be uncovered during daylight only
correct_answer: A. The engine must be so covered as not to be a source of danger
answer_information_text: When a motor vehicle is operated on a public road, its engine must be covered so that it poses no danger. This requirement excludes motorcycles and other cycles.

question_text: You are caught in slow-moving heavy traffic in the right lane of a busy urban road. The car in front of you would like to turn right into a driveway and has stopped, waiting as oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?
answer_text_a: Wait behind the car until you get an opportunity to pass on the left or to proceed
answer_text_b: Switch on your left indicator and move into the left lane
answer_text_c: Hoot and pass to the left
correct_answer: A. Wait behind the car until you get an opportunity to pass on the left or to proceed
answer_information_text: The vehicle turning right must be given time and space to complete the turn safely. Wait behind it, then pass on the left only when the road is clear and the manoeuvre can be completed without obstructing or endangering traffic.

question_text: Which statement is true regarding vehicle noise?
answer_text_a: A person may only drive a motor vehicle in such a way that it causes excessive noise outside a built-up area.
answer_text_b: A person may only drive a motor vehicle in such a way that it causes excessive noise in an urban area.
answer_text_c: No person may operate or permit the operation of a vehicle on a public road in a way that causes excessive noise they could avoid by taking reasonable care.
correct_answer: C. No person may operate or permit the operation of a vehicle on a public road in a way that causes excessive noise they could avoid by taking reasonable care.
answer_information_text: A person must not operate a vehicle, or allow it to be operated, on a public road so that it causes excessive noise they could avoid with reasonable care. This rule applies both inside and outside built-up areas.

question_text: When may a driver allow part of their body to protrude beyond a moving vehicle on a public road?
answer_text_a: It is never permissible
answer_text_b: When giving a hand signal required or authorised by the regulations, or when examining, testing or parking the vehicle
answer_text_c: Whenever the vehicle is travelling at less than 60 km/h
correct_answer: B. When giving a hand signal required or authorised by the regulations, or when examining, testing or parking the vehicle
answer_information_text: A driver may protrude part of their body while giving a required or authorised hand signal, or while examining, testing or parking the vehicle. Travelling below 60 km/h does not create an exception.

question_text: What colour must the indicator lamps fitted to the front emit?
answer_text_a: When in use, indicator lamps to the front must emit a white, yellow or amber light
answer_text_b: When in use, indicator lamps to the front must emit a green light
answer_text_c: When in use, indicator lamps to the front must emit a red light
correct_answer: A. When in use, indicator lamps to the front must emit a white, yellow or amber light
answer_information_text: Regulation 194 of the National Road Traffic Regulations, 2000 allows a direction indicator to show white, yellow or amber to the front. Red is kept for lamps facing to the rear, so a red lamp at the front would tell other drivers the wrong thing about which way your vehicle is facing.

question_text: You may...
answer_text_a: Leave the engine of your vehicle idling when you put petrol in it.
answer_text_b: Reverse your vehicle only if it is safe to do so.
answer_text_c: Drive your vehicle on the sidewalk at night.
correct_answer: B. Reverse your vehicle only if it is safe to do so.
answer_information_text: Reversing is allowed only when it can be done safely and without creating a danger or obstruction. Driving on a sidewalk is not permitted as an ordinary driving action, and the engine must be switched off while petrol is being put into the vehicle.

question_text: When you want to change lanes and drive from one lane to the other you must... (i) Only do it when it is safe to do so (ii) Switch on your flickers in time to show what you are going to do (iii) Use the mirrors of your vehicle to ensure that you know of other traffic around you
answer_text_a: Only (i) and (ii) are correct
answer_text_b: All of the above are correct
answer_text_c: Only (ii) and (iii) are correct
correct_answer: B. All of the above are correct
answer_information_text: Changing lanes is allowed only when it can be done safely, so check the mirrors and the blind spot for traffic that may not be visible in a mirror. Signal with the flicker early enough to warn other road users, then move across only when the lane is clear.

question_text: When may you drive on the shoulder of a road to let another vehicle overtake you?
answer_text_a: Between sunrise and sunset, while being overtaken on a road with one traffic lane in each direction, provided you endanger neither yourself nor other traffic, pedestrians or property, and people and vehicles on the road are clearly visible at least 150 metres away.
answer_text_b: At any time, including at night, provided the shoulder is clear and you want to let another vehicle pass.
answer_text_c: On a freeway with four lanes in each direction whenever you want to travel slower than 120 km/h.
correct_answer: A. Between sunrise and sunset, while being overtaken on a road with one traffic lane in each direction, provided you endanger neither yourself nor other traffic, pedestrians or property, and people and vehicles on the road are clearly visible at least 150 metres away.
answer_information_text: You may drive on the shoulder while being overtaken only between sunrise and sunset on a road with one traffic lane in each direction. You must not endanger yourself, other traffic, pedestrians or property, and people and vehicles on the road must be clearly visible at least 150 metres away.

question_text: You may not obtain a learner's licence if... (i) You already have a licence that authorises the driving of the same vehicle class. (ii) You are declared unfit to obtain a driving licence for a certain period and that period still prevails. (iii) Your licence was suspended temporarily and the suspension has not yet expired.
answer_text_a: (i) only is correct
answer_text_b: (i) and (iii)
answer_text_c: (i),(ii) and (iii) are correct.
correct_answer: C. (i),(ii) and (iii) are correct.
answer_information_text: A learner's licence cannot be obtained while you already hold a licence for the same vehicle class, while a declaration of unfitness is still in force, or while a licence suspension has not expired. Each condition prevents the issue of a learner's licence during the restricted period.

question_text: A motor vehicle licence and licence disc are normally valid for...
answer_text_a: 21 days
answer_text_b: 90 days
answer_text_c: 12 months
correct_answer: C. 12 months
answer_information_text: Under regulation 26, a motor vehicle licence and licence disc are normally valid for 12 months. A vehicle clearance certificate is a separate document.

question_text: The legal speed limit applicable to your vehicle...
answer_text_a: Is determined by the applicable posted or general speed limit, subject to any lower limit applicable to your vehicle
answer_text_b: Can be determined by yourself from the number of lanes the road has
answer_text_c: Is always 120 km/h outside an urban area
correct_answer: A. Is determined by the applicable posted or general speed limit, subject to any lower limit applicable to your vehicle
answer_information_text: General speed limits apply even where no speed-limit sign is displayed. A posted limit may change the general limit, but any lower limit applicable to your vehicle must still be obeyed.

question_text: What is the longest period that a vehicle may be parked on one place on a road outside urban areas?
answer_text_a: 7 days
answer_text_b: 48 hours
answer_text_c: 24 hours
correct_answer: C. 24 hours
answer_information_text: A vehicle may not be left in the same place on a public road outside an urban area for more than 24 hours. After that period it may be treated as abandoned and removed in accordance with the law.

question_text: At an intersection...
answer_text_a: Pedestrians who are already crossing the road when the red man signal starts showing, have right of way
answer_text_b: You can pass another vehicle waiting to turn right on his left side by going off the road
answer_text_c: You can stop in it to off load passengers
correct_answer: A. Pedestrians who are already crossing the road when the red man signal starts showing, have right of way
answer_information_text: A pedestrian who has already started crossing may finish crossing safely even when the red man signal appears. Drivers must give way to such pedestrians and must not stop in an intersection merely to offload passengers.

question_text: Unless a legal exception applies, you are not allowed to stop...
answer_text_a: Next to an obstruction where stopping is otherwise permitted and does not obstruct or endanger traffic
answer_text_b: On the right-hand side of the roadway facing oncoming traffic
answer_text_c: In a designated stopping bay where stopping is permitted
correct_answer: B. On the right-hand side of the roadway facing oncoming traffic
answer_information_text: Stopping on a public road’s right-hand side with your vehicle pointing towards approaching traffic is prohibited unless a legal exception applies.

question_text: You are not allowed to stop...
answer_text_a: Where you are also prohibited to park
answer_text_b: Opposite a vehicle, where the roadway is 10m wide
answer_text_c: 5m from a bridge
correct_answer: C. 5m from a bridge
answer_information_text: Stopping is prohibited on a bridge and within six metres of a bridge, so stopping five metres from one is not allowed. The restriction protects visibility and prevents a stopped vehicle from obstructing traffic near the bridge.

question_text: You may pass another vehicle travelling in the same direction on the left-hand side, provided it is safe, in which of these situations? (i) It signals that it is going to turn right, and you can pass without driving on the shoulder or verge. (ii) It keeps to the right, and you must drive on the shoulder to pass it. (iii) It travels in the right-hand lane of a two-way urban road with at least two traffic lanes in each direction, and you can pass without driving on the shoulder or verge.
answer_text_a: (i) and (iii) only are correct
answer_text_b: (i) only is correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: A. (i) and (iii) only are correct
answer_information_text: Safe passing on the left is permitted when the vehicle ahead signals a right turn or on a two-way urban road wide enough for at least two lines of moving vehicles in each direction. In these circumstances, you must not use the shoulder or verge to pass.

question_text: Provided it is safe, you may overtake another vehicle on the left-hand side... (i) When that vehicle is turning right or its driver has signalled an intention to turn right, with enough room to pass without using the shoulder or verge (ii) On a one-way roadway divided into marked traffic lanes, without using the shoulder or verge (iii) When a traffic officer directs you to do so
answer_text_a: Statement (iii) only is correct
answer_text_b: Statements (ii) and (iii) only are correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: C. All of the above are correct
answer_information_text: Safe passing on the left is permitted when the vehicle ahead is turning or signalling right, on a one-way roadway with marked traffic lanes, or as directed by a traffic officer. In the first two cases, you must not use the shoulder or verge.

question_text: You may on a public road...
answer_text_a: Pass another vehicle turning right, on it's left -hand side without driving on the shoulder of the road
answer_text_b: Not pass any vehicle on the left-hand side.
answer_text_c: Pass another vehicle at any place on the left-hand side if it is turning right
correct_answer: A. Pass another vehicle turning right, on it's left -hand side without driving on the shoulder of the road
answer_information_text: A vehicle turning right may be passed on its left if there is enough room to do so without driving on the shoulder and it is safe. Passing on the left is not automatically allowed every time a vehicle turns right; the safety and shoulder conditions still apply.

question_text: The last action that you must take before moving to another lane is to...
answer_text_a: Switch on your flicker
answer_text_b: Check the blind spot
answer_text_c: Look in rear view mirror
correct_answer: B. Check the blind spot
answer_information_text: Checking the blind spot is the final observation before moving across. Mirrors do not show every area beside and slightly behind your vehicle, so a quick blind-spot check confirms that another vehicle or motorcycle is not hidden there.

question_text: When are you allowed to drive your vehicle on the right -hand side of a road with traffic in both directions?
answer_text_a: Under no circumstances
answer_text_b: When you switch the emergency lights of your vehicle on
answer_text_c: When a traffic officer shows you to do so
correct_answer: C. When a traffic officer shows you to do so
answer_information_text: A traffic officer may direct traffic to use the right-hand side, and you must obey that instruction. Normally you keep left on a two-way road, but a traffic officer’s direction temporarily controls how you must proceed.

question_text: If you come to a robot and the red light flashes, you must...
answer_text_a: Stop and go only if it safe to do so
answer_text_b: Stop and wait for the light to change to green before you go
answer_text_c: Look out for a road block as the light shows you a police stop
correct_answer: A. Stop and go only if it safe to do so
answer_information_text: A flashing red robot must be treated like a stop sign. Stop first, then proceed only when it is safe and give way to pedestrians and traffic that has right of way; you do not wait for a green light.

question_text: A vehicle of which the brakes are not good, must be towed
answer_text_a: On a trailer
answer_text_b: With a tow-bar
answer_text_c: With a rope
correct_answer: B. With a tow-bar
answer_information_text: A vehicle with defective brakes cannot be safely controlled by a rope alone. It must be connected to the towing vehicle with a tow-bar or draw-bar so that the combination can be controlled safely.

question_text: A safe following distance is, when the vehicle in front of you suddenly stops, you could....
answer_text_a: Swerve and stop next to it
answer_text_b: Swerve and pass
answer_text_c: Stop without swerving
correct_answer: C. Stop without swerving
answer_information_text: A safe following distance gives you enough space to stop behind a vehicle that stops suddenly. You should be able to brake and stop in your lane without swerving, because swerving can cause a collision with other traffic.

question_text: You may not
answer_text_a: Leave your vehicle unattended while the engine is running
answer_text_b: Have passengers in the vehicle if you only have a learner's licence
answer_text_c: Drive in reverse for more than a 100m
correct_answer: A. Leave your vehicle unattended while the engine is running
answer_information_text: You may not leave a vehicle unattended while its engine is running. Switch off the engine and secure the vehicle before leaving it, even if you intend to be away for only a short time.

question_text: If you want to change lanes you must
answer_text_a: Apply the brakes lightly and then change lanes
answer_text_b: Give the necessary signal and after looking for other traffic, change lanes
answer_text_c: Switch on your indicator and change lanes
correct_answer: B. Give the necessary signal and after looking for other traffic, change lanes
answer_information_text: Changing lanes requires both a signal and proper observation. Give the necessary signal, check your mirrors and blind spot for traffic, and move only when the lane is clear and it is safe to do so.

question_text: The fastest speed at which you may tow a vehicle with a rope is.. km/h
answer_information_text: When a vehicle is towed with a rope, the maximum speed is 30 km/h. A tow-bar or draw-bar is required before towing at a higher speed, subject to the other towing rules.

question_text: You may not drive into an intersection when...
answer_text_a: There is not enough space in the intersection to turn right without blocking other traffic
answer_text_b: The robot (traffic signal) is yellow and you are already in the intersection.
answer_text_c: The vehicle in front of you wants to turn right and the road is wide enough to pass on the left side
correct_answer: A. There is not enough space in the intersection to turn right without blocking other traffic
answer_information_text: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space for your vehicle to clear it without obstructing other traffic. This applies even when you have permission to proceed, because blocking the intersection can prevent vehicles from moving safely in other directions.
