question_text: When you were involved in an accident you... (i) Must immediately stop your vehicle (ii) Must determine the damage to the vehicles (iii) May refuse to give your name and address to anyone except the police
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_text_b: (ii) only is correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_information_text: After an accident, you must stop immediately and determine the nature and extent of the damage. You must also provide your name and address when a person with reasonable grounds asks for them, not only when the police ask.

question_text: When you were involved in an accident you... (i) Must immediately stop your vehicle (ii) Must see if someone is injured (iii) May use a bit of alcohol for the shock
answer_text_a: (ii) only is correct
answer_text_b: (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: B. (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_information_text: After an accident, you must stop immediately and check whether anyone has been injured. You may not drink alcohol for shock or any other reason before complying with the required accident-reporting and medical examination rules.

question_text: When do you have the right of way? (i) When you are within a traffic circle (ii) When you have stopped first at a four – way stop (iii) When you want to turn right at an intersection in a two-way road
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_text_b: (i) only is correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_information_text: Traffic already within a traffic circle has priority over vehicles entering it. At a four-way stop, the vehicle that stopped first has the right to proceed first, but a driver turning right at a normal two-way intersection must give way to oncoming traffic.

question_text: If you want to turn left with your vehicle, you must...
answer_text_a: First move to the right to enable you to turn left easily
answer_text_b: Give the necessary signal in good time
answer_text_c: Slow down completely, stop and then turn
correct_answer: B. Give the necessary signal in good time
answer_information_text: A left turn must be communicated clearly to other road users by giving the required signal in good time. Signalling early gives following and approaching traffic enough time to react safely; stopping or moving right is not normally required for a left turn.

question_text: When you drive...
answer_text_a: You must have both hands on the steering wheel
answer_text_b: You must wear shoes with rubber soles
answer_text_c: Your vision of the road and the traffic must be unobstructed
correct_answer: C. Your vision of the road and the traffic must be unobstructed
answer_information_text: When driving, you must have an unobstructed view of the road and traffic around you. Objects, passengers or other obstructions must not prevent you from seeing hazards and controlling the vehicle safely.

question_text: On a public road, you may not... (i) Leave a stationary motor vehicle unattended with its engine running (ii) Operate a motor vehicle without an effective cap fitted to the fuel-tank filling opening (iii) Cause its wheels to spin on the roadway when pulling off, except in an emergency
answer_text_a: (i), (ii) and (iii)
answer_text_b: (i) only
answer_text_c: (ii) only
correct_answer: A. (i), (ii) and (iii)
answer_information_text: On a public road, a stationary motor vehicle may not be left unattended with its engine running, and a motor vehicle must have an effective fuel-tank cap. Causing wheels to spin on the roadway is prohibited except in an emergency.

question_text: What is important with regard to the hooter of your vehicle on a public road, assuming no statutory warning-device exemption applies?
answer_text_a: The prescribed minimum distance at which a person of normal hearing must clearly hear it under normal conditions is 50 m.
answer_text_b: You may use it merely to attract the attention of someone you would like to offer a lift.
answer_text_c: The tone and pitch of its sound may not vary.
correct_answer: C. The tone and pitch of its sound may not vary.
answer_information_text: Where no statutory exemption applies, the hooter's sound must not vary in tone or pitch. It must be clearly audible under normal conditions to a person of normal hearing from at least 90 m away.

question_text: You must stop your vehicle... (i) On a public road at the signal of a person driving sheep (ii) On a freeway when directed to do so by a traffic officer (iii) On any road to avoid an accident
answer_text_a: Only (iii) is correct
answer_text_b: Only (ii) and (iii) are correct
answer_text_c: (i), (ii) and (iii) are all correct
correct_answer: C. (i), (ii) and (iii) are all correct
answer_information_text: You must stop when a person driving sheep gives a stop signal on a public road. You must also stop when a traffic officer directs you to stop on a freeway, or when stopping is necessary to avoid an accident, so all three statements are correct.

question_text: Which of the following permits you to stop on a freeway outside a designated stopping or parking area?
answer_text_a: To pick up hitchhikers.
answer_text_b: To comply with a road traffic sign requiring you to stop.
answer_text_c: For a rest during a tiring journey.
correct_answer: B. To comply with a road traffic sign requiring you to stop.
answer_information_text: You may stop on a freeway to comply with a road traffic sign requiring you to stop. Stopping outside a designated stopping or parking area simply to rest or pick up hitchhikers is not permitted.

question_text: When may a driver who has no applicable statutory exemption disregard a direction conveyed by a lawfully displayed road traffic sign?
answer_text_a: Whenever the driver faces a personal emergency.
answer_text_b: Only when directed to do so by a traffic officer.
answer_text_c: Under no circumstances.
correct_answer: B. Only when directed to do so by a traffic officer.
answer_information_text: A driver without an applicable statutory exemption must obey a lawfully displayed road traffic sign unless a traffic officer directs otherwise. A personal emergency alone does not give permission to disregard the sign.

question_text: What is the duty of a driver when driving on a public road divided into two or more roadways by an intervening space, physical barrier or dividing section constructed to impede vehicular traffic?
answer_text_a: Drive on the left-hand roadway unless directed or permitted by an appropriate road traffic sign or a traffic officer to use another roadway.
answer_text_b: You may drive on any roadway after sunset or when there is no other traffic on the road.
answer_text_c: You may drive on any roadway at any time.
correct_answer: A. Drive on the left-hand roadway unless directed or permitted by an appropriate road traffic sign or a traffic officer to use another roadway.
answer_information_text: On a public road divided in this way, you must use the left-hand roadway. You may use another roadway only when an appropriate road traffic sign or a traffic officer directs or permits you to do so.

question_text: Show the correct statement......A driver may stop their vehicle on the road way of a public road...?
answer_text_a: When indicated by a traffic officer
answer_text_b: In contravention with any road traffic sign.
answer_text_c: In an intersection
correct_answer: A. When indicated by a traffic officer
answer_information_text: A driver may stop on the roadway when a traffic officer indicates that the vehicle must stop. Stopping in an intersection or in defiance of a road traffic sign can obstruct or endanger traffic and is not permitted.

question_text: Which one of the following statements are wrong...?
answer_text_a: If no seat equipped with a seatbelt is available, the driver must ensure that a child is seated on the rear seat if the vehicle has one.
answer_text_b: It is not the driver's responsibility to ensure that a child is in a child restraint.
answer_text_c: The driver must ensure that a child uses an appropriate child restraint where one is available; if none is available, the child must wear a seatbelt if an equipped seat is available.
correct_answer: B. It is not the driver's responsibility to ensure that a child is in a child restraint.
answer_information_text: The driver is responsible for ensuring that a child uses a suitable restraint where available. If there is no restraint or belted seat, the child must be placed on the rear seat when the vehicle has one.

question_text: The following vehicle may not be used on a freeway...?
answer_text_a: An abnormal loaded motor vehicle.
answer_text_b: An articulated motor vehicle
answer_text_c: An animal drawn vehicle
correct_answer: C. An animal drawn vehicle
answer_information_text: An animal-drawn vehicle may not be used on a freeway. Articulated and abnormal-load motor vehicles may use a freeway when they meet the applicable legal and safety requirements.

question_text: What is the minimum distance stop lamps must be visible to a person with normal eyesight in sunlight..?
correct_answer: A. 30m
answer_information_text: Stop lamps must be visible from at least 30 metres in sunlight to a person with normal eyesight. This gives following road users enough time to see that the vehicle is braking and react safely.

question_text: When driving a vehicle alone, what documents must you carry with you...?
answer_text_a: Any persons valid drivers licence if you only have a learners licence.
answer_text_b: Your original valid drivers licence.
answer_text_c: A certified copy of your drivers licence and id document.
correct_answer: B. Your original valid drivers licence.
answer_information_text: When driving alone, you must carry your original valid driver’s licence with you. A learner’s licence does not authorise unsupervised driving in place of the required driver’s licence.

question_text: When should you normally use the right-hand lane of a freeway if the left-hand lane is clear and no signs or traffic officers direct otherwise?
answer_text_a: Whenever you prefer, provided you do not stop in the lane.
answer_text_b: Whenever you are travelling at 120 km/h.
answer_text_c: When safely overtaking another vehicle; return to the left when safely clear.
correct_answer: C. When safely overtaking another vehicle; return to the left when safely clear.
answer_information_text: Normally, keep left and use the right-hand lane to overtake, returning left when safe. Overtaking is not the only lawful reason to use the right-hand lane.

question_text: How long must a flicker be displayed?
answer_text_a: for long enough to show vehicles or persons approaching you of your intentions
answer_text_b: For about 3 mins
answer_text_c: For about 2 mins
correct_answer: A. for long enough to show vehicles or persons approaching you of your intentions
answer_information_text: A flicker must be displayed for long enough to warn approaching vehicles and pedestrians of your intention. It is not displayed for a fixed number of minutes and should be cancelled after the manoeuvre.

question_text: When approaching from behind, may you pass a vehicle stopped at a pedestrian crossing to let pedestrians cross?
answer_text_a: Yes, if you think it is safe to do so.
answer_text_b: No, you must not pass that stopped vehicle.
answer_text_c: Yes, if the stopped vehicle's driver waves you past.
correct_answer: B. No, you must not pass that stopped vehicle.
answer_information_text: If a vehicle stops at a pedestrian crossing to let pedestrians cross the road, drivers approaching it from behind must not pass it.

question_text: A light motor vehicle fitted with a spot lamp may be used on a public road...
answer_text_a: With a light that's beam can shine in any direction
answer_text_b: If the lights are not connected
answer_text_c: If it's a breakdown vehicle at a collision scene
correct_answer: C. If it's a breakdown vehicle at a collision scene
answer_information_text: A spot lamp may be used on a light motor vehicle when it is a breakdown vehicle at a collision scene. It may not be fitted or used so that its beam can shine in any direction and dazzle other road users.

question_text: Which statement is False? A vehicle may be used on a public road if.......
answer_text_a: The fuel tank is defective
answer_text_b: The fuel cap is effective and closed
answer_text_c: The battery and electrical wiring are properly installed
correct_answer: A. The fuel tank is defective
answer_information_text: A vehicle may be used on a public road only when its fuel tank is safe and serviceable. A defective fuel tank can leak fuel and create a serious fire risk, so this is the false statement.

question_text: If you are driving towards a mini - circle and there are also vehicles from the other three sides you..
answer_text_a: May drive on if you were the first vehicle over the line
answer_text_b: Must always wait for the vehicle from your right before you drive on
answer_text_c: Must stop with all the vehicles and only drive on when it is safe
correct_answer: A. May drive on if you were the first vehicle over the line
answer_information_text: At a mini-circle, priority is based on which vehicle reaches and crosses its yield line first, rather than automatically giving priority to traffic from the right. If you were first over the line, you may proceed when it is safe and the intersection is clear.

question_text: Vehicle B...
answer_text_a: Can drive past vehicle A if there are no other vehicles
answer_text_b: Must stop behind vehicle A, drive closer if that vehicle has driven off, stop immediately behind the stop line and drive off when it is safe to do so
answer_text_c: Can drive over the stop line following vehicle A if there are no oncoming vehicles
correct_answer: B. Must stop behind vehicle A, drive closer if that vehicle has driven off, stop immediately behind the stop line and drive off when it is safe to do so
answer_information_text: Vehicle B must wait behind Vehicle A and must not pass it or cross the stop line while Vehicle A is still stopped. After Vehicle A moves, B moves forward, stops immediately behind the stop line, and proceeds only when it is safe and lawful.

question_text: Which is ALLOWED when towing another vehicle? (i) a motor car tows another motor car with a rope and drives 40 km/h (ii) you tow another vehicle with a tow-bar (iii) a tractor tows a trailer with 10 passengers on it at a speed of 30 km/h
answer_text_a: (i) only is correct
answer_text_b: (ii) and (iii) are only correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: B. (ii) and (iii) are only correct
answer_information_text: A tow-bar is an approved method of connecting the towing and towed vehicles. A vehicle carrying passengers may be towed at 30 km/h, but towing with a rope at 40 km/h is not allowed because rope towing is limited to 30 km/h.

question_text: It is illegal when you drive and a passenger...
answer_text_a: fiddles with the motor radios volume knob
answer_text_b: rides on the bumper of your vehicle
answer_text_c: sits directly behind you when you only have a learners licence
correct_answer: B. rides on the bumper of your vehicle
answer_information_text: A passenger may not ride on the bumper because it is not a proper seating position and the person can easily fall off or be injured. Passengers must sit inside the vehicle in seats intended for passengers.

question_text: What is true with regard to seatbelts? (i) An adult occupying a rear seat fitted with a seatbelt on a public road must wear it, unless legally exempt or while reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay or area. (ii) An adult driver need not wear a seatbelt while reversing. (iii) All children younger than 14 years are exempt from seatbelt and child-restraint requirements. (iv) If the front passenger seat has a seatbelt, your only adult passenger may not sit in a rear row where no seats have seatbelts.
answer_text_a: Only (i) is correct
answer_text_b: Only (i) and (ii) are correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: B. Only (i) and (ii) are correct
answer_information_text: Adults must wear fitted seatbelts unless legally exempt or while reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay or area. Children have restraint requirements, and the rule requiring adults to occupy available belted seats applies within the same row.

question_text: If you only have a learner's licence for a light motor vehicle with passenger seating, which statements are correct? (i) You must be directly supervised by someone holding a valid driving licence authorising that vehicle class, seated beside you or immediately behind you if they cannot sit beside you. (ii) You are not allowed to drive on a freeway. (iii) No passengers are allowed with you in the vehicle.
answer_text_a: Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
answer_text_b: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
answer_text_c: Only (i) is correct.
correct_answer: C. Only (i) is correct.
answer_information_text: The supervisor must hold a valid driving licence for that vehicle class and sit beside you, or immediately behind you if sitting beside you is impossible. A supervised learner may use freeways and carry passengers, subject to the applicable rules, but generally may not carry passengers for reward.

question_text: The load carried by a light/heavy vehicle should not project more than .... to the front of the vehicle
answer_text_a: 300 millimetres.
answer_text_b: 500 millimetres
answer_text_c: 100 millimetres
correct_answer: A. 300 millimetres.
answer_information_text: A load on a light or heavy vehicle may not project more than 300 millimetres beyond the front end. This is stated in Regulation 227.

question_text: What is the maximum distance a load may project beyond the rear end of a light or heavy vehicle on a public road?
answer_text_a: 300 millimetres.
answer_text_b: 1.8 metres.
answer_text_c: 3 metres.
correct_answer: B. 1.8 metres.
answer_information_text: A load may not project more than 1.8 metres beyond the rear end of the vehicle. The vehicle and its load must also remain within the applicable overall length limit.

question_text: How many windscreen wipers must light and heavy motor vehicles have? When in operation it must wipe the outside of the windscreen continuously, evenly and adequately.
answer_text_a: Two windscreen wipers, to clean the entire windscreen.
answer_text_b: Three windscreen wipers. Two fitted to the front windscreen and one fitted to the back window of the vehicle
answer_text_c: At least one windscreen wiper, to wipe the windscreen directly in front of the driver.
correct_answer: C. At least one windscreen wiper, to wipe the windscreen directly in front of the driver.
answer_information_text: At least one motorised windscreen wiper is required, and it must clear the windscreen directly in front of the driver continuously, evenly, and adequately. This is Regulation 203.

question_text: Displaying an emergency warning triangle shall not apply to a vehicle being stationary on the roadway of a public road... (i) Ina place where a road traffic sign authorises the loading or unloading of goods. (ii) In compliance with a road traffic sign or direction given by a traffic officer. (iii) On account of other traffic and the driver occupies the driving seat of such vehicle. (iv) In the course of events accompanying the carrying out of a state or municipal function.
answer_text_a: None of the above are correct.
answer_text_b: All of the above are correct.
answer_text_c: (i) and (ii) Only are correct.
correct_answer: B. All of the above are correct.
answer_information_text: All four listed situations are exceptions to the emergency-warning-triangle requirement when a vehicle is stationary. This is provided by Regulation 214.

question_text: When driving/riding you must always...
answer_text_a: Obey the traffic signs and rules of the road, unless directed otherwise by a traffic officer
answer_text_b: Do so at a speed of 60 km/h.
answer_text_c: Have a passenger in your vehicle/motorcycle
correct_answer: A. Obey the traffic signs and rules of the road, unless directed otherwise by a traffic officer
answer_information_text: Drivers and riders must obey traffic signs and road rules unless a traffic officer directs otherwise.

question_text: When intending to stop or turn left or right, when must you signal your intention?
answer_text_a: Only as you begin stopping or turning.
answer_text_b: Only after you have stopped or completed the turn.
answer_text_c: In good time, for long enough to warn other road users.
correct_answer: C. In good time, for long enough to warn other road users.
answer_information_text: Before stopping or turning, you must give a conspicuous signal of your intention for long enough to warn other road users.

question_text: You may not stop your vehicle...
answer_text_a: When a traffic officer instructs you to do so.
answer_text_b: If your vehicles brakes are faulty.
answer_text_c: Within 6 metres of any bridge, tunnel or subway.
correct_answer: C. Within 6 metres of any bridge, tunnel or subway.
answer_information_text: Regulation 304 prohibits stopping within six metres of a bridge, tunnel, or subway, subject to limited exceptions.

question_text: Acellular or mobile telephone or any other communication device should ... while driving.
answer_text_a: Not be handled with either hands or any other part of the body.
answer_text_b: Be handled with both hands
answer_text_c: Be handled with one hand
correct_answer: A. Not be handled with either hands or any other part of the body.
answer_information_text: A driver may not hold a cellular or mobile telephone or other communication device with either hand or any other part of the body while driving.

question_text: You may cross or enter a public road...
answer_text_a: If the road is clear for a short distance, even if moving traffic must brake to avoid you.
answer_text_b: Only if crossing can be completed with sufficient clearance from moving traffic without obstructing or endangering it, or entering can be done safely for yourself and other traffic.
answer_text_c: In any manner, as long as you use your indicator in time.
correct_answer: B. Only if crossing can be completed with sufficient clearance from moving traffic without obstructing or endangering it, or entering can be done safely for yourself and other traffic.
answer_information_text: To cross a public road, you need enough clearance from moving traffic to avoid obstructing or endangering it. To enter a public road, you must be able to do so safely for yourself and other traffic.

question_text: What must you do when you hear a siren or see red flashing lights from an ambulance or fire engine?
answer_text_a: The lane splits into more lanes in the direction of the arrow
answer_text_b: Flash your headlights to warn other traffic
answer_text_c: Give right of way to the emergency vehicle
correct_answer: C. Give right of way to the emergency vehicle
answer_information_text: A driver must give immediate right of way to an emergency vehicle sounding a siren or displaying the prescribed flashing lights.

question_text: What are the rules regarding electrical wiring and the battery of a vehicle when driving on the public road?
answer_text_a: They should be properly installed, insulated and maintained so that such wiring and battery do not cause a source of danger.
answer_text_b: They have to be in working condition.
answer_text_c: You have to replace them every 2 years, to ensure proper working order.
correct_answer: A. They should be properly installed, insulated and maintained so that such wiring and battery do not cause a source of danger.
answer_information_text: The vehicle rules require electrical wiring and the battery to be properly installed, insulated and maintained so they do not create a danger.

question_text: A South African Bureau of Standards (SABS) approved number plate should... (i) have clearly readable letters and figures. (ii) in an upright position or within 30 degrees of such position. (iii) not be personalised.
answer_text_a: (i) Only is correct
answer_text_b: (i) and (ii) Gnly are correct.
answer_text_c: (i) and (iii) Only are correct.
correct_answer: B. (i) and (ii) Gnly are correct.
answer_information_text: The plate must be clearly readable and upright within 30 degrees. Personalised plates are permitted, so (i) and (ii) only are correct.

question_text: What is your responsibility as a vehicle driver?
answer_text_a: Ensure that everyone is seated.
answer_text_b: Ensure you have drank an energy drink before driving,
answer_text_c: Ensure that all the people travelling in the vehicle wear a seatbelt
correct_answer: C. Ensure that all the people travelling in the vehicle wear a seatbelt
answer_information_text: The driver must ensure that passengers use the seatbelts provided. Being seated alone is not sufficient.

question_text: In which of these situations may you stop in a no-stopping zone? (i) If a traffic officer orders you to do so. (ii) For a situation beyond your control. (iii) To avoid an accident.
answer_text_a: (i), (ii) and (iii) are all correct
answer_text_b: (iii) only is correct
answer_text_c: (i) and (ii) only are correct
correct_answer: A. (i), (ii) and (iii) are all correct
answer_information_text: All three are recognized exceptions: an official instruction, a situation beyond the driver’s control, or avoiding an accident.

question_text: If your vehicle does not have ... then it is not allowed on a public road.
answer_text_a: A clutch
answer_text_b: An efficient exhaust silencer.
answer_text_c: A manual gearbox
correct_answer: B. An efficient exhaust silencer.
answer_information_text: A vehicle may not be used on a public road without an efficient exhaust silencer. A clutch and manual gearbox are not required on every vehicle.

question_text: If you see that someone wants to overtake you, you must... (i) Keep to the left as far as is safe. (ii) Not drive faster. (iii) Give hand signals to allow the person to pass safely.
answer_text_a: (ii) only is correct.
answer_text_b: (i) and (ii) only are correct.
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct.
correct_answer: B. (i) and (ii) only are correct.
answer_information_text: A driver being overtaken must keep left and must not accelerate. Giving a hand signal is not required.

question_text: You shall not stop on a freeway except. (i) In compliance with a road traffic sign. (ii) Ordered by a traffic officer. (iii) Any reason beyond your control.
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii)
answer_text_b: (i) and (iii)
answer_text_c: (i), (ii) and (iii)
correct_answer: C. (i), (ii) and (iii)
answer_information_text: A vehicle may stop on a freeway when a road sign or traffic officer requires it, or when a cause beyond the driver's control makes stopping necessary.

question_text: Goods should not be loaded on the vehicle in a way that it may...
answer_text_a: Come into contact with the road surface, or obscure the driver's view to the front, sides or rear
answer_text_b: Be covered with a tarpaulin
answer_text_c: Be secured with ropes or straps
correct_answer: A. Come into contact with the road surface, or obscure the driver's view to the front, sides or rear
answer_information_text: Goods must not be loaded so that they touch the road surface or block the driver's view of traffic to the front, sides or rear. Covering or tying down a load is what the law expects, not what it forbids.

question_text: A speed limit of... should apply in respect of every public road other than a freeway situated outside an urban area.
answer_text_a: 100 km/h
answer_text_b: 60 km/h
answer_text_c: 120 km/h
correct_answer: A. 100 km/h
answer_information_text: The general speed limit on a public road outside an urban area, excluding a freeway, is 100 km/h.

question_text: When is it not compulsory to wear a seatbelt? (i) When moving in or out of a parking area. (ii) When reversing your vehicle. (iii) When driving below 60 km/h
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii)
answer_text_b: (i) and (iii)
answer_text_c: All of the above
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii)
answer_information_text: Seatbelts are not compulsory while reversing or moving into or out of a parking area. Driving below 60 km/h is not an exemption.

question_text: For a motor car first registered after 1958 and used on a public road, its windscreen must... (i) Provide the driver with sufficient visibility for safe driving. (ii) Have visible light transmittance of at least 70 percent. (iii) Be made of safety glass. Which requirements apply?
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) only.
answer_text_b: (ii) and (iii) only.
answer_text_c: (i), (ii) and (iii).
correct_answer: C. (i), (ii) and (iii).
answer_information_text: A motor car first registered after 1958 and used on a public road must have a safety-glass windscreen that provides sufficient visibility for safe driving and transmits at least 70 percent of visible light.

question_text: A vehicle may not be operated on a public road if it...
answer_text_a: Causes excessive noise that could be avoided by exercising reasonable care.
answer_text_b: Carries 20 passengers.
answer_text_c: Moves at a low speed.
correct_answer: A. Causes excessive noise that could be avoided by exercising reasonable care.
answer_information_text: You may not operate or allow a vehicle to be operated on a public road if it makes excessive noise that reasonable care could prevent.

question_text: If you are towing a vehicle with faulty brakes, you must...
answer_text_a: Use a tow-bar or draw-bar and not a rope
answer_text_b: Not drive faster than 30 km/h
answer_text_c: Not carry more than one passenger in the towed vehicle
correct_answer: A. Use a tow-bar or draw-bar and not a rope
answer_information_text: A vehicle with faulty brakes may be towed only when connected by a drawbar or tow-bar, rather than a rope.

question_text: How long is a learner's license valid for?
answer_text_a: 12 moths
answer_text_b: 24 months
answer_text_c: 18 moths
correct_answer: B. 24 months
answer_information_text: A learner’s licence is valid for 24 months from the date of issue and cannot be extended.

question_text: Under the ordinary height limit, what is the maximum permitted overall height, including any load, of a motor vehicle other than a double-deck bus on a public road?
answer_text_a: 4.0 metres
answer_text_b: 4.65 metres
answer_text_c: 4.3 metres
correct_answer: C. 4.3 metres
answer_information_text: The ordinary maximum overall height of a motor vehicle other than a double-deck bus is 4.3 metres, including any load. The limit for a double-deck bus is 4.65 metres.

question_text: Any load carried on a vehicle must
answer_text_a: Not obscure the driver's view.
answer_text_b: Be covered with sheeting
answer_text_c: Have red triangles or flags tied to it
correct_answer: A. Not obscure the driver's view.
answer_information_text: A load must not obstruct the driver’s view of traffic. Covering and warning markers apply only in particular circumstances.

question_text: Before you reach the exit where you will be leaving the freeway, how should you position
answer_text_a: In the middle lane.
answer_text_b: In the left-hand lane.
answer_text_c: In the shoulder of the road
correct_answer: B. In the left-hand lane.
answer_information_text: Before taking a freeway exit, move into the left-hand lane in good time and prepare to leave safely.

question_text: Which statements about adjustable spotlights on vehicles operated on public roads are correct? (i) They may be fitted to vehicles belonging to medical practitioners or veterinarians and used for their professional work, or to breakdown vehicles and used only at an accident or breakdown scene or to inspect overhead telephone, telegraph or power lines. (ii) Adjustable spotlights must illuminate persons or vehicles at least 100 metres ahead. (iii) Game-spotting vehicles are exempt from the restriction on adjustable spotlights.
answer_text_a: Only statement (i) is correct.
answer_text_b: Statements (i) and (iii) only are correct.
answer_text_c: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are all correct.
correct_answer: A. Only statement (i) is correct.
answer_information_text: Adjustable spotlights are permitted on qualifying professional and breakdown vehicles subject to specific use restrictions; game spotting provides no public-road exemption. The 100-metre illumination requirement applies to main-beam headlamps.

question_text: Under adverse conditions such as rain, slippery road surface, poor visibility or when being followed too closely, the driver/rider of a vehicle shall
answer_text_a: Decrease their following distance.
answer_text_b: Put on emergency lights of their vehicles.
answer_text_c: Increase their following distance.
correct_answer: C. Increase their following distance.
answer_information_text: Following distance must be increased in rain, on slippery roads, in poor visibility and when being followed too closely.

question_text: Which of the following vehicles may, in the execution of their duties and while displaying the prescribed identification lamps, stop or park where necessary on a public road, provided they cause no unnecessary danger or confusion to other road users? (i) Fire-fighting vehicles. (ii) Ambulances and emergency medical response vehicles. (iii) Vehicles engaged in civil protection. (iv) Vehicles used for construction or maintenance of a public road.
answer_text_a: Only (i) and (ii).
answer_text_b: Only (i), (ii) and (iii).
answer_text_c: All four listed categories.
correct_answer: C. All four listed categories.
answer_information_text: All four listed categories qualify for this exemption when performing the relevant duties and displaying the prescribed identification lamps. They may stop or park only where necessary, without causing unnecessary danger or confusion to other road users.

question_text: Which of the following is allowed on a freeway? (i) Stopping or parking within an area reserved by an appropriate road traffic sign. (ii) Being on foot in the shoulder of the road under normal circumstances. (iii) Giving hand signals.
answer_text_a: Only (i) is correct
answer_text_b: All of the above are correct
answer_text_c: None of the above are correct
correct_answer: A. Only (i) is correct
answer_information_text: Stopping or parking in an area reserved by an appropriate sign is allowed. Walking on the shoulder normally and giving hand signals while driving on a freeway are not allowed.

question_text: Under normal circumstances a combination of motor vehicles is restricted to... (i) a drawing vehicle and a maximum of two trailers. (ii) a drawing vehicle and one other motor vehicle, which is not a trailer. (iii) a drawing vehicle and two other motor vehicles, which are not trailers.
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) are correct.
answer_text_b: Only (i) is correct.
answer_text_c: (i) and (iii) are correct.
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii) are correct.
answer_information_text: Normally, a combination may consist of a drawing vehicle with one or two trailers, or one other motor vehicle that is not a trailer. Two non-trailer vehicles are not generally permitted.

question_text: For a professional driver referred to in section 32, what is the minimum blood-alcohol concentration prohibited when driving on a public road?
answer_text_a: 0.2 g per 100 ml of blood
answer_text_b: 0.05 g per 100 ml of blood
answer_text_c: 0.02 g per 100 ml of blood
correct_answer: C. 0.02 g per 100 ml of blood
answer_information_text: A professional driver referred to in section 32 may not drive on a public road with a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.02 g per 100 ml or more. This is a separate offence from driving under the influence.

question_text: The number plate(s) of a vehicle should correspond with the...
answer_text_a: Province the vehicle is being used in
answer_text_b: Vehicle's roadworthy certificate
answer_text_c: Vehicle's licence disc
correct_answer: C. Vehicle's licence disc
answer_information_text: The number on the vehicle's plate must match the licence number shown on its licence disc. The province where the vehicle is being used does not determine the plate.

question_text: Which of the following vehicles are regarded as emergency vehicles? (i) A fire-fighting vehicle (with red warning light). (ii) An ambulance (with red warning light). (iii) A vehicle driven by a traffic officer in the carrying out of duties (blue warning light). (iv) A vehicle driven by a person while engaged in civil protection (green warning light).
answer_text_a: (i), (ii) and (iii) only are correct
answer_text_b: All of the above are correct.
answer_text_c: Only (i) and (ii) are correct
correct_answer: B. All of the above are correct.
answer_information_text: Fire-fighting vehicles, ambulances, traffic-officer vehicles on duty, and vehicles used for civil protection are treated as emergency vehicles.

question_text: The windscreen of a light motor vehicle must have visible light transmittance through the windscreen of...
answer_text_a: at least 70 percent
answer_text_b: at least 30 percent
answer_text_c: 100 percent
correct_answer: A. at least 70 percent
answer_information_text: A light motor vehicle’s windscreen must allow at least 70 percent visible light transmittance.

question_text: The driver/rider of a vehicle intending to pass a stationary bus must...
answer_text_a: Accelerate and drive past the bus as quick as possible, in case it moves off when your vehicle is next to it.
answer_text_b: Be on the lookout for persons approaching or leaving or who might approach or leave such bus
answer_text_c: Stop behind such bus and wait for it to move off.
correct_answer: B. Be on the lookout for persons approaching or leaving or who might approach or leave such bus
answer_information_text: A driver passing a stationary bus must take care for people approaching, leaving, or likely to approach or leave the bus.

question_text: When driving a motor vehicle on a public road which is divided into traffic lanes by means of road markings, the driver/rider shall not turn from one lane into another unless he/she...
answer_text_a: Can speed up enough to take a gap between traffic
answer_text_b: Has a clear view of the road ahead for atleast 150 m.
answer_text_c: Can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic.
correct_answer: C. Can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic.
answer_information_text: A lane change is permitted only when it can be made without obstructing or endangering other traffic.

question_text: The tread pattern of your vehicle's tyres may not be less than... mm.
answer_information_text: Tyre tread must be at least 1 mm deep with a clearly visible pattern around the tyre.

question_text: What colour and how many retro-reflectors should be fitted on the rear of a light motor vehicle?
answer_text_a: Two red retro-reflectors.
answer_text_b: Two pink retro-reflectors.
answer_text_c: Three yellow retro-reflectors.
correct_answer: A. Two red retro-reflectors.
answer_information_text: A light motor vehicle must have two red retro-reflectors at the rear, one on each side. This is stated in Regulation 187.

question_text: A person driving a vehicle on a public road should never . . .
answer_text_a: Drive slower than the speed limit
answer_text_b: Drive on the road that has potholes.
answer_text_c: Negligently or willfully deposit any petrol or other liquid fuel or any oil or grease or other flammable or offensive matter, ashes or other refuse, of whatever nature, from such vehicle upon or alongside such road.
correct_answer: C. Negligently or willfully deposit any petrol or other liquid fuel or any oil or grease or other flammable or offensive matter, ashes or other refuse, of whatever nature, from such vehicle upon or alongside such road.
answer_information_text: A driver may not negligently or wilfully deposit fuel, oil, grease, flammable matter or refuse on or alongside a public road.

question_text: When towing a vehicle fitted with steering gear on a public road, with its steerable wheels on the ground and not controlled by the connecting device, who must control its steering gear?
answer_text_a: Any person who knows how to steer, even without a driving licence.
answer_text_b: A person holding a driving licence authorising them to drive that class of vehicle.
answer_text_c: A person holding any driving licence, even if it does not authorise them to drive that class of vehicle.
correct_answer: B. A person holding a driving licence authorising them to drive that class of vehicle.
answer_information_text: In these circumstances, the towed vehicle's steering gear must be controlled by a person holding a driving licence authorising them to drive that class of vehicle.

question_text: A driver/rider should not drive/ride a vehicle on a public road . . . . . .
answer_text_a: If it does not have a car stereo.
answer_text_b: In such a manner that wilfully disregard the safety of individuals or property.
answer_text_c: If it does not have a sunroof.
correct_answer: B. In such a manner that wilfully disregard the safety of individuals or property.
answer_information_text: A driver must not drive recklessly or negligently, including deliberately disregarding the safety of people or property.

question_text: You should not park a vehicle on the roadway of a public road if . . .
answer_text_a: You have a flat tire.
answer_text_b: It is beyond your control.
answer_text_c: It will obstruct any private or public vehicular entrance
correct_answer: C. It will obstruct any private or public vehicular entrance
answer_information_text: Parking is prohibited where the vehicle would obstruct a private or public vehicular entrance. A flat tyre does not itself prohibit parking.

question_text: You should not park a vehicle on the roadway of a public road within an urban area if . . .
answer_text_a: The vehicle has been forced to stop by a cause beyond your control.
answer_text_b: The vehicle is within 5 metres of any intersection and no road traffic sign permits parking there.
answer_text_c: The vehicle has been forced to stop because of a flat tyre.
correct_answer: B. The vehicle is within 5 metres of any intersection and no road traffic sign permits parking there.
answer_information_text: Parking on the roadway within an urban area is prohibited within 5 metres of any intersection unless a road traffic sign permits parking there.

question_text: Unless a statutory speed-limit exemption applies, a driver/rider on a public road may never . . .
answer_text_a: Exceed the applicable speed limit when overtaking or passing.
answer_text_b: Have passengers when overtaking.
answer_text_c: Pass to the right at a safe distance when overtaking is otherwise lawful.
correct_answer: A. Exceed the applicable speed limit when overtaking or passing.
answer_information_text: Overtaking or passing does not permit you to exceed the applicable speed limit unless a statutory speed-limit exemption applies.

question_text: You may not drive a motor vehicle on a public road while the concentration of alcohol in your body is . . . in a case of a professional driver
answer_text_a: 0,01 grams per 100ml of blood or more
answer_text_b: 0,002 grams per 100ml of blood or more
answer_text_c: 0,02 grams per 100ml of blood or more
correct_answer: C. 0,02 grams per 100ml of blood or more
answer_information_text: For a professional driver, driving is prohibited at a blood-alcohol concentration of 0.02 grams per 100 ml or more. This is stated in section 65 of the National Road Traffic Act.

question_text: Pedestrians should cross a roadway only at a pedestrian crossing, at an intersection or a distance further than ..... from such pedestrian or intersection crossing.
answer_text_c: 9m
correct_answer: A. 50m
answer_information_text: A pedestrian may cross at a pedestrian crossing or intersection, or more than 50 m away from one. This is stated in Regulation 316.

question_text: Which statements about stop lamps are correct for motor vehicles other than tractors and trailers drawn by tractors? (i) A vehicle without stop lamps may not be driven on a public road. (ii) You may drive a vehicle without stop lamps on a public road. (iii) When in use, stop lamps must be visible in normal sunlight from at least 30 metres away to a person of normal eyesight.
answer_text_a: Only statement (ii) is correct.
answer_text_b: Statements (i) and (iii) are correct.
answer_text_c: All of the above.
correct_answer: B. Statements (i) and (iii) are correct.
answer_information_text: Motor vehicles other than tractors and trailers drawn by tractors must have stop lamps to be operated on a public road. When in use, these lamps must emit red light visible in normal sunlight from at least 30 metres away to a person of normal eyesight.

question_text: Which statement is correct about number plates?
answer_text_a: A valid licence disc allows you to drive without required number plates on a public road.
answer_text_b: A driver may remove required number plates when driving on a freeway.
answer_text_c: As a general rule, required number plates must be securely attached, clearly legible and visible.
correct_answer: C. As a general rule, required number plates must be securely attached, clearly legible and visible.
answer_information_text: Required number plates must normally be securely attached, clearly legible and visible. The 20-metre requirement concerns the white light illuminating the rear number plate.

question_text: Under regulation 225, except for a bus-train or a twin-steer four-axle rigid goods vehicle, the maximum permitted turning radius of a motor vehicle on a public road is . . . .
answer_text_a: 6 metres.
answer_text_b: 15 metres.
answer_text_c: 13.1 metres.
correct_answer: C. 13.1 metres.
answer_information_text: The general maximum turning radius is 13.1 metres. Bus-trains and twin-steer four-axle rigid goods vehicles have a maximum turning radius of 17.5 metres.

question_text: What are the rules regarding a vehicle hooter?
answer_text_a: You may use your hooter for safety reasons and it must be audible from 90 metres away.
answer_text_b: You may use the hooter to get attention from pedestrians.
answer_text_c: You may use the hooter for other drivers on the road.
correct_answer: A. You may use your hooter for safety reasons and it must be audible from 90 metres away.
answer_information_text: The hooter may be used when necessary for safety, and the warning device must be audible from 90 metres. Simply seeking attention is not a general permitted use.

question_text: The wipers of your windscreen should . . . . .
answer_text_a: Be black in colour.
answer_text_b: Wipe the outside of the windscreen directly in front of the driver,continuously, evenly and adequately.
answer_text_c: Be able to wipe the sunroof window.
correct_answer: B. Wipe the outside of the windscreen directly in front of the driver,continuously, evenly and adequately.
answer_information_text: The windscreen wiper must wipe the outside of the windscreen directly in front of the driver continuously, evenly and adequately. Regulation 203 states this requirement.

question_text: Before you reach the exit where you will be exiting the freeway, which lane should you position yourself on the roadway
answer_text_a: On the shoulder of the road.
answer_text_b: In the middle lane.
answer_text_c: On the left-hand lane.
correct_answer: C. On the left-hand lane.
answer_information_text: To take a freeway exit, move into the left-hand lane in good time before reaching the exit. The shoulder is not a travel lane.

question_text: Which statement about adjustable spot lamps on vehicles operated on public roads is correct?
answer_text_a: They must illuminate other vehicles or people at least 100 metres ahead.
answer_text_b: They are permitted merely because a vehicle is used for game spotting.
answer_text_c: They may be fitted to vehicles owned by medical practitioners or veterinarians for use in their professional duties, or to breakdown vehicles for use at an accident or breakdown scene.
correct_answer: C. They may be fitted to vehicles owned by medical practitioners or veterinarians for use in their professional duties, or to breakdown vehicles for use at an accident or breakdown scene.
answer_information_text: Adjustable spot lamps are generally prohibited on vehicles operated on public roads, except for specified official, professional and service uses. Game spotting alone is not an exception, and the 100-metre lighting requirement does not apply to adjustable spot lamps.

question_text: When are you allowed to park in a parking bay reserved for disabled individuals? (i) If you are a disabled person or the driver of a motor vehicle conveying disabled individuals. (ii) If such vehicle is issued with a sticker for disabled individuals or conveying of disabled individuals. (iii) If you are conveying elderly individuals. (iv) If you have an emergency and there are no other parking bays available.
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) are correct.
answer_text_b: (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
answer_text_c: All of the above.
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii) are correct.
answer_information_text: A disabled person or a vehicle conveying disabled persons may use the bay, with the required disabled-persons sticker for the conveying vehicle. Carrying elderly people or having an emergency does not create an exception.

question_text: Unless permitted by an appropriate road traffic sign, what is the maximum distance between the edge of the roadway and the outside of any left-hand wheel of a vehicle parked on the left-hand side of a public road within an urban area?
answer_text_a: 300 mm
answer_text_b: 550 mm
answer_text_c: 450 mm
correct_answer: C. 450 mm
answer_information_text: The outside of any left-hand wheel must be no more than 450 mm from the edge of the roadway, unless an appropriate road traffic sign permits otherwise.

question_text: Which of the following vehicles may stop or park where necessary on a public road, provided they display the prescribed identification lamps while stopped or parked and cause no unnecessary danger or confusion to other road users? (i) Fire-fighting vehicles being driven in the execution of the driver's duties. (ii) Ambulances and emergency medical response vehicles being driven in the execution of the driver's duties. (iii) A vehicle whose driver is engaged in civil protection. (iv) A vehicle being used in connection with the construction or maintenance of a public road.
answer_text_a: Only (i) and (ii).
answer_text_b: All four listed categories.
answer_text_c: Only (i), (ii) and (iii).
correct_answer: B. All four listed categories.
answer_information_text: All four listed categories qualify for this stopping or parking exemption. They must stop or park only where necessary, display the prescribed identification lamps while stopped or parked, and cause no unnecessary danger or confusion to other road users.

question_text: Which statement is true with regards to a vehicle's fuel tank?
answer_text_a: You may drive your vehicle with a cloth in the filling orifice of the fuel tank until you are able to replace the fuel cap.
answer_text_b: You only have to put a cap on the filling orifice of the fuel tank if you don't want to spill and loose fuel whilst driving.
answer_text_c: The filling orifice of the fuel tank must be fitted with an effective cap at all times.
correct_answer: C. The filling orifice of the fuel tank must be fitted with an effective cap at all times.
answer_information_text: The fuel-tank filling orifice must have an effective cap. A cloth or an optional cap does not meet this requirement under Regulation 205.

question_text: What special maximum speed applies to a goods vehicle over 9 000 kg GVM, a goods vehicle towing one or two trailers with a total GVM (drawing vehicle plus trailers) over 9 000 kg, an articulated motor vehicle with a truck-tractor GCM over 9 000 kg, or a breakdown vehicle towing another vehicle, subject to any lower general or signposted speed limit?
answer_text_a: 80 km/h.
answer_text_c: 60 km/h.
correct_answer: A. 80 km/h.
answer_information_text: The special maximum speed for these vehicle categories is 80 km/h. Any lower general or signposted speed limit must still be obeyed.

question_text: What is the overall length allowed in the case of a combination of vehicles, consisting of a drawing vehicle and a semi-trailer?
answer_information_text: A drawing vehicle and semi-trailer combination may not exceed an overall length of 18.5 metres, including the drawbar or coupling, under Regulation 221.

question_text: If a light or heavy motor vehicle is fitted with brackets for the conveyance of goods, such brackets may not project more than ..... beyond the widest part of such vehicle, excluding side mirrors and direction indicators.
answer_text_a: 450mm
answer_text_b: 300mm
answer_text_c: 150mm
correct_answer: C. 150mm
answer_information_text: A bracket may project no more than 150 millimetres beyond the vehicle's widest part, excluding the permitted mirror and indicator projections, under Regulation 227.

question_text: May a motorcycle be used to tow another vehicle on a public road?
answer_text_a: Yes, if the towed vehicle is lightweight.
answer_text_b: No, a motorcycle may not tow another vehicle.
answer_text_c: Yes, but only below 30 km/h.
correct_answer: B. No, a motorcycle may not tow another vehicle.
answer_information_text: Regulation 330 prohibits using a motorcycle, motor tricycle, motor quadrucycle or pedal cycle to tow another vehicle.

question_text: What reflective equipment must a goods vehicle with a GVM exceeding 10 000 kg display?
answer_text_a: Red reflective material only along both sides.
answer_text_b: White reflective material only on the front.
answer_text_c: Yellow reflective material along both sides and across the rear.
correct_answer: C. Yellow reflective material along both sides and across the rear.
answer_information_text: Goods vehicles over 10 000 kg must display yellow reflective material on both sides and the rear.

question_text: On a dual-carriageway with two lanes in your direction, which lane should you use to overtake slower traffic travelling in the left-hand lane, when safe and permitted?
answer_text_a: The right-hand lane.
answer_text_b: The left-hand lane.
answer_text_c: The emergency lane on the shoulder.
correct_answer: A. The right-hand lane.
answer_information_text: Use the right-hand lane to overtake traffic travelling in the left-hand lane when it is safe and permitted. You must not use the shoulder to overtake.

question_text: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with its warning signal operating?
answer_text_a: Follow closely behind it to move through traffic more quickly.
answer_text_b: Give it right of way by moving left or stopping if necessary, and let it pass safely.
answer_text_c: Maintain your speed because the emergency vehicle must wait for you.
correct_answer: B. Give it right of way by moving left or stopping if necessary, and let it pass safely.
answer_information_text: An emergency vehicle using its warning signal has right of way. Move left or stop when necessary so it can pass safely.

question_text: Which statement about seat belts is correct?
answer_text_a: Only the driver is required to wear a seat belt.
answer_text_b: Seat belts are compulsory only when travelling on a freeway.
answer_text_c: The driver must ensure that occupants comply with the applicable seat-belt or child-restraint requirements.
correct_answer: C. The driver must ensure that occupants comply with the applicable seat-belt or child-restraint requirements.
answer_information_text: The driver must ensure that occupants comply with applicable seat-belt and child-restraint requirements under Regulation 213.

question_text: Which circumstance can lawfully exempt a person from wearing a seat belt?
answer_text_a: The journey is shorter than five kilometres.
answer_text_b: A medical exemption has been granted on the prescribed grounds and conditions.
answer_text_c: The person is seated in the rear of the vehicle.
correct_answer: B. A medical exemption has been granted on the prescribed grounds and conditions.
answer_information_text: Regulation 213 allows an exemption from wearing a seat belt on approved medical grounds and subject to the applicable conditions.

question_text: Which situation requires a driver to stop?
answer_text_a: The driver approaches an empty intersection with no stop sign or signal.
answer_text_b: A pedestrian is standing beside the road but is not crossing.
answer_text_c: A road traffic sign or a uniformed traffic officer directs the driver to stop.
correct_answer: C. A road traffic sign or a uniformed traffic officer directs the driver to stop.
answer_information_text: A driver must stop when directed by a stop sign or other traffic sign, or by a uniformed traffic officer.

question_text: Which is a lawful circumstance in which a person may be on foot on a freeway?
answer_text_a: Within an area reserved for stopping or parking by an appropriate road traffic sign.
answer_text_b: Across the freeway whenever traffic is light.
answer_text_c: On the shoulder whenever it provides a shorter walking route.
correct_answer: A. Within an area reserved for stopping or parking by an appropriate road traffic sign.
answer_information_text: A person may be on foot on a freeway within an appropriately signed stopping or parking area.

question_text: Apart from a formal medical exemption, when may an adult drive without wearing the seat belt fitted to the vehicle?
answer_text_a: Whenever driving on an urban road.
answer_text_b: While reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay or area.
answer_text_c: Whenever travelling below 40 km/h.
correct_answer: B. While reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay or area.
answer_information_text: An adult may omit the seat belt while reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay or area. A medical exemption is the other recognised exception.

question_text: May a driver allow the vehicle to straddle two marked traffic lanes while travelling along the road?
answer_text_a: Yes; provided the driver is travelling below the speed limit.
answer_text_b: Yes; whenever traffic is moving slowly.
answer_text_c: No; the vehicle should remain within one lane unless changing lanes safely.
correct_answer: C. No; the vehicle should remain within one lane unless changing lanes safely.
answer_information_text: A vehicle should remain within its lane. It may cross into another lane only when changing lanes safely and without obstructing or endangering traffic.

question_text: When they conflict, which instruction takes priority over traffic signals and road markings?
answer_text_a: A traffic-light signal.
answer_text_b: A road-surface marking.
answer_text_c: An instruction given by a traffic officer.
correct_answer: C. An instruction given by a traffic officer.
answer_information_text: A traffic officer's instruction takes priority over conflicting traffic signals and road markings.

question_text: Which circumstance can disqualify a person from obtaining a learner’s licence?
answer_text_a: Being addicted to a drug with a narcotic effect.
answer_text_b: Wearing glasses that correct vision to the prescribed standard.
answer_text_c: Being deaf while otherwise meeting the licensing requirements.
correct_answer: A. Being addicted to a drug with a narcotic effect.
answer_information_text: Addiction to a drug with a narcotic effect disqualifies a person from obtaining or holding a learner’s licence. Deafness alone and corrected vision do not automatically disqualify the applicant.

question_text: When driving at night through a city centre, which lights should normally be used?
answer_text_a: Main-beam headlights.
answer_text_b: Dipped-beam headlights.
answer_text_c: Parking lamps only.
correct_answer: B. Dipped-beam headlights.
answer_information_text: Dipped-beam headlights should normally be used at night in a city centre; main beam can dazzle other road users.

question_text: How should you check whether another vehicle is in a blind spot beside you?
answer_text_a: Turn your head and look over the appropriate shoulder
answer_text_b: Flash your headlamps and wait for a response
answer_text_c: Look only in the interior rear-view mirror
correct_answer: A. Turn your head and look over the appropriate shoulder
answer_information_text: Mirrors do not cover every area beside and behind the vehicle. Turn your head and look over the appropriate shoulder to check the blind spot.

question_text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches while sounding its siren?
answer_text_a: Follow closely behind it to pass through traffic
answer_text_b: Maintain your course and speed because it must overtake you safely
answer_text_c: Give it immediate and absolute right of way, moving aside safely as necessary
correct_answer: C. Give it immediate and absolute right of way, moving aside safely as necessary
answer_information_text: An emergency vehicle sounding its siren must be given immediate and absolute right of way. Move aside safely and allow it to pass.

question_text: What must you obtain before practising driving a particular class of motor vehicle on a public road?
answer_text_a: A valid learner's licence authorising that class of vehicle
answer_text_b: Written permission from the vehicle's owner
answer_text_c: A receipt showing that you have booked a learner's licence test
correct_answer: A. A valid learner's licence authorising that class of vehicle
answer_information_text: You must hold a valid learner’s licence authorising the class of vehicle you are practising to drive.

question_text: Which statement about an adult travelling in a motor vehicle on a public road is correct?
answer_text_a: Wearing a seatbelt is optional when travelling below 60 km/h
answer_text_b: The adult must wear the seatbelt fitted to the occupied seat, except while reversing or moving into or out of a parking area
answer_text_c: Only the driver and front-seat passenger must wear seatbelts
correct_answer: B. The adult must wear the seatbelt fitted to the occupied seat, except while reversing or moving into or out of a parking area
answer_information_text: Regulation 213 requires adults to wear an available seatbelt, with exceptions for reversing and moving into or out of a parking bay or area.

question_text: When must you keep your learner's licence with you in the vehicle?
answer_text_a: Only when attending a driving lesson with a registered instructor
answer_text_b: Only when taking the practical driving test
answer_text_c: Whenever you drive on a public road under its authority
correct_answer: C. Whenever you drive on a public road under its authority
answer_information_text: You must keep your learner’s licence with you whenever you drive on a public road under its authority.

question_text: Who may park a motor vehicle in a parking bay reserved for disabled persons?
answer_text_a: A disabled person entitled to use the reserved bay
answer_text_b: Any driver making a stop of less than five minutes
answer_text_c: Any driver who remains in the vehicle
correct_answer: A. A disabled person entitled to use the reserved bay
answer_information_text: A disabled person may use the reserved bay; an authorised vehicle conveying disabled persons may also qualify. Remaining in the vehicle or stopping briefly is not enough.

question_text: When may you drive, pull or push a motor vehicle on a sidewalk?
answer_text_a: When travelling slowly to pass a stationary vehicle
answer_text_b: Never
answer_text_c: When the roadway is congested
correct_answer: B. Never
answer_information_text: A vehicle may not be driven, pulled or pushed on a sidewalk.

question_text: For a motor vehicle required to carry an emergency warning triangle, when must the triangle normally be displayed?
answer_text_a: Only after a collision in which someone is injured
answer_text_b: Whenever the vehicle is travelling substantially below the speed limit
answer_text_c: When the vehicle is stationary on the roadway or shoulder of a public road
correct_answer: C. When the vehicle is stationary on the roadway or shoulder of a public road
answer_information_text: When such a vehicle is stationary on the roadway or shoulder of a public road, an emergency warning triangle must normally be displayed, subject to limited exceptions.

question_text: Unless a special provision for certain buses applies, what is the maximum overall width of a motor vehicle with a GVM below 12 000 kg on a public road?
answer_text_a: 2.5 metres
answer_text_b: 2.6 metres
answer_text_c: 3.0 metres
correct_answer: A. 2.5 metres
answer_information_text: Regulation 223 sets the general maximum overall width at 2.5 metres. Certain large buses and goods vehicles have separate 2.6-metre provisions.

question_text: Between sunset and sunrise, when must a parked motor vehicle display permitted lights, such as parking lamps?
answer_text_a: When it is parked on the roadway of a public road, outside a parking place demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs, and more than 12 metres from a lighted street lamp illuminating that road
answer_text_b: Whenever it is parked in a parking place demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs
answer_text_c: Whenever it is parked off the roadway of a public road
correct_answer: A. When it is parked on the roadway of a public road, outside a parking place demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs, and more than 12 metres from a lighted street lamp illuminating that road
answer_information_text: At night, parked motor vehicles must display lights unless parked off the roadway, in a parking place demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs, or within 12 metres of a lighted street lamp illuminating that road. The front-light requirement may be met by dipped headlights, compliant parking lamps or two compliant fog lamps.

question_text: Which circumstance disqualifies a person from obtaining a learner's licence?
answer_text_a: The applicant is 75 years old
answer_text_b: The applicant has a medical condition that is controlled and does not make the person unfit to drive
answer_text_c: A court-imposed disqualification from obtaining or holding a driving licence is still in force
correct_answer: C. A court-imposed disqualification from obtaining or holding a driving licence is still in force
answer_information_text: A current court or authority disqualification from obtaining or holding a driving licence also prevents issue of a learner’s licence. Being 75 is not by itself disqualifying, and a controlled condition that does not make the person unfit is not disqualifying.

question_text: Which parking position is prohibited on a public road?
answer_text_a: Parking where the vehicle obscures a road traffic sign
answer_text_b: Parking in a bay where a road traffic sign expressly permits parking
answer_text_c: Parking completely off the public road on private property with the owner's permission
correct_answer: A. Parking where the vehicle obscures a road traffic sign
answer_information_text: A vehicle may not be parked where it obscures a road traffic sign. The other choices describe permitted parking situations.

question_text: What is required at the filling opening of a motor vehicle's fuel tank?
answer_text_a: It may be closed with a cloth while the vehicle is driven
answer_text_b: It must be fitted with an effective fuel cap
answer_text_c: A cap is optional if the tank is less than half full
correct_answer: B. It must be fitted with an effective fuel cap
answer_information_text: The fuel-tank filling opening must have an effective cap when the vehicle is used on a public road. A cloth or low fuel level does not replace this requirement.

question_text: A vehicle's main-beam headlights must enable the driver to see a person, vehicle or substantial object at least how far ahead?
answer_text_a: 100 metres
answer_text_b: 45 metres
answer_text_c: 200 metres
correct_answer: A. 100 metres
answer_information_text: Main-beam headlights must enable the driver to see a person, vehicle or substantial object at least 100 metres ahead.

question_text: How close to a bridge is a driver prohibited from parking?
answer_text_a: Within 9 metres
answer_text_b: Within 6 metres
answer_text_c: Within 10 metres
correct_answer: B. Within 6 metres
answer_information_text: Parking is prohibited within 6 metres of a bridge.

question_text: May motorcyclists ride two abreast simply because the road appears wide enough?
answer_text_a: Yes, whenever there is enough space
answer_text_b: No; they must ride in single file, except when overtaking another motorcycle
answer_text_c: Yes, but only outside urban areas
correct_answer: B. No; they must ride in single file, except when overtaking another motorcycle
answer_information_text: Motorcycles must travel in single file; riding abreast is not allowed merely because there is space. Passing another motorcycle is the recognised exception.

question_text: What is the general maximum overall length of a single motor vehicle, excluding a bus, articulated vehicle and any combination of motor vehicles?
answer_text_a: 22 metres
answer_text_b: 18.5 metres
answer_text_c: 12.5 metres
correct_answer: C. 12.5 metres
answer_information_text: Regulation 221 sets the general maximum for another single vehicle at 12.5 metres; the larger limits apply to combinations.

question_text: When is an adult occupant not required to wear a fitted seat belt?
answer_text_a: When travelling on a road with little traffic
answer_text_b: While the vehicle is reversing or being moved into or out of a parking bay or area
answer_text_c: Whenever the vehicle is travelling below 60 km/h
correct_answer: B. While the vehicle is reversing or being moved into or out of a parking bay or area
answer_information_text: Under Regulation 213, the seat-belt requirement does not apply while reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay or area.

question_text: When may a motor vehicle be moved onto a pedestrian sidewalk?
answer_text_a: When the road surface is damaged
answer_text_b: When traffic is congested
answer_text_c: Never
correct_answer: C. Never
answer_information_text: A motor vehicle may not be driven, pulled or pushed onto a sidewalk. Traffic congestion or road damage does not create a general exception.

question_text: When may you talk on a cellphone while driving?
answer_text_a: When it is used hands-free through a device fixed to the vehicle or a compliant headset, without holding it
answer_text_b: When traffic is moving slowly
answer_text_c: When you hold it below the steering wheel
correct_answer: A. When it is used hands-free through a device fixed to the vehicle or a compliant headset, without holding it
answer_information_text: Regulation 308A permits use of a cellphone only when it is affixed to the vehicle or used through compliant hands-free headgear, without holding it.

question_text: Assuming all other legal towing requirements are met, which arrangement is allowed?
answer_text_a: A motor car tows another vehicle with a tow-rope at 40 km/h
answer_text_b: A vehicle tows another vehicle with a tow-bar at 30 km/h
answer_text_c: A motorcycle tows another vehicle with a tow-rope at 20 km/h
correct_answer: B. A vehicle tows another vehicle with a tow-bar at 30 km/h
answer_information_text: A vehicle may tow another vehicle at up to 30 km/h with a tow-bar. Towing above 30 km/h requires a tow-bar or drawbar, and a motorcycle may not tow another vehicle.

question_text: Which location is prohibited for parking in an urban area?
answer_text_a: At the left edge of a wide road, more than 5 metres from an intersection and otherwise permitted
answer_text_b: In a marked parking bay on a wider road, with no restriction applying
answer_text_c: On the roadway of a two-way public road that is less than 5.5 metres wide
correct_answer: C. On the roadway of a two-way public road that is less than 5.5 metres wide
answer_information_text: In an urban area, parking on the roadway of a two-way public road less than 5.5 metres wide is prohibited. The narrow-road exception requires both one-way traffic and appropriate signs permitting parking.

question_text: Which circumstance disqualifies a person from obtaining a learner’s licence while it remains in force?
answer_text_a: The person’s driving licence was suspended by a competent authority and the suspension has not expired
answer_text_b: The person has never held a driving licence
answer_text_c: The person is 75 years old but meets the medical and eyesight requirements
correct_answer: A. The person’s driving licence was suspended by a competent authority and the suspension has not expired
answer_information_text: Section 15 of the National Road Traffic Act disqualifies a person from obtaining a learner’s licence while an existing driving-licence suspension remains in force.

question_text: How many number plates must a light or heavy motor vehicle normally display when used on a public road?
answer_text_a: One, at the rear only
answer_text_b: Two, one at the front and one at the rear
answer_text_c: Three, at the front, rear and roof
correct_answer: B. Two, one at the front and one at the rear
answer_information_text: A light or heavy motor vehicle normally displays two number plates: one at the front and one at the rear.

question_text: How must you respond when all the traffic lights facing you are flashing red at an intersection?
answer_text_a: Slow down and continue because you have right of way
answer_text_b: Stop and proceed only when safe, applying the rules for a three-way or four-way stop
answer_text_c: Remain stationary until a steady green light appears
correct_answer: B. Stop and proceed only when safe, applying the rules for a three-way or four-way stop
answer_information_text: Flashing red traffic lights require a complete stop. Proceed only when safe, following the applicable stop-intersection rules.

question_text: Under which conditions may fog lamps be illuminated while a vehicle is being driven on a public road?
answer_text_a: When visibility is poor because of snow, fog, mist, dust or smoke
answer_text_b: Whenever it is raining or the road surface is wet
answer_text_c: At any time between sunset and sunrise
correct_answer: A. When visibility is poor because of snow, fog, mist, dust or smoke
answer_information_text: Regulation 163(6) permits fog lamps only in poor visibility caused by snow, fog, mist, dust or smoke.

question_text: What is the maximum permitted length of a tow-rope, chain or tow-bar between a towing vehicle and the vehicle being towed?
answer_text_a: 5 metres
answer_text_b: 3.5 metres
answer_text_c: 2.5 metres
correct_answer: B. 3.5 metres
answer_information_text: Regulation 330(a) limits the distance between the towing and towed vehicles to 3.5 metres.

question_text: Which colours may a vehicle's direction indicators show while operating?
answer_text_a: Amber or red to the front, and white or yellow to the rear
answer_text_b: White only to the front and red only to the rear
answer_text_c: White, yellow or amber to the front, and yellow, amber or red to the rear
correct_answer: C. White, yellow or amber to the front, and yellow, amber or red to the rear
answer_information_text: Regulation 194(g) allows white, yellow or amber to the front, and yellow, amber or red to the rear.

question_text: How should you respond when approaching a vehicle stopped at the roadside?
answer_text_a: Slow down, leave sufficient clearance and watch for people or the vehicle moving into your path
answer_text_b: Maintain your speed because the vehicle is outside your traffic lane
answer_text_c: Sound the hooter and accelerate past before the vehicle moves off
correct_answer: A. Slow down, leave sufficient clearance and watch for people or the vehicle moving into your path
answer_information_text: Slow down, leave enough clearance, and watch for pedestrians or the stopped vehicle moving into your path.

question_text: At a three-way or four-way stop, which vehicle should move off first when several vehicles are waiting?
answer_text_a: The largest vehicle
answer_text_b: The vehicle that stopped first
answer_text_c: The vehicle travelling straight ahead, regardless of when it stopped
correct_answer: B. The vehicle that stopped first
answer_information_text: At a three-way or four-way stop, the vehicle that stopped first should move off first, provided it is safe.

question_text: Which statement correctly describes how goods must be carried on a vehicle using a public road?
answer_text_a: They may be left unsecured if the journey is shorter than 10 kilometres
answer_text_b: They may block the driver's rearward view if the vehicle is travelling below 60 km/h
answer_text_c: They must be safely contained or securely fastened and protected against being dislodged or spilled
correct_answer: C. They must be safely contained or securely fastened and protected against being dislodged or spilled
answer_information_text: Goods must be safely contained or securely fastened and protected against being dislodged or spilled. They must also not obstruct the driver’s view.

question_text: Where must the licence disc be displayed on a motor vehicle fitted with a transparent windscreen?
answer_text_a: On the lower left-hand corner of the windscreen, clearly legible from outside
answer_text_b: On the lower right-hand corner of the rear window
answer_text_c: In the centre of the windscreen behind the rear-view mirror
correct_answer: A. On the lower left-hand corner of the windscreen, clearly legible from outside
answer_information_text: The licence disc must be displayed in the lower left-hand corner of a transparent windscreen and be legible from outside.

question_text: On an otherwise unrestricted urban roadway, where no sign permits closer parking, which vehicle is parked illegally?
answer_text_a: A vehicle parked six metres from an intersection
answer_text_b: A vehicle parked two metres to the side of a clearly visible fire hydrant
answer_text_c: A vehicle parked three metres from an intersection
correct_answer: C. A vehicle parked three metres from an intersection
answer_information_text: Parking within five metres of an intersection is prohibited unless specifically permitted, so three metres is illegal. Two metres from a clearly visible hydrant is outside the one-and-a-half-metre restriction.

question_text: When is it okay to disobey a road sign?
answer_text_a: When the traffic officer orders you to do so
answer_text_b: Under no circumstance.
answer_text_c: If it is safe to do so.
correct_answer: A. When the traffic officer orders you to do so
answer_information_text: A traffic officer’s lawful instruction takes precedence over a road sign, so the sign may be disobeyed when the officer directs you to do so.

question_text: The minimum required tyre tread depth for light motor vehicles is: / (i) 5mm / (ii) 0.5mm / (iii) 1mm
answer_text_a: (iii) only is correct
answer_text_b: (ii) only is correct
answer_text_c: (i) only is correct
correct_answer: A. (iii) only is correct
answer_information_text: Light motor vehicle tyres must have at least 1 mm of visible tread depth. The 5 mm and 0.5 mm options are incorrect.
answer_text_d: All of the above are correct

question_text: A vehicle left unattended on a public road: (i) must have its parking lights switched on if left unattended for more than 1 hour (ii) must be locked (iii) must have its brake set or be secured by another method that effectively prevents it from moving
