answer_text_a: (i) only is correct
answer_text_b: (iii) only is correct
answer_text_c: (ii) only is correct
correct_answer: B. (iii) only is correct
answer_information_text: An unattended vehicle on a public road must have its brake set or be secured by another effective method to prevent movement. There is no general one-hour parking-light requirement or compulsory locking requirement.
answer_text_d: All of the above are correct

question_text: A vehicle left unattended on a public road...
answer_text_a: Must have its parking lights switched on if unattended for more than one hour.
answer_text_b: Must be locked.
answer_text_c: Must have its brake set or be secured by another method that effectively prevents it from moving.
correct_answer: C. Must have its brake set or be secured by another method that effectively prevents it from moving.
answer_information_text: Before leaving a vehicle unattended on a public road, set its brake or use another effective way to keep it stationary.

question_text: The minimum required tyre tread depth for a light motor vehicle is...
answer_text_a: 1 mm
answer_text_b: 2 mm.
answer_text_c: 0.5 mm
correct_answer: A. 1 mm
answer_information_text: The required minimum tread depth for a light motor vehicle is 1 mm across the required tread area.

question_text: The minimum required tyre tread depth for light motor vehicles is... mm
answer_information_text: A light motor vehicle must have at least 1 millimetre of tyre tread depth.

question_text: A motor vehicle which is designed for or capable of reaching a speed of... km/h or more, must be equipped with a speedometer which is in good working condition.
answer_information_text: A motor vehicle capable of reaching 60 km/h or more must have a speedometer in good working order.

question_text: If the robot is flashing red, which of the following are appropriate?
answer_text_a: Maintain speed and continue if safe to do so
answer_text_b: Slow down, then continue driving
answer_text_c: Come to a complete stop, take off when safe to do so
correct_answer: C. Come to a complete stop, take off when safe to do so
answer_information_text: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop, followed by proceeding only when it is safe.
answer_text_d: Stop and wait for the green light

question_text: A safe following distance is: / (i) a one-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead of you / (ii) at least a two-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead of you / (iii) a 3 meter gap between you and the vehicle ahead of you
answer_text_a: (i) only is correct
answer_text_b: (iii) only is correct
answer_text_c: (ii) only is correct
correct_answer: C. (ii) only is correct
answer_information_text: The learner-test rule uses a time gap, with at least two seconds as the minimum for light vehicles and motorcycles; a fixed one-second or three-metre gap is not reliable.
answer_text_d: All of the above are correct

question_text: You may use your hooter to:
answer_text_a: Attract a traffic officers attention
answer_text_b: Avoid a collision
answer_text_c: Relieve stress while driving
correct_answer: B. Avoid a collision
answer_information_text: A hooter may be used when necessary for safety, such as to help avoid a collision.
answer_text_d: Attract a vendors attention

question_text: A hooter may be sounded: / (i) to alert the driver ahead that the traffic light has changed to green / (ii) to warn the driver in front he is rolling back into you / (iii) only during the day
answer_text_a: (i) only is correct
answer_text_b: (ii) only is correct
answer_text_c: (iii) only is correct
correct_answer: B. (ii) only is correct
answer_information_text: A hooter may be used when necessary for safety, such as warning a driver whose vehicle is rolling back. It may not be used merely because a light changed or only during the day.
answer_text_d: None of the above are correct

question_text: You may use your hooter of your vehicle...
answer_text_a: To avoid a collision.
answer_text_b: Relieve stress while driving.
answer_text_c: To attract a traffic officer's attention.
correct_answer: A. To avoid a collision.
answer_information_text: A hooter may be used when necessary on safety grounds, such as avoiding a collision. It is not for attracting officials or relieving stress.

question_text: A hooter may be sounded...
answer_text_a: To warn the driver in front if he is rolling back into you.
answer_text_b: To alert the driver ahead that the traffic light has changed to green.
answer_text_c: Only during the day.
correct_answer: A. To warn the driver in front if he is rolling back into you.
answer_information_text: The hooter may be sounded to warn a driver who is rolling back and creating a danger. It is not limited to daytime use and should not be used merely to hurry traffic at a green light.

question_text: On a public road, if no seat equipped with a seat belt is available in a vehicle that has a rear seat, a child aged 3 to 14 years who is no taller than 1.5 m must sit on the rear seat:
answer_text_a: False
answer_text_b: True
answer_text_c: This rule does not apply if the child is sitting on a parent's lap
correct_answer: B. True
answer_information_text: If no seat equipped with a seat belt is available and the vehicle has a rear seat, a child aged 3 to 14 years who is no taller than 1.5 m must sit there. Sitting on a parent's lap does not create an exception.

question_text: When may you drive without a seatbelt?
answer_text_a: If the seatbelts have been damaged.
answer_text_b: When parking or reversing.
answer_text_c: If you are travelling under 20 km/h.
correct_answer: B. When parking or reversing.
answer_information_text: You may be without a seatbelt while reversing or moving into or out of a parking area. Damaged seatbelts and low speed are not general exemptions.

question_text: Wherever a vehicle is stationary on a public road, a reflective red triangle should be displayed...
answer_text_a: Only if you have one in your vehicle.
answer_text_b: True
answer_text_c: False
correct_answer: C. False
answer_information_text: A triangle is generally required when a motor vehicle is stationary on a public road, but the rule has exceptions. The word “wherever” makes the statement false.

question_text: A red triangle should be displayed at least 45 m behind a broken down vehicle.
answer_text_a: False
answer_text_b: True, however this is only required on nationals roads.
answer_text_c: True
correct_answer: C. True
answer_information_text: An emergency warning triangle must be placed not less than 45 m from a broken-down vehicle in the direction from which traffic approaches. This applies on public roads generally, not only national roads.

question_text: Where must you place the emergency triangle if you incur problems with your vehicle on the road?
answer_text_a: 45 M behind the vehicle.
answer_text_b: Next to the vehicle.
answer_text_c: On the roof of the vehicle.
correct_answer: A. 45 M behind the vehicle.
answer_information_text: The triangle must be placed at least 45 m away along the roadway, in the direction from which approaching traffic will come.

question_text: A driver/rider of a vehicle can exceed the speed limit when overtaking/passing another vehicle
answer_text_a: True
answer_text_b: Neither
answer_text_c: False
correct_answer: C. False
answer_information_text: Overtaking does not create an exception to the maximum lawful speed. The driver or rider must remain at or below the applicable speed limit.

question_text: A speed limit of … should apply in respect of every public road situated within an urban area
answer_text_a: 100 kilometres per hour
answer_text_b: 60 kilometres per hour
answer_text_c: 120 kilometres per hour
correct_answer: B. 60 kilometres per hour
answer_information_text: The general speed limit on a public road within an urban area is 60 km/h under regulation 292.

question_text: What does the speed limit mean?
answer_text_a: The fastest speed that you may drive at on a specific road.
answer_text_b: The average speed you should maintain with your vehicle on a specific road.
answer_text_c: The slowest speed that you may drive at on a specific road.
correct_answer: A. The fastest speed that you may drive at on a specific road.
answer_information_text: A speed limit is the maximum lawful speed allowed on that road, subject to any lower posted limit.

question_text: If the overall height of a double-decker bus, including any load, is …, then it is NOT allowed on a public road.
answer_text_a: 4.3 metres
answer_text_b: 4.65 metres
answer_text_c: More than 4.65 metres
correct_answer: C. More than 4.65 metres
answer_information_text: Regulation 224(a) prohibits operating a double-decker bus on a public road if its overall height, including any load, exceeds 4.65 metres.

question_text: The following motor vehicles may NOT be used on a public road if the overall height, together with any load thereon, … / (i) in the case of a double-deck bus. Exceeds 4.65m / (ii) in the case of a goods vehicle, exceeds 4.3m / (iii) in the case of a motorcar (carrying goods on the roof), does not exceed more than half the height of the vehicle
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_text_b: (iii) only is correct
answer_text_c: None of the above are correct
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii) only are correct
answer_information_text: The 4.65-metre double-deck-bus limit and 4.3-metre general limit are correct. Roof goods on a motorcar are prohibited only when they exceed half the car’s height, so (iii) is false.

question_text: Which of the following vehicles are considered as goods vehicles? / (i) Truck-tractor. / (ii) Breakdown vehicle. / (iii) Converter dolly
answer_text_a: (i) Only is correct.
answer_text_b: None of the above are correct.
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: C. All of the above are correct
answer_information_text: The definition of a goods vehicle expressly includes truck-tractors, breakdown vehicles and converter dollies.

question_text: Which of the following are legal with regards to carrying goods? / (i) The goods may not touch the road surface. / (ii) The goods may not block the drivers view. / (iii) The goods may not stand out more than 1.8 m at the rear. / (iv) The goods may not be fragile.
answer_text_a: (i) and (iv) Only are correct.
answer_text_b: (i), (ii) and (iii) Only are correct.
answer_text_c: (i), (iii) and (iv) Only are correct.
correct_answer: B. (i), (ii) and (iii) Only are correct.
answer_information_text: Goods must not touch the road, obstruct the driver's view, or project more than 1.8 m behind the vehicle. Fragile goods are allowed if properly contained, secured, and protected.

question_text: The headlamps, rear lamps and number plate lamps of your motor vehicle need NOT be kept lit between sunset and sunrise when the vehicle is parked:
answer_text_a: On the roadway, solely because its engine is switched off.
answer_text_b: On the roadway, solely because its hazard warning lights are flashing.
answer_text_c: Off the roadway of a public road, in a parking place demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs, or within 12 metres of a lighted street lamp illuminating the public road on which the vehicle is parked.
correct_answer: C. Off the roadway of a public road, in a parking place demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs, or within 12 metres of a lighted street lamp illuminating the public road on which the vehicle is parked.
answer_information_text: These lamps need not remain lit when the vehicle is parked off the roadway, in a parking place demarcated by appropriate road traffic signs, or within 12 metres of a lighted street lamp illuminating the public road where it is parked.

question_text: In which case is it permitted to travel with only the parking lights of your vehicle switched on? / (i) When driving in heavy rain. / (ii) When dusk is falling. / (iii) When driving in snow.
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) are correct.
answer_text_b: (iii) only is correct.
answer_text_c: (ii) only is correct.
correct_answer: D. In none of the above cases
answer_information_text: A vehicle may not be driven with only its parking lamps lit, regardless of rain, dusk, or snow.
answer_text_d: In none of the above cases

question_text: When must a car’s headlamps be kept on while driving on a public road? (i) Throughout daytime, regardless of visibility. (ii) Between sunset and sunrise. (iii) When insufficient light or unfavourable weather makes persons and vehicles on the public road not clearly discernible at 150 metres.
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii)
answer_text_b: (ii) and (iii)
answer_text_c: (ii) only
correct_answer: B. (ii) and (iii)
answer_information_text: A car’s headlamps must be kept on between sunset and sunrise and whenever insufficient light or unfavourable weather prevents persons and vehicles on the public road from being clearly seen at 150 metres.

question_text: What is the maximum distance your parked motor vehicle may be from a lighted street lamp illuminating the public road on which it is parked for the parking-lamp exemption to apply?
answer_text_a: 10 metres.
answer_text_b: 12 metres.
answer_text_c: 6 metres.
correct_answer: B. 12 metres.
answer_information_text: Parking lamps need not be kept lit if the motor vehicle is parked within 12 metres of a lighted street lamp illuminating the public road on which it is parked.

question_text: When should you dip the main beam (bright) of your vehicle. / (i) For oncoming traffic. / (ii) When following another vehicle. / (iii) When you want to see better.
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) Only are correct
answer_text_b: (i), (ii) and (iii)
answer_text_c: (i) Only is correct.
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii) Only are correct
answer_information_text: Dip the main beam for approaching traffic and when following another vehicle, so that it does not cause glare.

question_text: Which lights must you use when driving at night if the main beam could cause dangerous glare to oncoming traffic?
answer_text_a: Main-beam headlights (bright).
answer_text_b: Dipped-beam headlights.
answer_text_c: Parking lamps only.
correct_answer: B. Dipped-beam headlights.
answer_information_text: Use dipped-beam headlights when the main beam could cause dangerous glare to oncoming traffic. Parking lamps alone are insufficient when driving at night.

question_text: Fog lamps may be lit while driving on a public road only in certain conditions. Which of the following qualify? (i) Poor visibility caused by snow, fog or mist. (ii) Poor visibility caused by dust or smoke. (iii) Poor visibility caused by heavy rain alone. (iv) Any time at night if you want to see better.
answer_text_a: (i) only.
answer_text_b: (i) and (ii) only.
answer_text_c: (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv).
correct_answer: B. (i) and (ii) only.
answer_information_text: Fog lamps may be used while driving on a public road only in poor visibility caused by snow, fog, mist, dust or smoke. Heavy rain alone and ordinary night driving do not qualify.

question_text: What is the function of the silencer of the exhaust?
answer_text_a: To increase the sound produced by the exhaust.
answer_text_b: To allow exhaust gases to pass through it while reducing and muffling exhaust noise.
answer_text_c: To cool the engine coolant.
correct_answer: B. To allow exhaust gases to pass through it while reducing and muffling exhaust noise.
answer_information_text: Regulation 209(a) requires exhaust gases to pass through an efficient silencer or muffling device that effectively reduces and muffles exhaust noise.

question_text: When driving an ordinary (non-emergency) vehicle, you are allowed to park in emergency vehicle parking bays:
answer_text_a: On weekends
answer_text_b: On public holidays
answer_text_c: This is never allowed
correct_answer: C. This is never allowed
answer_information_text: An emergency-vehicle bay is reserved for authorized emergency vehicles. Weekends and public holidays do not make ordinary parking lawful.
answer_text_d: At night only

question_text: Unless permitted by an appropriate road traffic sign, you may NOT park your vehicle on the left-hand side of a roadway with the outside of any left-hand wheel thereof more than … within the roadway
answer_text_a: 300mm
answer_text_b: 450mm
answer_text_c: 550mm
correct_answer: B. 450mm
answer_information_text: The outside of the left-hand wheel may not be more than 450 mm into the roadway unless an appropriate sign permits it.

question_text: Within an urban area, no person shall park a vehicle on the roadway of a public road which is less than... wide, unless the road concerned is restricted to traffic moving in one direction and such parking is permitted by an appropriate traffic sign.
answer_text_a: 10 meters.
answer_text_b: 5.5 meters
answer_text_c: 9 meters.
correct_answer: B. 5.5 meters
answer_information_text: Regulation 305 prohibits parking on an urban public road that is less than 5.5 metres wide, unless it is one-way and parking is permitted by an appropriate sign.

question_text: Which vehicle is parked illegally?
answer_text_a: A vehicle parked in a designated parking bay where parking is permitted.
answer_text_b: A vehicle parked on the roadway of a two-way public road in an urban area where the roadway is 4 m wide.
answer_text_c: A vehicle parked near a fire hydrant, entirely outside the restricted area extending 1.5 m on either side of it, where parking is otherwise permitted.
correct_answer: B. A vehicle parked on the roadway of a two-way public road in an urban area where the roadway is 4 m wide.
answer_information_text: Parking on the roadway of a two-way public road in an urban area is prohibited if the roadway is less than 5.5 m wide. The hydrant restriction applies on the hydrant’s side of the road within 1.5 m on either side when the hydrant is clearly visible and recognisable to drivers of moving vehicles or indicated by an appropriate road traffic sign.

question_text: For ordinary parking on a public road, which of the following are NOT legal parking spots? (i) On the right-hand side of the roadway of a two-way road, facing oncoming traffic. (ii) Anywhere your vehicle would obscure a road traffic sign. (iii) In a bay reserved by signs for emergency or public transport vehicles when your vehicle is not authorised to use it.
answer_text_a: (i) and (iii) only.
answer_text_b: (i) and (ii) only.
answer_text_c: All of the above.
correct_answer: C. All of the above.
answer_information_text: Ordinary parking is prohibited on the right-hand side facing oncoming traffic and wherever the vehicle would obscure a road traffic sign. You may not park in a reserved bay unless your vehicle is authorised to use it.

question_text: You may NOT park your vehicle alongside or opposite any other vehicle on a road where such roadway is less than... wide.
answer_text_a: 6 m
answer_text_c: 9 m
correct_answer: C. 9 m
answer_information_text: Parking alongside or opposite another vehicle is prohibited when the roadway is less than 9 metres wide.

question_text: You may use a mobile phone while driving on a public road:
answer_text_a: If it remains affixed to the vehicle or is used through specially designed or adapted headgear that remains attached to your ear, without holding the phone in either hand or with any other part of your body.
answer_text_b: If you hold it in your hand while stationary at an intersection.
answer_text_c: If it lies loose on the passenger seat and you use its loudspeaker without holding it.
correct_answer: A. If it remains affixed to the vehicle or is used through specially designed or adapted headgear that remains attached to your ear, without holding the phone in either hand or with any other part of your body.
answer_information_text: The phone must remain affixed to the vehicle or be used through specially designed or adapted headgear, without being held in a hand or with another part of the body. Being stationary at an intersection does not permit handheld use.

question_text: You must give way to pedestrians:
answer_text_a: Who are crossing within a pedestrian crossing without traffic signals and are on your half of the roadway, or approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger.
answer_text_b: Who need to cross a freeway, because that need gives them right of way.
answer_text_c: Who are crossing within a pedestrian crossing without traffic signals, but only once they have reached your half of the roadway.
correct_answer: A. Who are crossing within a pedestrian crossing without traffic signals and are on your half of the roadway, or approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger.
answer_information_text: At a pedestrian crossing without traffic signals, you must slow down or stop if necessary to yield to pedestrians crossing on your half of the roadway or approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger. Needing to cross a freeway does not give pedestrians right of way.

question_text: When must you give way to pedestrians?
answer_text_a: Pedestrian crossing.
answer_text_b: Freeway.
answer_text_c: Railway crossing.
correct_answer: A. Pedestrian crossing.
answer_information_text: Drivers must give way to pedestrians crossing at a designated pedestrian crossing.

question_text: When do you have the right of way?
answer_text_a: When you are the first to stop at a 4-way stop, or are already within a traffic circle
answer_text_b: When you want to turn right at an intersection in a two-way road
answer_text_c: When you are entering a traffic circle
correct_answer: A. When you are the first to stop at a 4-way stop, or are already within a traffic circle
answer_information_text: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that stopped first proceeds first; vehicles already in a traffic circle have priority. Turning right at an ordinary two-way intersection does not automatically give priority.
answer_text_d: Whenever you are on the wider of two roads

question_text: Within an urban area, a vehicle left continuously in the same place on a public road is deemed abandoned after more than ....
answer_text_a: 3 days
answer_text_b: 7 days
answer_text_c: 4 days
correct_answer: B. 7 days
answer_information_text: The vehicle is deemed abandoned once it has remained there continuously for longer than seven days. Other stopping and parking restrictions may apply before then.

question_text: You should never drive a light motor vehicle on a public road if...
answer_text_a: It is fitted with lamps that produce an amber light to rear.
answer_text_b: It is not fitted with lamps at the rear, emitting a red light to the rear.
answer_text_c: It does not have orange lamps at the rear of the vehicle.
correct_answer: B. It is not fitted with lamps at the rear, emitting a red light to the rear.
answer_information_text: A light motor vehicle must have rear lamps that emit red light to the rear. Amber light may be used for permitted indicators, but it does not replace the required red rear lamps.

question_text: What should you never do on a public road?
answer_text_a: Drive at a speed appropriate for the conditions and within the applicable speed limit.
answer_text_b: Give an authorised hand signal to indicate your intention to turn.
answer_text_c: Cause or allow your vehicle's engine to produce smoke or fumes beyond those it would produce in good condition while running efficiently.
correct_answer: C. Cause or allow your vehicle's engine to produce smoke or fumes beyond those it would produce in good condition while running efficiently.
answer_information_text: On a public road, you must not cause or allow an engine to produce smoke or fumes that it would not produce in good condition while running efficiently.

question_text: What is the general rule of the road in South Africa?
answer_text_a: Always drive at 60 km/h.
answer_text_b: As a general rule, drive on the left side of the roadway.
answer_text_c: You may only obtain a driving licence at the age of 21 years.
correct_answer: B. As a general rule, drive on the left side of the roadway.
answer_information_text: Vehicles generally travel on the left side of the roadway. The law permits specified exceptions, and this requirement does not apply to one-way roads.

question_text: Under regulation 221(f), what is the maximum permitted overall length, including any drawbar or coupling, of a vehicle not covered by the other length categories in regulation 221, excluding a semi-trailer?
answer_text_a: 20 metres
answer_text_b: 12.5 metres
answer_text_c: 14 metres
correct_answer: B. 12.5 metres
answer_information_text: Vehicles in this remaining category may not exceed an overall length of 12.5 metres, including any drawbar or coupling. Semi-trailers are excluded from this category.

question_text: What is the minimum enclosure height above the surface on which a person is seated when carried in a goods vehicle?
answer_text_a: 350 millimetres
answer_text_b: 900 millimetres
answer_text_c: 200 millimetres
correct_answer: A. 350 millimetres
answer_information_text: The enclosure must extend at least 350 millimetres above the surface on which the person is seated.

question_text: If you are driving towards the mini-circle in the sketch, and there are also vehicles from the other three sides, you...
answer_text_a: Must always wait for the vehicle from your right before you drive on.
answer_text_b: Must stop with all the vehicles and only drive on when it is safe.
answer_text_c: May drive on if you were the first vehicle over the line.
correct_answer: C. May drive on if you were the first vehicle over the line.
answer_information_text: At a mini-circle, the vehicle that crosses its yield line first has priority, provided it is safe to proceed. The vehicle that arrives later must yield.

question_text: Which of the following vehicles may be used on a freeway?
answer_text_a: A vehicle with a mass not exceeding 230 kg, designed for the use of a person suffering from a physical disability.
answer_text_b: A motorcycle with an engine capacity of 125 cc.
answer_text_c: A pedal cycle.
correct_answer: B. A motorcycle with an engine capacity of 125 cc.
answer_information_text: The freeway prohibition applies to motorcycles not exceeding 50cc, so a 125cc motorcycle may be used. Pedal cycles and the specified lightweight disability vehicle may not use a freeway.

question_text: When transporting goods on a vehicle on a public road, which of the following statements are/is true? / (i) Goods may be loaded onto a vehicle in such a manner that it obstructs the driver's/ rider's view in the rearview mirrors of traffic to the rear, as long as the vehicle has red flags tied to all the corners of such load. / (ii) Goods may be transported on the roof of a motorcar if the height of such goods, measured from the highest point of such roof, does not exceed one half of the height of the motor vehicle, measured from ground level. / (iii) When a pedal cycle is being transported on a motorcar's roof, the rule in ii is not applicable.
answer_text_a: (ii) and (iii) Only are correct.
answer_text_b: All of the above are correct.
answer_text_c: None of the above is correct.
correct_answer: A. (ii) and (iii) Only are correct.
answer_information_text: Goods carried on a motorcar’s roof may not extend above the roof by more than half the car’s height measured from ground level, but this height restriction does not apply to pedal cycles. Loads must not obstruct the driver’s view of rear traffic in the mirrors, even if red flags are attached.

question_text: The fastest speed at which you may tow another vehicle with a rope is:
answer_text_a: 60 km/h
answer_text_b: 30 km/h
answer_text_c: 40 km/h
correct_answer: B. 30 km/h
answer_information_text: Regulation 330 of the National Road Traffic Regulations limits towing with a rope to 30 km/h on a public road.
answer_text_d: 20 km/h

question_text: If you are towing a vehicle with faulty brakes, you should:
answer_text_a: Keep a maximum speed of 45 km/h
answer_text_b: Not carry more than 1 passenger in the towed vehicle
answer_text_c: Use a wire with a length not exceeding 3m
correct_answer: D. Only use a tow bar to tow the vehicle
answer_information_text: Regulation 330(d) requires a drawbar or tow bar when the towed vehicle has faulty brakes. This rigid connection prevents it from running into the towing vehicle when slowing down.
answer_text_d: Only use a tow bar to tow the vehicle

question_text: What is legal with regard to the towing of another vehicle? / (i) You may tow it with a 750cc motorcycle. / (ii) You may tow it with a tricycle. / (iii) You may not tow it with any motorcycle.
answer_text_a: (iii) only is correct.
answer_text_b: (i) only is correct.
answer_text_c: (ii) only is correct.
correct_answer: A. (iii) only is correct.
answer_information_text: You may not tow another vehicle on a public road using a motorcycle, regardless of its engine size. Motor tricycles are also prohibited from towing another vehicle.
answer_text_d: All of the above are correct

question_text: Unless otherwise shown by a sign, the general speed limit in a town/city is...km/h / (i) 60. / (ii) 80. / (iii) 100.
answer_text_a: (i) is correct.
answer_text_b: (iii) is correct.
answer_text_c: (ii)is correct.
correct_answer: A. (i) is correct.
answer_information_text: The general speed limit on roads in a town or city is 60 km/h, unless a road sign shows a different limit. This is prescribed by regulation 292 of the National Road Traffic Regulations.
answer_text_d: None of the above are correct

question_text: You may tow a vehicle with damaged brakes: / (i) never / (ii) with a tow-bar / (iii) with its engine switched on
answer_text_a: (ii) only is correct
answer_text_b: (iii) only is correct
answer_text_c: (i) only is correct
correct_answer: A. (ii) only is correct
answer_information_text: A vehicle with damaged brakes may be towed using a rigid tow-bar or drawbar, as required by Regulation 330. Switching on the engine does not remove this requirement.
answer_text_d: All of the above are correct

question_text: The fastest speed at which you may tow a vehicle with a rope is...km/h / (i) 60. / (ii) 45. / (iii) 30.
answer_text_a: (i) only is correct.
answer_text_b: (ii) only is correct.
answer_text_c: (iii) only is correct
correct_answer: C. (iii) only is correct
answer_information_text: Regulation 330 of the National Road Traffic Regulations limits towing with a rope on a public road to 30 km/h.
answer_text_d: None of the above are correct

question_text: A rider can use a motorcycle to tow another vehicle?
answer_text_a: False.
answer_text_b: Neither.
answer_text_c: True.
correct_answer: A. False.
answer_information_text: A motorcycle may not be used to tow another vehicle on a public road. The road traffic regulations prohibit this.

question_text: How should you tow a vehicle with damaged brakes?
answer_text_a: With its engine switched on
answer_text_b: With a tow-bar.
answer_text_c: You should never tow a vehicle with no brakes.
correct_answer: B. With a tow-bar.
answer_information_text: Regulation 330 requires a vehicle with defective brakes to be connected to the towing vehicle by a drawbar or tow-bar. This rigid connection prevents the towed vehicle from rolling into the towing vehicle when it slows down.

question_text: The maximum distance between two vehicles which are being towed is?
answer_information_text: The tow rope, chain or tow bar between the towing vehicle and the vehicle being towed may not exceed 3.5 m in length, as required by Regulation 330.

question_text: Unless otherwise shown by a sign, the general speed limit in a town or city is?
answer_text_b: 100 km/h
answer_text_c: 60 km/h.
correct_answer: C. 60 km/h.
answer_information_text: The general speed limit on public roads in a town or city is 60 km/h, unless a road sign indicates a different limit.

question_text: If your vehicle is involved in an accident you must / (i) Immediately stop your vehicle / (ii) Ascertain the nature and extent of any injuries / (iii) Drink a bit to calm your nerves down
answer_text_b: (iii) only
answer_text_c: (i), (ii), (iii)
correct_answer: A. (i), (ii)
answer_information_text: You must stop immediately and check whether anyone is injured and how serious their injuries are. Drinking alcohol to calm your nerves is not a duty after an accident and is restricted by law.

question_text: If a person has been killed or injured in an accident and such accident causes a complete obstruction on a roadway, no vehicle may be moved from the position from where it came to rest unless
answer_text_a: A certified tow-truck arrives on the scene and removes such vehicle(s) from the roadway
answer_text_b: The driver authorised such removal
answer_text_c: Its position has been clearly marked on the road surface by the person moving the vehicle, or such removal has been authorized by a traffic officer
correct_answer: C. Its position has been clearly marked on the road surface by the person moving the vehicle, or such removal has been authorized by a traffic officer
answer_information_text: After an accident in which someone is killed or injured, a vehicle may be moved if a traffic officer authorises it. If the roadway is completely blocked, the person moving the vehicle must first clearly mark its position on the road surface, then move it only far enough to let traffic pass.

question_text: The procedure following an accident is... / (i) to immediately stop your vehicle. / (ii) to inspect to determine if anyone is injured. / (iii) to drive off if you are uninsured.
answer_text_a: (i) and (ii) Only are correct.
answer_text_b: (i) Only is correct.
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct.
correct_answer: A. (i) and (ii) Only are correct.
answer_information_text: After an accident, you must stop immediately and check whether anyone is injured and how seriously. Being uninsured does not allow you to drive off without carrying out your duties.

question_text: A towed vehicle carrying no persons may NOT travel faster than 30 km/h on a public road unless...
answer_text_a: The vehicles are connected by a tow-rope no longer than 3.5 metres.
answer_text_b: The vehicles are connected by a drawbar or tow-bar.
answer_text_c: The towed vehicle's tail lights are working.
correct_answer: B. The vehicles are connected by a drawbar or tow-bar.
answer_information_text: Regulation 330(e) permits towing above 30 km/h only when the vehicles are connected by a drawbar or tow-bar. A tow-rope or working tail lights do not allow a higher towing speed.

question_text: Assuming all other legal requirements are met, you may tow another vehicle on a public road at a speed exceeding 30 km/h if …
answer_text_a: The vehicles are connected by a drawbar or tow-bar
answer_text_b: The vehicles are connected by a chain
answer_text_c: The vehicles are connected by a tow-rope
correct_answer: A. The vehicles are connected by a drawbar or tow-bar
answer_information_text: Regulation 330 allows towing above 30 km/h only when the vehicles are connected by a drawbar or tow-bar, provided all other legal requirements are met. Towing with a rope or chain is limited to 30 km/h.

question_text: An accident causes property damage but no death or injury, and you have not already reported it to a police or traffic officer at the scene. When must you report it?
answer_text_a: As soon as reasonably practicable, and no later than the first working day after the accident.
answer_text_b: Immediately, by summoning the police to the scene.
answer_text_c: Within two weeks after the accident.
correct_answer: A. As soon as reasonably practicable, and no later than the first working day after the accident.
answer_information_text: When an accident causes property damage but no death or injury, you must report it as soon as reasonably practicable, and no later than the first working day after the accident, unless you already reported it to a police or traffic officer at the scene.

question_text: Which statement correctly describes your legal duty to assist someone injured in an accident you are involved in as a driver?
answer_text_a: You must wait for the police before giving any assistance.
answer_text_b: You must render such assistance to the injured person as you are capable of rendering.
answer_text_c: You must assist the injured person only if you caused the accident.
correct_answer: B. You must render such assistance to the injured person as you are capable of rendering.
answer_information_text: If you are involved in an accident as a driver, you must give an injured person whatever assistance you are capable of providing. This duty applies regardless of who caused the accident and does not depend on the police arriving.

question_text: If your motor vehicle is in motion on a public road . . .
answer_text_a: You may drive with only your parking lamps lighted if the road has street lighting.
answer_text_b: You may drive with only your parking lamps lighted during daylight.
answer_text_c: You may not drive with only your parking lamps lighted.
correct_answer: C. You may not drive with only your parking lamps lighted.
answer_information_text: Regulation 165(2) prohibits driving a motor vehicle on a public road with only its parking lamps lighted while it is moving. This applies during daylight and on roads with street lighting.

question_text: You may not reverse your vehicle on a public road further than...
answer_text_c: Is necessary for the safety or reasonable convenience of any occupant of the vehicle or other traffic, and reversing must be safe.
correct_answer: C. Is necessary for the safety or reasonable convenience of any occupant of the vehicle or other traffic, and reversing must be safe.
answer_information_text: You may reverse on a public road only when it is safe, and only as far or as long as necessary for the safety or reasonable convenience of anyone in the vehicle or other traffic. There is no fixed distance limit in metres.

question_text: Except where a lawful exception applies, where is stopping your vehicle on the roadway of a public road prohibited?
answer_text_a: Alongside or opposite an excavation or obstruction on the public road, if stopping would obstruct or endanger other traffic.
answer_text_b: In any area without street lights.
answer_text_c: Wherever traffic officers are present.
correct_answer: A. Alongside or opposite an excavation or obstruction on the public road, if stopping would obstruct or endanger other traffic.
answer_information_text: Regulation 304(a) prohibits stopping on the roadway alongside or opposite an excavation or obstruction if doing so would block or endanger other traffic, unless a lawful exception applies.

question_text: Which statements correctly describe vehicles prohibited on a public road under the overall-width limits? (i) Any vehicle with an overall width exceeding 2.5 metres. (ii) A bus whose front-wheel tyre centre-lines are more than 1.9 metres apart, if its overall width exceeds 2.6 metres. (iii) A goods vehicle with a gross vehicle mass of 12 000 kg or more, if its overall width exceeds 2.6 metres.
answer_text_a: Statement (iii) only.
answer_text_b: Statements (ii) and (iii) only.
answer_text_c: All of the above.
correct_answer: B. Statements (ii) and (iii) only.
answer_information_text: Buses with front-wheel tyre centre-lines more than 1.9 metres apart and goods vehicles with a gross vehicle mass of at least 12 000 kg are prohibited if their overall width exceeds 2.6 metres. The 2.5-metre limit applies to other vehicles, so it does not prohibit every vehicle wider than 2.5 metres.

question_text: When you want to change lanes and drive from L1 to L2 in the picture you must. . . . (i) Only do it when it is safe to do so.(ii) Switch your indicators on in time to show what you are going to do.(iii) Use the mirror(s) of your vehicle to ensure that you know of other traffic.
answer_text_a: Only (ii) and (iii) are correct
answer_text_b: Only (i) and (ii) are correct
answer_text_c: All of the above are correct
correct_answer: C. All of the above are correct
answer_information_text: Before moving from L1 to L2, check your mirrors and blind spot for other traffic, and signal in good time to show your intention. Change lanes only when it is safe to do so. Road Signs and Markings

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: You must move onto the left lane
answer_text_b: A red bus to the right
answer_text_c: The road to the right ends
correct_answer: C. The road to the right ends
answer_information_text: This warning means that the road to the right ends. It alerts you to a change in the road layout, so reduce speed, keep a proper lookout and be ready to follow the continuing roadway safely.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is an exit 300 metres ahead
answer_text_b: There is an exit 200 metres ahead
answer_text_c: There is an exit 100 metres ahead
correct_answer: A. There is an exit 300 metres ahead
answer_information_text: This sign shows an exit 300 metres ahead. The distance shown on an advance direction sign tells you how far away the exit is, so you can prepare early and move into the correct lane safely.

question_text: What does this road marking mean?
answer_text_a: You can only stop here on weekends
answer_text_b: You are allowed to park here
answer_text_c: You are not allowed to park here
correct_answer: B. You are allowed to park here
answer_information_text: This road marking indicates that parking is permitted at that location, subject to the usual parking rules and any nearby signs. You must still park safely, without obstructing traffic or access.

question_text: Which vehicle is not allowed past this marking?
answer_text_a: Motorcycles
answer_text_b: Sedans
answer_text_c: SUV
correct_answer: A. Motorcycles
answer_information_text: A vehicle restriction marking applies to the vehicle type shown by the road symbol, so motorcycles must not proceed past it. The restriction is enforced by the marking at that point, not by the size or body style of the vehicle.

question_text: Which type of vehicles is this lane reserved for?
answer_text_a: High-occupancy vehicles
answer_text_b: Vehicles carrying hazardous goods only.
answer_text_c: Motorcycles only.
correct_answer: A. High-occupancy vehicles
answer_information_text: The yellow diamond marking indicates a lane reserved for high-occupancy vehicles. Vehicles using the lane must meet the occupancy requirement indicated on the accompanying sign.

question_text: Are you allowed to stop on this yellow box to park?
answer_text_a: Yes
answer_text_b: Only on weekends
answer_text_c: No
correct_answer: C. No
answer_information_text: A yellow box marking must be kept clear because stopping or parking on it can obstruct traffic and junction movements. You may enter it only when the road ahead is clear enough for you to leave it without causing an obstruction.

question_text: What are you supposed to do when you see this marking?
answer_text_a: Yield and give way to other vehicles
answer_text_b: Come to a complete stop if there are no other vehicles around
answer_text_c: Increase your speed
correct_answer: A. Yield and give way to other vehicles
answer_information_text: The marking requires you to yield and give way to other vehicles before proceeding. Reduce speed, check the traffic you must yield to, and continue only when it is safe.

question_text: What type of vehicles are allowed to park here?
answer_text_a: All vehicles are allowed here
answer_text_b: Ambulances only
answer_text_c: Agricultural vehicles
correct_answer: B. Ambulances only
answer_information_text: Parking in this area is reserved for ambulances. Other vehicles, including agricultural vehicles, may not use the reserved parking space.

question_text: What type of vehicles are allowed to park here?
answer_text_a: Perimeter vehicles
answer_text_b: Purple vehicles
answer_text_c: Police vehicles only
correct_answer: C. Police vehicles only
answer_information_text: The parking restriction is reserved for police vehicles, so ordinary vehicles may not park there. A vehicle’s colour or its intended use does not create an exception unless it is an authorised police vehicle.

question_text: Under which circumstances are you allowed to cross this line?
answer_text_a: When overtaking a slow-moving vehicle
answer_text_b: Whenever no oncoming traffic is visible
answer_text_c: Only to pass a stationary obstruction or to enter or leave property on the other side of the road, when it is safe
correct_answer: C. Only to pass a stationary obstruction or to enter or leave property on the other side of the road, when it is safe
answer_information_text: You may cross this line only when safely passing a stationary obstruction or gaining direct access to land on the opposite side. It may not be crossed to overtake a moving vehicle.

question_text: What should you do when you see this road marking?
answer_text_a: Continue driving as you have the right of way
answer_text_b: Give way to pedestrians
answer_text_c: Only allow buses to pass
correct_answer: B. Give way to pedestrians
answer_information_text: This road marking requires you to give way to pedestrians who are crossing or about to cross. Slow down and stop if necessary, allowing them to cross safely before continuing.

question_text: What does this sign prohibit?
answer_text_a: It prohibits you from using your headlights
answer_text_b: It prohibits you from parking in that area
answer_text_c: It prohibits you from using your hooter in this area
correct_answer: C. It prohibits you from using your hooter in this area
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits hooting in the area. Do not use the hooter unless it is necessary to warn another road user of an immediate danger, even when this sign is displayed.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: A crossroad
answer_text_b: An airport
answer_text_c: A church
correct_answer: A. A crossroad
answer_information_text: This warning sign indicates a crossroad ahead, where traffic may enter or cross your path from either side. Slow down, keep a good lookout and be ready to stop or give way as required.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You must turn on your high beams in this area
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to park in this area
answer_text_c: You must speed up in this area
correct_answer: B. You are not allowed to park in this area
answer_information_text: This sign means that parking is prohibited in the area. You may not leave the vehicle parked there, so stop only when permitted and do not obstruct traffic.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a dealership ahead
answer_text_b: There is a parking lot ahead
answer_text_c: There is a tunnel ahead
correct_answer: C. There is a tunnel ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign indicates a tunnel ahead. Reduce speed, switch on the required lights, keep a safe following distance and do not stop inside the tunnel unless necessary.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You are approaching a two or more track railway level crossing
answer_text_b: There is a gate ahead
answer_text_c: There is a stop ahead
correct_answer: A. You are approaching a two or more track railway level crossing
answer_information_text: This sign warns that you are approaching a railway level crossing with two or more tracks. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and cross only when it is safe and the crossing is clear.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a yield sign ahead
answer_text_b: There is an arrestor bed lane ahead
answer_text_c: There is a flag ahead
correct_answer: B. There is an arrestor bed lane ahead
answer_information_text: This sign warns of an arrestor bed lane ahead. It provides an escape route for a vehicle that cannot stop safely, especially on a steep downhill section, so never enter it unless you need to use it.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a stop sign ahead
answer_text_b: There is a reservoir ahead
answer_text_c: There is a police block beyond this sign
correct_answer: C. There is a police block beyond this sign
answer_information_text: This sign indicates that a police block is beyond the sign. Slow down, obey the instructions of the traffic or police officials and be prepared to stop for inspection.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Indicate the minimum speed limit in the lane
answer_text_b: You must drive on the right lane
answer_text_c: Indicate the maximum speed limit
correct_answer: A. Indicate the minimum speed limit in the lane
answer_information_text: This sign indicates the minimum speed that must be maintained in the lane. It does not set the maximum speed, so you must still obey the applicable maximum speed limit and drive at a safe speed for the conditions.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: This lane is reserved for buses and midibuses only
answer_text_b: Buses and midibuses may not use this lane
answer_text_c: A bus terminus is ahead
correct_answer: A. This lane is reserved for buses and midibuses only
answer_information_text: A reservation sign (marked R) shows which vehicles may use the lane or area; here only buses and midibuses may use it.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You must have 12 passengers
answer_text_b: Only 12 vehicles are allowed here
answer_text_c: If the mass of your vehicle exceeds 12 tons you are not allowed past this point
correct_answer: C. If the mass of your vehicle exceeds 12 tons you are not allowed past this point
answer_information_text: A mass-limit sign applies to the vehicle’s gross vehicle mass, not to the number of passengers or vehicles. A vehicle whose mass exceeds 12 tons may not pass the sign unless an exemption or supplementary sign applies.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You have to yield to pedestrians
answer_text_b: You must stop at the traffic light ahead
answer_text_c: You have to yield to horses
correct_answer: A. You have to yield to pedestrians
answer_information_text: This sign gives priority to pedestrians at the crossing or area indicated. Slow down, watch carefully and yield so pedestrians can cross safely; it is not a horse warning or an instruction to stop at a traffic light.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a beach ahead
answer_text_b: There is a drift ahead that may contain water or debris
answer_text_c: There is a pool ahead
correct_answer: B. There is a drift ahead that may contain water or debris
answer_information_text: A drift warning sign indicates a low section of road where water, mud, stones or other debris may lie across the roadway. Reduce speed and cross only when it is safe, because the depth and surface condition can change.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a right turn ahead
answer_text_b: There is a left turn ahead
answer_text_c: It indicates the converging of traffic lanes
correct_answer: C. It indicates the converging of traffic lanes
answer_information_text: This warning sign shows that traffic lanes join or converge ahead. Adjust your speed and position, keep a proper following distance and give way where required by the lane markings or other signs.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: A skew junction ahead with traffic potentially entering from the left.
answer_text_b: The roadway narrows from the left ahead.
answer_text_c: The roadway comes to an end ahead.
correct_answer: A. A skew junction ahead with traffic potentially entering from the left.
answer_information_text: This sign warns of a skew junction where traffic may enter from the left. Reduce speed and be prepared for other traffic.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: This is a no towing zone
answer_text_b: You must pay toll fees
answer_text_c: You must be towing a vehicle in this lane
correct_answer: B. You must pay toll fees
answer_information_text: A toll-road sign indicates that you must pay a toll to use the road or facility beyond the sign. Follow the lane and payment instructions at the toll plaza; the sign does not relate to towing.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only 10-ton vehicles are allowed here
answer_text_b: There is a parking lot ahead
answer_text_c: The parking area is reserved for dangerous goods vehicles
correct_answer: C. The parking area is reserved for dangerous goods vehicles
answer_information_text: This sign means that the parking area is reserved for dangerous goods vehicles. It does not mean that every vehicle of a particular mass may park there; the restriction is based on the vehicle's dangerous-goods designation.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a staggered junction ahead
answer_text_b: There is a parking lot ahead
answer_text_c: There is a broken ladder ahead
correct_answer: A. There is a staggered junction ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign shows that a staggered junction is ahead, with the side roads offset from each other. Slow down, observe carefully for traffic from both sides, and proceed when it is safe.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Trucks are not allowed here
answer_text_b: A goods vehicle may not overtake another goods vehicle for the next 500 metres
answer_text_c: You are not allowed to race a truck
correct_answer: B. A goods vehicle may not overtake another goods vehicle for the next 500 metres
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits a goods vehicle from overtaking another goods vehicle for the next 500 metres. It does not ban all trucks or refer to racing; the restriction is specifically on overtaking between goods vehicles.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: If a vehicle is carrying 15 passengers it is not allowed on this read
answer_text_b: 15-ton vehicles are not allowed on this road
answer_text_c: If the length of a vehicle exceeds the length on the sign it is not allowed beyond this point
correct_answer: C. If the length of a vehicle exceeds the length on the sign it is not allowed beyond this point
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits vehicles whose overall length exceeds the length shown on the sign. It is a length restriction, not a restriction based on vehicle mass or the number of passengers carried.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Dangerous goods vehicles are prohibited from using this road
answer_text_b: Black trucks are not allowed here
answer_text_c: 2-ton vehicles are not allowed on this road
correct_answer: A. Dangerous goods vehicles are prohibited from using this road
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits vehicles transporting dangerous goods from using the road beyond the sign. Such vehicles must take another permitted route, even if they comply with other size and mass limits.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: No pedestrians are allowed ahead
answer_text_b: Goods vehicles are prohibited beyond this point
answer_text_c: Only trucks are allowed ahead
correct_answer: B. Goods vehicles are prohibited beyond this point
answer_information_text: The enclosed box truck in a red circle with a slash is the 'no goods vehicles' sign: goods vehicles may not proceed beyond it. The 'no delivery vehicles' sign shows a light truck with an open load bed carrying goods.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a parking spot to the right
answer_text_b: There is a dead end to the left
answer_text_c: There is a dead end to the right
correct_answer: C. There is a dead end to the right
answer_information_text: This sign shows that the road to the right is a dead end and has no through route. You may enter it if your destination is there, but it cannot be used to continue through to another road.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only bicycles may ride here
answer_text_b: Bicycles may not ride here
answer_text_c: Motorbikes may ride here
correct_answer: A. Only bicycles may ride here
answer_information_text: This sign designates a facility for bicycles. Bicycles may use it, while motorbikes and other motor vehicles must keep off it unless another sign specifically allows them.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: Slow-moving heavy goods vehicles ahead on a downhill section
answer_text_b: An accident ahead
answer_text_c: Heavy goods vehicles crossing the road ahead
correct_answer: A. Slow-moving heavy goods vehicles ahead on a downhill section
answer_information_text: This sign warns that heavy goods vehicles may be travelling very slowly in a low gear on a steep downhill section ahead.

question_text: What does this sign forbid you from doing?
answer_text_a: Driving under 100 km/h at night
answer_text_b: Driving at night
answer_text_c: Driving above 100 km/h at night
correct_answer: C. Driving above 100 km/h at night
answer_information_text: This sign sets a maximum speed of 100 km/h during the time shown, so you must not drive faster than 100 km/h at night. It does not prohibit night driving; it restricts the speed at which you may drive.

question_text: What does this sign forbid you from doing?
answer_text_a: Driving a motorcar beyond this sign at any time of day.
answer_text_b: Parking a motorcar here between 06:30 and 09:00.
answer_text_c: Driving a motorcar beyond this sign between 06:30 and 09:00.
correct_answer: C. Driving a motorcar beyond this sign between 06:30 and 09:00.
answer_information_text: Motorcars may not proceed beyond this sign between 06:30 and 09:00. The time plate limits the prohibition to those hours.

question_text: What does this road marking indicate?
answer_text_a: Only automatic vehicles may park here
answer_text_b: This spot is available for ambulances only
answer_text_c: This spot is available for tow trucks only
correct_answer: B. This spot is available for ambulances only
answer_information_text: This road marking reserves the parking space for ambulances only. Tow trucks and other vehicles may not park there simply because the space is available.

question_text: What does this road marking indicate?
answer_text_a: You are allowed to ride your bike in this lane
answer_text_b: Buses are not allowed on this section of the road
answer_text_c: Only buses are allowed on this section of the road
correct_answer: C. Only buses are allowed on this section of the road
answer_information_text: This road marking reserves the section of road for buses. Other vehicles, including bicycles, may not use this bus-only section unless an authorised exception applies.

question_text: What does this sign warn of?
answer_text_a: A driveway joining the road ahead.
answer_text_b: An urban area ahead.
answer_text_c: A gate or boom across the road ahead.
correct_answer: C. A gate or boom across the road ahead.
answer_information_text: This sign warns that a gate may close the road ahead. It also warns of gates, booms or barriers at a railway crossing.

question_text: What does the solid white centre line in this picture mean?
answer_text_a: You must not cross the line or drive on its right-hand side to overtake a moving motor vehicle.
answer_text_b: You may cross the line to overtake whenever no traffic is approaching.
answer_text_c: You must not overtake any vehicle, even while staying entirely to the left of the line.
correct_answer: A. You must not cross the line or drive on its right-hand side to overtake a moving motor vehicle.
answer_information_text: This is a no-overtaking line: you must not cross it or drive on its right-hand side to overtake a moving motor vehicle. Overtaking that stays entirely on the permitted side is allowed if it is otherwise safe and lawful.

question_text: What does this sign instruct you to do?
answer_text_a: Proceed through the narrow section because you have priority over oncoming traffic.
answer_text_b: Proceed straight ahead because the road is one-way.
answer_text_c: Yield to oncoming traffic at the narrow or obstructed section; proceed only when you can do so without endangering that traffic or forcing it to stop.
correct_answer: C. Yield to oncoming traffic at the narrow or obstructed section; proceed only when you can do so without endangering that traffic or forcing it to stop.
answer_information_text: This sign requires you to give way to oncoming traffic at a narrow or obstructed section. Stop if necessary and proceed only when you can pass without endangering that traffic or forcing it to stop.

question_text: Where do you find this sign?
answer_text_a: Between an off-ramp and the continuing freeway
answer_text_b: On a rural road
answer_text_c: On an urban road
correct_answer: A. Between an off-ramp and the continuing freeway
answer_information_text: This sign is found at the gore between an off-ramp and the continuing freeway. It marks the point where the routes separate, so follow the lane markings and pass on the correct side for the route you intend to take.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: An ambulance ahead
answer_text_b: A yield sign ahead
answer_text_c: A speed-up sign ahead
correct_answer: B. A yield sign ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign shows that a yield sign is ahead. Slow down, look for the yield control and be prepared to give way or stop before entering the intersecting road.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: A pool ahead
answer_text_b: A beach
answer_text_c: The road ends due to water ahead
correct_answer: C. The road ends due to water ahead
answer_information_text: Water blocks the road beyond the sign, so the road ends for through traffic at that point. Slow down, do not drive into the water, and find a safe route or turn around.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: Emergency lights flashing
answer_text_b: A traffic light ahead
answer_text_c: A sunrise ahead
correct_answer: A. Emergency lights flashing
answer_information_text: This sign warns of a hazard ahead, indicated by an emergency flashing light. Slow down and look for further signs or instructions showing the specific danger.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: A driveway on the left
answer_text_b: Traffic approaching from the left
answer_text_c: A race track ahead
correct_answer: B. Traffic approaching from the left
answer_information_text: This sign warns that traffic may approach or join the road from the left ahead. Slow down, look carefully to the left and be ready to stop or give way if necessary.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: A skew T-junction ahead
answer_text_b: A tourist destination ahead
answer_text_c: A right-angle T-junction ahead
correct_answer: A. A skew T-junction ahead
answer_information_text: This sign warns of a skew T-junction ahead, where your road ends at another road at an angle rather than at a right angle.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: Speed bump
answer_text_b: A police station
answer_text_c: Sand dunes
correct_answer: A. Speed bump
answer_information_text: This sign warns that a speed bump or speed hump is ahead. Slow down before reaching it so that you cross safely without losing control or damaging the vehicle.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: There is a crossroad ahead where your road has priority over the intersecting road
answer_text_b: There is a roundabout ahead
answer_text_c: There is a crossroad ahead where the intersecting road has priority over your road
correct_answer: A. There is a crossroad ahead where your road has priority over the intersecting road
answer_information_text: This sign warns of a crossroad ahead where your road has priority over the intersecting road. Approach cautiously and obey any traffic officer, traffic signals or regulatory signs.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: There is a hump ahead
answer_text_b: There is a beach nearby
answer_text_c: The road is uneven
correct_answer: C. The road is uneven
answer_information_text: An uneven-road warning marks a section where the road surface is not level or smooth. Slow down and keep control because suspension movement and changes in wheel grip can affect steering and braking.

question_text: What does this sign prevent you from doing?
answer_text_a: Hitch-hiking, or stopping to pick up hitch-hikers
answer_text_b: Hooting
answer_text_c: Overtaking
correct_answer: A. Hitch-hiking, or stopping to pick up hitch-hikers
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits hitch-hiking on that road: people may not ask passing vehicles for a lift there, and drivers may not stop to pick them up.

question_text: What does this warn you of?
answer_text_a: A restaurant ahead
answer_text_b: It warns of a T-junction ahead
answer_text_c: A left turn ahead
correct_answer: B. It warns of a T-junction ahead
answer_information_text: This sign warns of a T-junction ahead, where the road you are travelling on meets another road and you must turn left or right. Slow down, watch for cross-traffic and be prepared to stop before turning safely.

question_text: What does this sign prohibit you from doing?
answer_text_a: Racing in this area
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to own two vehicles
answer_text_c: Overtaking in this area
correct_answer: C. Overtaking in this area
answer_information_text: A no-overtaking sign prohibits you from overtaking another vehicle on this section of road. You must remain behind the vehicle ahead until the restriction ends, even if the road looks clear.

question_text: What does this sign prohibit you from doing?
answer_text_a: Stopping in this area
answer_text_b: Making a sharp turn in this area
answer_text_c: Starting your vehicle in this area
correct_answer: A. Stopping in this area
answer_information_text: A no-stopping sign prohibits stopping in the controlled area, except where stopping is required by traffic conditions or an instruction from a traffic officer or robot. Do not stop there to wait, load passengers or park.

question_text: What does this sign prohibit you from doing?
answer_text_a: Reversing
answer_text_b: Making a U-turn
answer_text_c: Turning right
correct_answer: B. Making a U-turn
answer_information_text: A no-U-turn sign prohibits turning the vehicle around to travel in the opposite direction at that place. Continue ahead and turn around only where U-turns are permitted and safe.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You are allowed to turn left
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to turn right
answer_text_c: You can not turn left
correct_answer: C. You can not turn left
answer_information_text: A no-left-turn sign prohibits turning left at the indicated junction or entrance. Follow the permitted direction and use another route if you need to travel left.

question_text: What does this sign indicate?
answer_text_a: There is a one-way road in the direction indicated
answer_text_b: You must stop when you see this sign
answer_text_c: You must turn left at this sign
correct_answer: A. There is a one-way road in the direction indicated
answer_information_text: A one-way road sign shows that traffic may travel along the road only in the direction of the arrow. It does not necessarily require you to turn left; the arrow identifies the permitted direction of travel.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a helipad ahead
answer_text_b: There are low flying aircrafts ahead
answer_text_c: There is an airshow ahead
correct_answer: B. There are low flying aircrafts ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign indicates that aircraft may fly low over or near the road ahead. Reduce speed, stay alert and be prepared for aircraft-related hazards in the warning area.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You have the right of way
answer_text_b: There is only traffic on the left-hand side ahead
answer_text_c: The road narrows from the right-hand side
correct_answer: C. The road narrows from the right-hand side
answer_information_text: This warning sign shows that the road will become narrower on the right-hand side ahead. Keep a proper lookout, adjust your speed and give other traffic enough space as the usable road width reduces.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is two-way traffic ahead
answer_text_b: You have the right of way
answer_text_c: There is an intersection ahead
correct_answer: A. There is two-way traffic ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign indicates two-way traffic ahead, so vehicles may approach from the opposite direction. Keep left, maintain a safe speed and watch carefully for oncoming traffic.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You must keep left
answer_text_b: You must keep right
answer_text_c: You have to reverse
correct_answer: B. You must keep right
answer_information_text: A keep-right regulatory sign requires you to pass on the right-hand side indicated by the sign. It is a compulsory K53 instruction, so you must not choose the left side or reverse instead.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You have to reverse
answer_text_b: You must keep right
answer_text_c: You must keep left
correct_answer: C. You must keep left
answer_information_text: A keep-left regulatory sign requires you to pass on the left-hand side indicated by the sign. It is a compulsory K53 instruction, so you must not move to the right instead.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There are temporary road works ahead
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to proceed
answer_text_c: There is a new road surface ahead
correct_answer: A. There are temporary road works ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign tells you that temporary road works are ahead. Slow down, watch for workers and temporary traffic-control signs, and follow any directions given by a flag person or robot. Road conditions and lanes may change while the work is in progress.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: The road has debris ahead
answer_text_b: The road ahead is slippery
answer_text_c: You are allowed to drift ahead
correct_answer: B. The road ahead is slippery
answer_information_text: This warning sign tells you that the road ahead may be slippery. Reduce speed, avoid harsh braking or steering, and leave a larger following distance so that the tyres can maintain grip.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Do not enter the road beyond this sign.
answer_text_b: Slow down and stop only if other traffic is approaching.
answer_text_c: Come to a complete stop behind the stop line; if there is no stop line, stop before entering the intersecting roadway.
correct_answer: C. Come to a complete stop behind the stop line; if there is no stop line, stop before entering the intersecting roadway.
answer_information_text: A STOP sign requires you to stop completely behind the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the intersecting roadway.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: It prohibits animal-drawn vehicles ahead
answer_text_b: No cattle are allowed ahead
answer_text_c: You are not allowed to race animal-drawn vehicles
correct_answer: A. It prohibits animal-drawn vehicles ahead
answer_information_text: This is a prohibition, not a warning: animal-drawn vehicles may not proceed beyond the sign. A driver must obey the restriction and not enter that section with an animal-drawn vehicle.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: It warns you of a desert ahead
answer_text_b: It warns you of a speed hump ahead
answer_text_c: It means there is an incline ahead
correct_answer: B. It warns you of a speed hump ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign tells you that a speed hump is ahead. Slow down before reaching it and cross at a safe speed, because braking or swerving on the hump can reduce control of the vehicle.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: It warns you of a stop street ahead
answer_text_b: It means you have right of way
answer_text_c: It warns you of a traffic light ahead
correct_answer: C. It warns you of a traffic light ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign tells you that traffic lights, or a robot, are ahead. Slow down, watch the lights and other traffic, and be ready to stop because the signal may change before you reach it.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: It warns you of a pedestrian crossing ahead
answer_text_b: There is a school ahead
answer_text_c: You are not allowed to cross the road in this area
correct_answer: A. It warns you of a pedestrian crossing ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign tells you that a pedestrian crossing is ahead. Slow down, look carefully for pedestrians, and be ready to stop and give them right of way at the crossing.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You are not allowed to carry livestock
answer_text_b: It warns you of wild animals crossing ahead
answer_text_c: It warns you of a zoo ahead
correct_answer: B. It warns you of wild animals crossing ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign shows that wild animals may cross the road ahead. Reduce speed, watch both sides of the road, and be prepared to stop because animals may enter the roadway suddenly.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: It warns you of a right turn ahead
answer_text_b: You must yield at the mini-circle to vehicles that will cross their yield lines before you cross yours and whose paths will cross yours, and proceed clockwise
answer_text_c: It warns you of a left turn ahead
correct_answer: B. You must yield at the mini-circle to vehicles that will cross their yield lines before you cross yours and whose paths will cross yours, and proceed clockwise
answer_information_text: Yield to vehicles that will cross their yield lines before you cross yours and whose paths will cross yours. Proceed clockwise and try not to drive over the central mini-circle.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: It warns that the road narrows from the left and right hand side
answer_text_b: It warns that the road narrows from the right hand side
answer_text_c: It warns that the road narrows from the left hand side
correct_answer: A. It warns that the road narrows from the left and right hand side
answer_information_text: This warning sign means that the road will become narrower from both the left and right sides. Reduce speed and keep a safe following distance because there will be less space for vehicles to pass.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only 100 vehicles are allowed on this road
answer_text_b: The speed limit is 100 km/h
answer_text_c: You must drive above 100 km/h
correct_answer: B. The speed limit is 100 km/h
answer_information_text: This sign sets the maximum permitted speed at 100 km/h. You must not drive faster than 100 km/h, and you should still reduce your speed when road, traffic or weather conditions require it.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You are only allowed to park beyond this sign
answer_text_b: You are allowed to stop by this sign
answer_text_c: You are not allowed to stop where you see this sign
correct_answer: C. You are not allowed to stop where you see this sign
answer_information_text: This prohibition sign means that you may not stop at the place where it applies. Do not park, wait, load or unload there, except when stopping is necessary because of an emergency or to obey a traffic instruction.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: The maximum speed limit is 50 km/h.
answer_text_b: The recommended speed is 50 km/h.
answer_text_c: The minimum speed is 50 km/h.
correct_answer: C. The minimum speed is 50 km/h.
answer_information_text: This sign requires drivers to maintain a speed of at least 50 km/h on the road or lane to which it applies.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: The sign is empty you don't have to do anything
answer_text_b: You must yield and give way to other vehicles
answer_text_c: You have to increase your speed
correct_answer: B. You must yield and give way to other vehicles
answer_information_text: This yield sign requires you to slow down and give way to other vehicles with right of way. Stop if necessary, and proceed only when it is safe without forcing another road user to brake or change direction.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only people with forklift permits are allowed here
answer_text_b: Only forklifts are allowed past this sign
answer_text_c: Forklifts are not allowed past this sign
correct_answer: C. Forklifts are not allowed past this sign
answer_information_text: This is a prohibition sign for forklifts, so forklifts may not pass the sign. Prohibition signs identify a vehicle, road user or action that is not allowed beyond the sign.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only full-size buses are allowed on this lane
answer_text_b: Only mini buses are allowed on this lane
answer_text_c: Only mid buses are allowed on this lane
correct_answer: A. Only full-size buses are allowed on this lane
answer_information_text: This sign reserves the lane for mid buses. A vehicle-specific lane sign applies to the type of vehicle shown by the symbol, so mini buses and full-size buses may not use the lane unless another sign or road marking allows it.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: There is a beach ahead
answer_text_b: This sign warns of an uneven road ahead
answer_text_c: There are sand dunes ahead
correct_answer: B. This sign warns of an uneven road ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign indicates an uneven road ahead. Slow down, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and watch for changes in the road surface, because the uneven section can affect the vehicle's stability and braking.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only 6 vehicles are allowed on this road.
answer_text_b: Vehicles must weigh over 6 tons to be a truck
answer_text_c: If the vehicle's axle mass exceeds 6 tons, use another road not indicated by this sign
correct_answer: C. If the vehicle's axle mass exceeds 6 tons, use another road not indicated by this sign
answer_information_text: This restriction applies when a vehicle's axle mass exceeds 6 tonnes. Such a vehicle may not use this road and must take another route, because the road ahead is not suitable for that axle loading.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Vehicles exceeding 12 tonnes GVM prohibited
answer_text_b: Only yellow trucks are allowed here
answer_text_c: Only 12 vehicles are allowed on this road.
correct_answer: A. Vehicles exceeding 12 tonnes GVM prohibited
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits vehicles with a gross vehicle mass exceeding 12 tonnes. GVM is the total permitted mass of the loaded vehicle, including its load, rather than the vehicle's colour or the number of vehicles allowed.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You need to have a permit to ride a horse
answer_text_b: No horse riding is allowed past this point
answer_text_c: You may not ride horses during the day
correct_answer: B. No horse riding is allowed past this point
answer_information_text: This prohibition sign means that horse riding is not allowed beyond the sign. It applies to riding horses on that road or area, not only to riding during the day and not merely to riders without a permit.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only mini busses can drive on this lane
answer_text_b: Only mid buses can drive on this lane
