answer_text_c: Only buses can drive on this lane
correct_answer: C. Only buses can drive on this lane
answer_information_text: This sign reserves the lane for buses. The bus symbol covers buses generally, so the lane is not restricted only to mid buses or mini buses.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Bicycles are not allowed past this sign
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to ride a bicycle at night
answer_text_c: You can only ride a bicycle at night
correct_answer: A. Bicycles are not allowed past this sign
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits bicycles beyond the sign. It does not limit the prohibition to night-time and does not make cycling compulsory at night; the bicycle symbol with the prohibition marking means bicycles may not pass.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: You are not allowed to ride a taxi
answer_text_b: Taxis are not allowed past this sign
answer_text_c: Taxis are only allowed here on weekends
correct_answer: B. Taxis are not allowed past this sign
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits taxis from continuing beyond the sign. A taxi may not pass it unless another sign or a traffic officer gives a lawful instruction that changes the restriction.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: This lane is dedicated to police vehicles only
answer_text_b: Only sedans may park here
answer_text_c: Only taxis may drive here
correct_answer: C. Only taxis may drive here
answer_information_text: This sign reserves the road or lane for taxis, so other vehicle types may not use it. A taxi must still obey the robot, speed limit and other road rules while driving there.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Only abnormal vehicles may drive here
answer_text_b: Only hatchback vehicles may drive here
answer_text_c: Only automatic vehicles may drive here
correct_answer: A. Only abnormal vehicles may drive here
answer_information_text: This sign permits abnormal vehicles to use the road or lane. An abnormal vehicle exceeds the normal legal limits for dimensions or mass and is subject to special road rules and permits.

question_text: What colour boards do Guidance and Information signs have for freeways?
answer_text_a: Green
answer_text_b: Red
answer_text_c: Blue
correct_answer: C. Blue
answer_information_text: Guidance and Information signs for freeways use blue boards. This colour helps distinguish freeway route and direction information from other sign categories, so blue is the colour to recognise for these signs.

question_text: What colour background does a permanent tourism direction sign have?
answer_text_a: White
answer_text_b: Blue
answer_text_c: Brown
correct_answer: C. Brown
answer_information_text: Permanent tourism direction signs have a brown background and guide road users to tourist destinations and facilities.

question_text: At a stop sign you must:
answer_text_a: Slow down and proceed if it is safe
answer_text_b: Stop only if there are other vehicles
answer_text_c: Bring your car to a complete stop and proceed only when safe
correct_answer: C. Bring your car to a complete stop and proceed only when safe
answer_information_text: At a stop sign, bring your vehicle to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question_text: At a yield sign you must:
answer_text_a: Slow down and proceed when safe
answer_text_b: Bring your car to a complete stop always
answer_text_c: Ignore it if no other vehicles are present
correct_answer: A. Slow down and proceed when safe
answer_information_text: At a yield sign, slow down and be prepared to stop. Proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question_text: This sign warns a driver that ...
answer_text_a: A T-junction is ahead
answer_text_b: A skew T-junction is ahead
answer_text_c: A side road joins from the right at an acute angle ahead
correct_answer: C. A side road joins from the right at an acute angle ahead
answer_information_text: This sign warns of a sharp junction ahead where a side road joins from the right. Approach cautiously and watch for traffic entering or leaving at the junction.

question_text: This sign shows the driver that ...
answer_text_a: All vehicles are prohibited from overtaking for the next 500 metres.
answer_text_b: Motor vehicles may not overtake goods vehicles.
answer_text_c: A goods vehicle may not overtake another goods vehicle for the next 500 metres.
correct_answer: C. A goods vehicle may not overtake another goods vehicle for the next 500 metres.
answer_information_text: Goods vehicles may not overtake other goods vehicles for the next 500 metres. The restriction does not prohibit every type of overtaking.

question_text: This road marking warns you that ...
answer_text_a: You may not enter this parking area
answer_text_b: A railway line will be crossing the road at the same level
answer_text_c: You will have to change lanes ahead
correct_answer: B. A railway line will be crossing the road at the same level
answer_information_text: This road marking warns that a railway line crosses the road at the same level. Approach cautiously, obey railway signals or barriers, and give way where required before crossing.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: Level crossing ahead
answer_text_b: A marked pedestrian crossing ahead
answer_text_c: You must be on the lookout for cyclists
correct_answer: B. A marked pedestrian crossing ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign indicates a marked pedestrian crossing ahead. Slow down, look out for pedestrians and be ready to stop.

question_text: When a vehicle is travelling in the right hand lane, as shown in this sign, the driver must ...
answer_text_a: Overtake vehicles in the right-hand lane travelling slower than 80 km/h.
answer_text_b: Drive slower than 80 km/h.
answer_text_c: Drive at 80 km/h or faster, unless road or traffic conditions require a slower speed.
correct_answer: C. Drive at 80 km/h or faster, unless road or traffic conditions require a slower speed.
answer_information_text: The blue circular 80 sign indicates a minimum speed of 80 km/h, subject to safe road and traffic conditions. It does not require overtaking in that lane.

question_text: What does this road sign indicate?
answer_text_a: No overtaking is permitted.
answer_text_b: A two-lane roadway joins from the left without reducing the combined number of lanes.
answer_text_c: The vehicle in the right-hand lane has right of way.
correct_answer: B. A two-lane roadway joins from the left without reducing the combined number of lanes.
answer_information_text: A two-lane roadway converges with another two-lane roadway from the left. All four lanes continue beyond the junction.

question_text: When may you stop where this sign applies?
answer_text_a: When stopping briefly to load or unload goods
answer_text_b: When picking up passengers
answer_text_c: When necessary to avoid an accident, obey a road traffic sign or a traffic officer's direction, or because of circumstances beyond your control
correct_answer: C. When necessary to avoid an accident, obey a road traffic sign or a traffic officer's direction, or because of circumstances beyond your control
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits stopping, including brief stops to collect passengers or load goods. Exceptions include avoiding an accident, obeying a road traffic sign or signal or a traffic officer's direction, and circumstances beyond the driver's control.

question_text: This sign shows you that ...
answer_text_a: There is a roadside shop to your left.
answer_text_b: You have to turn off to a weigh bridge.
answer_text_c: An arrestor bed is ahead to help stop a vehicle if its brakes fail.
correct_answer: C. An arrestor bed is ahead to help stop a vehicle if its brakes fail.
answer_information_text: The red-and-white pattern warns of an arrestor bed ahead, intended to stop vehicles whose brakes have failed. The image does not indicate that the arrestor bed is specifically to the left.

question_text: This sign shows you that ...
answer_text_a: The road to the left is a dead end.
answer_text_b: The road ahead is one-way.
answer_text_c: The road to the right is a dead end.
correct_answer: C. The road to the right is a dead end.
answer_information_text: The red block marks the closed end of the road branching to the right. That road has no through route.

question_text: In order to draw attention, the background of temporary signs is usually ...
answer_text_a: Red
answer_text_b: White
answer_text_c: Yellow
correct_answer: C. Yellow
answer_information_text: Temporary road signs have yellow backgrounds so that they stand out and draw attention to temporary road conditions or controls. Drivers must pay particular attention to these signs and follow their instructions.

question_text: A temporary sign ...
answer_text_a: Has the same legal significance as a permanent sign
answer_text_b: Need not be taken seriously at all times of the day
answer_text_c: Is of less consequence to road users than a permanent sign
correct_answer: A. Has the same legal significance as a permanent sign
answer_information_text: A temporary sign has the same legal significance as a permanent sign while it is displayed. Road users must obey it and adjust their driving to the temporary traffic control, roadworks or hazard.

question_text: The use of a temporary sign implies that for some reason ...
answer_text_a: The rules of the road do not apply
answer_text_b: Circumstances on the roadway are not normal
answer_text_c: Traffic has to move slowly
correct_answer: B. Circumstances on the roadway are not normal
answer_information_text: A temporary sign is used when road conditions or traffic arrangements are different from normal. It warns you to expect a temporary hazard or change, such as roadworks, a diversion or lane restrictions, and to adjust your driving accordingly.

question_text: Which statement about pedestrian traffic-light signals is correct?
answer_text_a: When the green man is showing, pedestrians may walk across; when the red light is showing, pedestrians may not walk across
answer_text_b: When the green man is showing, pedestrians should run across the street as fast as they can
answer_text_c: When the red man is showing, pedestrians have priority
correct_answer: A. When the green man is showing, pedestrians may walk across; when the red light is showing, pedestrians may not walk across
answer_information_text: The green pedestrian signal permits pedestrians to cross the road, while the red pedestrian signal prohibits them from starting to cross. Pedestrians should still watch for vehicles and cross carefully; the green signal does not mean they must run.

question_text: Reversible lane road markings (lanes that may be used by traffic in opposite directions at different times) warn the road user that ...
answer_text_a: The road will split
answer_text_b: The same lane may be used by vehicles in opposite directions at different times
answer_text_c: No overtaking is allowed
correct_answer: B. The same lane may be used by vehicles in opposite directions at different times
answer_information_text: Reversible-lane markings indicate that a lane can carry traffic in one direction at one time and in the opposite direction at another time. Follow the signs and lane-control signals carefully because the direction of traffic in that lane can change.

question_text: A sign showing a camera icon at a traffic light tells you that ...
answer_text_a: There is a photographic studio nearby
answer_text_b: The taking of photographs is not permitted
answer_text_c: There is a camera monitoring the intersection at the traffic light
correct_answer: C. There is a camera monitoring the intersection at the traffic light
answer_information_text: A camera symbol at traffic lights indicates that the intersection is monitored by a camera. Obey the robot and approach the intersection in accordance with the traffic signal and other road rules.

question_text: When the robot is red and the green arrow flashes to the right, it shows you that...
answer_text_a: All traffic must turn right there
answer_text_b: If you want to turn right, you may go
answer_text_c: Only pedestrians may walk
correct_answer: B. If you want to turn right, you may go
answer_information_text: A red robot normally stops traffic, but a flashing green arrow gives permission to turn right. The turn applies only to traffic facing that signal, and you must still give way to pedestrians and traffic lawfully in the intersection.

question_text: This road sign shows you that you must...
answer_text_a: Stop and then turn left or drive straight
answer_text_b: Stop but if you want to turn left, you can use it as a yield sign
answer_text_c: Turn left at stop sign
correct_answer: B. Stop but if you want to turn left, you can use it as a yield sign
answer_information_text: If you are going straight, you must stop at this sign. If you are turning left, you may treat it as a yield sign and proceed without stopping only after giving way to traffic that could be affected.

question_text: This road sign shows you...
answer_text_a: Make sure that it is safe, wait until all traffic is departed and then drive on
answer_text_b: It is the same as a yield sign and you can proceed without stopping
answer_text_c: Stop and drive on when it is safe to do so in the sequence that the vehicles stopped at the stop lines
correct_answer: C. Stop and drive on when it is safe to do so in the sequence that the vehicles stopped at the stop lines
answer_information_text: Every vehicle must stop at an all-way stop. Vehicles proceed when it is safe, in the same order in which they stopped at the stop lines.

question_text: When you see this road sign you...
answer_text_a: Give right of way to pedestrians who would like to cross the street
answer_text_b: Stop because school kids might cross the road
answer_text_c: Know that, that section of the road is for the use of pedestrians only
correct_answer: A. Give right of way to pedestrians who would like to cross the street
answer_information_text: This sign gives pedestrians priority at the crossing. Slow down and give way to pedestrians who are crossing or clearly want to cross; it does not mean the whole section is for pedestrians or that you must stop automatically.

question_text: This road sign shows you that...
answer_text_a: The entry is for ambulances only
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to enter there
answer_text_c: The road ends
correct_answer: B. You are not allowed to enter there
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits entry from your direction. Do not drive past it, even though the road may continue beyond the sign.

question_text: If you see this road sign you know that...
answer_text_a: That section of the road can only carry vehicles that weigh up to 10 tonne
answer_text_b: Vehicles with a mass of more than 10 tonne may not drive there
answer_text_c: Vehicles with a mass of 10 tonne and less may not drive there
correct_answer: C. Vehicles with a mass of 10 tonne and less may not drive there
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits vehicles with a mass of 10 tonnes or less from using that section of road. Only vehicles exceeding 10 tonnes may pass, subject to any other restrictions shown by road signs.

question_text: This road sign shows you that you...
answer_text_a: Must only drive straight on
answer_text_b: Will get a one-way road ahead
answer_text_c: Will get a freeway ahead
correct_answer: A. Must only drive straight on
answer_information_text: This is a compulsory direction sign requiring you to continue straight ahead. You may not turn left or right at that point, and the sign does not indicate a freeway or a one-way road.

question_text: This road sign shows you that you...
answer_text_a: Will get a one-way road to the right
answer_text_b: Must turn right at the next road
answer_text_c: Can expect a sharp bend to the right
correct_answer: B. Must turn right at the next road
answer_information_text: This is a compulsory direction sign requiring a right turn at the next road or intersection. It is not merely a warning of a sharp bend and does not indicate that a one-way road begins to the right.

question_text: If you see this road sign...
answer_text_a: No vehicles may drive there because only pedestrians may walk there
answer_text_b: It shows two-way traffic ahead
answer_text_c: You may only drive there if you have special permission
correct_answer: C. You may only drive there if you have special permission
answer_information_text: This sign means that only authorised vehicles may use that road or area. You may enter only if you have the required special permission; it does not mean that all vehicles are banned or that two-way traffic lies ahead.

question_text: This road sign shows you that...
answer_text_a: No motor vehicles may pass each other
answer_text_b: Only motor cars may not pass each other
answer_text_c: There is a bridge ahead where only one vehicle at a time can cross
correct_answer: A. No motor vehicles may pass each other
answer_information_text: This sign prohibits motor vehicles from overtaking or passing one another on that section of road. You must remain behind the vehicle ahead until the restriction ends, even if the road seems wide enough to pass safely.

question_text: This road sign shows you the...
answer_text_a: Recommended speed when your lights are on
answer_text_b: Maximum speed allowed at night
answer_text_c: Distance to the next town
correct_answer: B. Maximum speed allowed at night
answer_information_text: This sign gives the highest speed at which you may drive during the night. It is a legal speed limit, not merely advice, so you must not exceed it when the night-time restriction applies.

question_text: What does This road sign show you
answer_text_a: A number of sharp curves ahead
answer_text_b: The road winds ahead
answer_text_c: A concealed entrance to the left is followed by one to the right
correct_answer: C. A concealed entrance to the left is followed by one to the right
answer_information_text: The sign warns that a concealed entrance on the left is followed by another concealed entrance on the right. Reduce speed and be ready for vehicles or pedestrians entering the road where they may not be visible early.

question_text: This road sign shows you that...
answer_text_a: You must be on the lookout for cyclists
answer_text_b: It is a special lane for cyclists
answer_text_c: No cyclists are allowed there
correct_answer: A. You must be on the lookout for cyclists
answer_information_text: This is a warning to look out for cyclists using or crossing the road ahead. Slow down, check carefully, and give cyclists enough space when passing them.

question_text: When you see this road sign you must slow down because...
answer_text_a: There is a dual track railway line in front
answer_text_b: There is a motor gate on the left-hand side of the road
answer_text_c: The surface of the road is uneven on the left-hand side
correct_answer: B. There is a motor gate on the left-hand side of the road
answer_information_text: The warning identifies a motor gate on the left-hand side of the road ahead. Slow down so you can approach the gate safely and obey any traffic control there.

question_text: What does this road sign show you?
answer_text_a: The road temporarily narrows from both sides
answer_text_b: Traffic congestion ahead
answer_text_c: The freeway temporarily ends ahead
correct_answer: B. Traffic congestion ahead
answer_information_text: This sign warns of possible slow-moving or stationary traffic ahead. Reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question_text: All road signs with a yellow background are...signs
answer_text_a: Temporary
answer_text_b: Warning
answer_text_c: Tourism
correct_answer: A. Temporary
answer_information_text: A yellow background identifies a temporary road sign. These signs apply to temporary conditions such as roadworks or changed traffic arrangements, and you must obey them while they are displayed.

question_text: This road sign shows you that...
answer_text_a: There is a narrow bridge ahead
answer_text_b: There is a drift ahead where the road may be flooded
answer_text_c: The road ends because of water ahead
correct_answer: B. There is a drift ahead where the road may be flooded
answer_information_text: This sign warns of a drift ahead where water may cover the road. The drift may also be a hazardous depression when dry.

question_text: When you see this road sign you must...
answer_text_a: Look out for road works where tractors operate
answer_text_b: Know that only agricultural vehicles may drive there
answer_text_c: Be on the lookout for agricultural vehicles that may be on the road
correct_answer: C. Be on the lookout for agricultural vehicles that may be on the road
answer_information_text: This warning sign alerts you that agricultural vehicles may be using or crossing the road. Slow down, keep a proper lookout and be ready for a tractor or other slow-moving agricultural vehicle, especially near farms or entrances.

question_text: This road sign shows you that there is a...
answer_text_a: Temporary obstruction left of the road / Pass on the right of this sign
answer_text_b: Curve to the left ahead
answer_text_c: Temporary detour to the left
correct_answer: A. Temporary obstruction left of the road / Pass on the right of this sign
answer_information_text: This warning means that a temporary obstruction is on the left side of the road and traffic must pass on its right. Slow down, check that it is safe, and pass on the right before returning to your normal lane.

question_text: When you get to this road sign you must...
answer_text_a: When you want to drive on straight, ignore it because traffic from the sides must stop
answer_text_b: Be ready to stop and turn left or right
answer_text_c: Choose to turn left or right or drive on straight after you have stopped
correct_answer: B. Be ready to stop and turn left or right
answer_information_text: This sign warns you to slow down and be prepared to stop before turning either left or right. It does not permit you to continue straight through the junction, so choose one of the indicated directions only when safe.

question_text: This road sign shows you that the road
answer_text_a: Winds 12km from there
answer_text_b: Is slippery for 12km
answer_text_c: Winds for 12km
correct_answer: C. Winds for 12km
answer_information_text: The sign shows that the road winds for 12 km from the sign. The distance applies to the winding section ahead, not to a point 12 km away, and it does not warn that the surface is slippery.

question_text: When the this road sign is illuminated, it shows you that...
answer_text_a: This is a lane for traffic coming only from the front
answer_text_b: There is an unguarded railway crossing ahead
answer_text_c: There is no throughway there
correct_answer: A. This is a lane for traffic coming only from the front
answer_information_text: When illuminated, this signal identifies a lane carrying traffic only in the direction facing you. Do not treat it as a lane for traffic travelling in the opposite direction or as a warning about a railway crossing.

question_text: What is the difference between these road marking
answer_text_a: There is no difference between the two and both show you that you may not pass other vehicles
answer_text_b: A single line shows you that you may not pass other vehicles while a double line as well shows you that you may not drive over it to turn into a yard or anything else
answer_text_c: Both shows you that you may not pass other vehicles but you will find a single line on all roads and a double lines on freeways only
correct_answer: B. A single line shows you that you may not pass other vehicles while a double line as well shows you that you may not drive over it to turn into a yard or anything else
answer_information_text: A single line means you may not cross it to pass another vehicle. A double no-crossing line also prevents you from driving over it to turn into a yard or another access, unless a specific lawful marking permits that movement.

question_text: This Road marking is a...
answer_text_a: Pedestrian crossing where you must stop for pedestrians
answer_text_b: Chevron that indicates a curve to the left
answer_text_c: Painted island where you are not allowed to drive on or stop
correct_answer: C. Painted island where you are not allowed to drive on or stop
answer_information_text: The marking is a painted island, which separates or guides traffic. You may not drive on it or stop on it, except when a lawful traffic instruction or an emergency requires it.

question_text: This Road marking shows you that only...may park there
answer_text_a: Municipal buses
answer_text_b: Motor cycles
answer_text_c: Minibuses
correct_answer: C. Minibuses
answer_information_text: The exclusive parking marking reserves that parking area for minibuses. Vehicles that are not minibuses may not park there, even if parking would otherwise be allowed on that road.

question_text: This road sign shows you that...
answer_text_a: The road turning to the left ends ahead
answer_text_b: You are not allowed to turn left there
answer_text_c: There is a T- junction to the left
correct_answer: A. The road turning to the left ends ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign shows that the side road turning left ends ahead. It warns about a dead-end side road; it does not prohibit turning left or show that your road ends at a T-junction.

question_text: Road marking GM1 in this sketch.....
answer_text_a: Divides the road in two sections
answer_text_b: Shows the lanes for road users
answer_text_c: Is only found in a parking area
correct_answer: B. Shows the lanes for road users
answer_information_text: GM1 markings are broken white lines used to separate lanes for traffic travelling in the same direction. They show road users where the lanes are and help them keep within their lane.

question_text: This arrow shows you that you...
answer_text_a: Can turn right or move straight on if it is safe
answer_text_b: Can still change lanes if you want to go on straight
answer_text_c: Must turn right from the lane
correct_answer: C. Must turn right from the lane
answer_information_text: A mandatory direction arrow applies to traffic in that lane. A right-pointing arrow means you must turn right at the junction and may not continue straight from that lane.

question_text: When you see road-marking you...
answer_text_a: May not park there at all because it's a no stopping road marking.
answer_text_b: May not park there because it is parking for ambulances only
answer_text_c: Know it is a lane reserved for emergency vehicle
correct_answer: A. May not park there at all because it's a no stopping road marking.
answer_information_text: A no-stopping road marking means you may not stop or park there. The restriction does not override a lawful instruction from a traffic officer, robot, road sign or another authorised traffic control.

question_text: Road marking RTM 1 shows you that...
answer_text_a: If you are driving in car A, must reduce speed and ride on if it is safe
answer_text_b: If you are driving in car A, must stop before this line
answer_text_c: If you are driving in car B, can pass car A if there are no other vehicles in the Intersection
correct_answer: B. If you are driving in car A, must stop before this line
answer_information_text: RTM1 is a stop line, so car A must come to a complete stop before reaching the line. The vehicle must not stop on or beyond the line, even when the intersection looks clear.

question_text: Road markings RTM3 in the sketch...
answer_text_a: Show you that you may not stop further than the front one of the two
answer_text_b: Are lines that indicate another traffic line
answer_text_c: Are the lines where pedestrians walk
correct_answer: C. Are the lines where pedestrians walk
answer_information_text: RTM3 markings are the white lines forming a pedestrian crossing across the roadway. Drivers must give way to pedestrians who are crossing or clearly waiting to cross there.

question_text: This road sign shows you that you...
answer_text_a: Must turn left at the next road
answer_text_b: Will get a one-way road to the left
answer_text_c: Can expect a sharp bend to the left
correct_answer: A. Must turn left at the next road
answer_information_text: A mandatory left-turn sign means traffic approaching it must turn left at the next road or junction. It is an instruction, not a warning of a bend or an indication of a one-way road.

question_text: This sign prohibits you from...
answer_text_a: Stopping there between 06:30 and 09:00
answer_text_b: Parking there at certain hours
answer_text_c: Using that section of the road during certain hours
correct_answer: B. Parking there at certain hours
answer_information_text: A no-parking restriction at stated times prohibits parking during those times. It does not generally prohibit every brief stop, but stopping is limited to permitted purposes such as picking up or setting down passengers or loading and unloading.

question_text: This sign warns you that there is a...
answer_text_a: Obstruction left on the road
answer_text_b: Detour to the left
answer_text_c: Sharp curve to the left ahead
correct_answer: C. Sharp curve to the left ahead
answer_information_text: This warning sign indicates a sharp curve to the left ahead. Slow down before the curve, keep to your side of the road and be prepared for hazards hidden around it.

question_text: This sign warns you that...
answer_text_a: There is a robot ahead
answer_text_b: You are now entering an urban area
answer_text_c: There is a compulsory police stop ahead
correct_answer: A. There is a robot ahead
answer_information_text: This sign warns that a robot is ahead, where traffic may stop or change direction. Reduce speed, watch the signal and be ready to stop safely.

question_text: This sign shows you that
answer_text_a: Potholes are to be found on the road ahead
answer_text_b: The road which you are driving is going to change to a gravel road
answer_text_c: The road is ending ahead
correct_answer: B. The road which you are driving is going to change to a gravel road
answer_information_text: This sign warns that the paved road changes to a gravel road ahead. Reduce speed before the surface changes because gravel provides less grip and may cause loss of control.

question_text: What does this road sign show you when it flashes?
answer_text_a: There is danger in the road ahead
answer_text_b: The police have a blockade ahead
answer_text_c: There is a robot ahead
correct_answer: A. There is danger in the road ahead
answer_information_text: When this sign flashes, it warns of danger in the road ahead. Slow down, increase your following distance and look carefully for the hazard.

question_text: This road sign shows that there is a/an...
answer_text_a: Detour to the right
answer_text_b: Obstruction to the right of the road / that you must pass on the left
answer_text_c: Curve to the right ahead
correct_answer: B. Obstruction to the right of the road / that you must pass on the left
answer_information_text: The sign shows an obstruction on the right side of the road, so you must pass it on the left. Check for approaching traffic and keep a safe clearance from the obstruction.

question_text: What does this road sign show you?
answer_text_a: The road on which you are driving is going to change to a gravel road
answer_text_b: The road is ending ahead
answer_text_c: Potholes are to be found on the road ahead
correct_answer: C. Potholes are to be found on the road ahead
answer_information_text: This sign warns that potholes are present on the road ahead. Reduce speed, choose the safest path and avoid sudden swerving or harsh braking near other traffic.

question_text: This Road marking shows that you must...
answer_text_a: Give right of way to all users of the road and possibly also trains
answer_text_b: Stop
answer_text_c: Look out for school kids
correct_answer: A. Give right of way to all users of the road and possibly also trains
answer_information_text: A yield line means you must give right of way to road users whose paths cross yours and, at a railway crossing, to trains. Slow down and be ready to stop before the line when necessary.

question_text: This road marking shows you that...
answer_text_a: Traffic in either direction must not cross these lines, except to pass a stationary obstruction when safe
answer_text_b: The road surface is uneven
answer_text_c: It is a lane reserved for buses only
correct_answer: A. Traffic in either direction must not cross these lines, except to pass a stationary obstruction when safe
answer_information_text: Double solid white lines prohibit crossing from either direction. You may cross them only to pass a stationary obstruction in the roadway when it is safe to do so.

question_text: This road marking shows that only... may stop in the bay.
answer_text_a: Construction vehicles
answer_text_b: Passenger cars picking up passengers
answer_text_c: Goods vehicles while loading or unloading
correct_answer: C. Goods vehicles while loading or unloading
answer_information_text: The "L" marking reserves the bay for goods vehicles while they load or unload, and only for as long as that reasonably takes.

question_text: This road marking shows you that...
answer_text_a: You may not park adjacent to the lines next to the black arrows during certain hours
answer_text_b: You may not stop adjacent to the lines next to the black arrows
answer_text_c: The road is under construction.
correct_answer: A. You may not park adjacent to the lines next to the black arrows during certain hours
answer_information_text: A time-based parking restriction applies only during the hours shown on the accompanying sign. During those hours, parking alongside the marked lines is prohibited; outside them, that specific restriction does not apply.

question_text: This traffic signal can be found on
answer_text_a: Only where a railway line crosses a road.
answer_text_b: At intersections and other places where vehicular traffic needs to be controlled.
answer_text_c: Only on roads where accidents frequently occur.
correct_answer: B. At intersections and other places where vehicular traffic needs to be controlled.
answer_information_text: This signal controls vehicular traffic at intersections and other suitable locations. Railway crossings normally use flashing red signals rather than this standard red-amber-green signal.

question_text: These road markings
answer_text_a: Shows you that you may not stop in front of the two lines
answer_text_b: Are the lines that indicate another lane
answer_text_c: Are the lines where pedestrians walk at an intersection
correct_answer: C. Are the lines where pedestrians walk at an intersection
answer_information_text: These are pedestrian crossing lines at an intersection. They show where pedestrians cross, so drivers must slow down and give priority to pedestrians crossing or wanting to cross.

question_text: This sign indicates....
answer_text_a: You are entering a freeway.
answer_text_b: There are heavy vehicles entering on your left.
answer_text_c: There are 2 additional lanes ahead.
correct_answer: C. There are 2 additional lanes ahead.
answer_information_text: The two curved arrows show lanes being added from the left. The sign does not indicate a freeway entrance or heavy vehicles.

question_text: What does this sign warn you of?
answer_text_a: The dual roadway ends and the two carriageways become one road
answer_text_b: The road narrows from both sides ahead
answer_text_c: Two traffic lanes merge ahead
correct_answer: A. The dual roadway ends and the two carriageways become one road
answer_information_text: The symbol shows two separate carriageways, with a gap between them, joining into one: the dual roadway ends and oncoming traffic will share the road.

question_text: What is the function of this road marking....
answer_text_a: It tells the driver that he may not cross it
answer_text_b: It warns the driver to slow down.
answer_text_c: It is a dividing line that shows the lanes for road users
correct_answer: C. It is a dividing line that shows the lanes for road users
answer_information_text: This line separates the traffic lanes and helps road users keep to the correct lane. It is not, by itself, a no-crossing line; whether it may be crossed depends on the type and pattern of the marking.

question_text: When you come across the mini-circle road markings shown, you must...
answer_text_a: Stop beyond the yield line before deciding whether to enter the mini-circle.
answer_text_b: Yield to any vehicle that will cross its yield line before you cross yours and whose path will cross yours.
answer_text_c: Yield only to vehicles approaching from your right.
correct_answer: B. Yield to any vehicle that will cross its yield line before you cross yours and whose path will cross yours.
answer_information_text: At a mini-circle, yield to vehicles that cross their yield lines before you cross yours and whose paths will cross yours, stopping if necessary. Travel clockwise around the centre.

question_text: This sign can be found at...?
answer_text_a: A bridge.
answer_text_b: A single freeway.
answer_text_c: A dual freeway.
correct_answer: C. A dual freeway.
answer_information_text: This sign identifies a dual freeway, where the two directions of traffic are carried on separate carriageways. A single freeway has one carriageway carrying traffic in both directions, so the sign does not refer to that type of road.

question_text: When driving on a road with this sign displayed, It tells a driver that...?
answer_text_a: They have right of way at the next intersection.
answer_text_b: They should give right of way to traffic from the right hand side.
answer_text_c: Traffic from the other directions have right of way.
correct_answer: A. They have right of way at the next intersection.
answer_information_text: This is a priority-road instruction: traffic approaching the next intersection must give way to you. You must still drive defensively and obey any traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign that controls the intersection.

question_text: When seeing this sign...?
answer_text_a: There is no cell phone reception for the next 500 m.
answer_text_b: An SOS emergency telephone is available here.
answer_text_c: There is a public phone 500 m ahead.
correct_answer: B. An SOS emergency telephone is available here.
answer_information_text: The SOS symbol identifies an emergency telephone or call station. It does not indicate a distance or a lack of mobile-phone reception.

question_text: This sign indicates to a driver that there is...
answer_text_a: An obstruction in the road for 1km.
answer_text_b: Road works within 1km
answer_text_c: An obstruction in the road 1 km ahead which will affect the traffic flow.
correct_answer: C. An obstruction in the road 1 km ahead which will affect the traffic flow.
answer_information_text: The marked answer warns of an obstruction 1 km ahead that will affect the movement of traffic. Reduce speed, keep a safe following distance, and be prepared to stop or change lanes only when it is safe and permitted.

question_text: This sign indicates...
answer_text_a: The direction to a freeway.
answer_text_b: There is a bridge ahead where you can turn right
answer_text_c: That all traffic must turn right.
correct_answer: A. The direction to a freeway.
answer_information_text: This direction sign points towards a freeway. It gives a route direction to the freeway; it does not mean that every vehicle must turn right unless a separate compulsory-direction sign says so.

question_text: This road marking shows you that.
answer_text_a: It is a lane reserved for busses only.
answer_text_b: Traffic may not pass or cross it from either side.
answer_text_c: It is permitted to pass slow moving vehicles.
correct_answer: B. Traffic may not pass or cross it from either side.
answer_information_text: A double solid line may not be crossed or straddled from either direction — it separates opposing traffic where overtaking would be dangerous. Stay on your own side of it until the marking changes.

question_text: This sign tells road users that....?
answer_text_a: The road is closed to traffic permanently
answer_text_b: They are approaching a temporary dead end
answer_text_c: A portion of the road is temporary closed to traffic.
correct_answer: C. A portion of the road is temporary closed to traffic.
answer_information_text: A temporary road-closure sign warns that part of the road is closed for a limited period, usually because of roadworks, an obstruction or an emergency. Obey the barricades and follow any diversion shown.

question_text: The sign indicates to a driver that there is a high speed exit in...?
answer_text_b: 2km
answer_information_text: The distance shown for the high-speed exit is 200 metres, giving you advance warning to prepare. Reduce speed and move into the correct lane safely before reaching the exit.

question_text: This sign commands the driver of a vehicle....?
answer_text_a: The fastest speed in the right hand lane is 80kph
answer_text_b: The minimum speed in the right hand lane is temporary 80kph
answer_text_c: The minimum speed in the right hand lane is permanently 80kph.
correct_answer: B. The minimum speed in the right hand lane is temporary 80kph
answer_information_text: A temporary minimum-speed instruction means that vehicles in the right-hand lane must not travel below 80 km/h while it is displayed. The instruction is temporary and applies only while the sign is in force.

question_text: This overhead signal shows you...?
answer_text_a: A railway crossing ahead
answer_text_b: Cross roads ahead
answer_text_c: Not to drive in this lane it's for vehicles from the front
correct_answer: C. Not to drive in this lane it's for vehicles from the front
answer_information_text: The marked answer tells you not to drive in that lane because the overhead red-cross signal closes it to traffic approaching from your direction. Move out of the lane safely and obey the lane-control signal.

question_text: This signal indicates...?
answer_text_a: The vehicles that want to turn right may do so but other vehicles must stop.
answer_text_b: A driver must stop before turning right
answer_text_c: The driver must turn right at this robot
correct_answer: A. The vehicles that want to turn right may do so but other vehicles must stop.
answer_information_text: A green arrow is permission, not an instruction: it lets the traffic wanting to move in the direction of the arrow proceed, while the red signal continues to hold back everyone else. You are never forced to turn because an arrow is showing.

question_text: When driving behind another vehicle, this road making shows you to...?
answer_text_a: Slow down and when it is safe pass the slow moving traffic.
answer_text_b: Slow down and keep a safe following distance behind the slow moving vehicles
answer_text_c: Pass only when no traffic is approaching from the front
correct_answer: B. Slow down and keep a safe following distance behind the slow moving vehicles
answer_information_text: This marking warns that passing is restricted, so slow down and keep a safe following distance behind slow-moving vehicles. Do not cross the marking to overtake, even if the road ahead looks clear.

question_text: This sign indicates a high speed exit in...?
answer_text_a: 3km
answer_information_text: The high-speed exit is 300 metres ahead, so you have time to plan your speed and lane position. Move across safely and never cross lanes suddenly to reach the exit.

question_text: This sign shows the driver of a vehicle that...?
answer_text_a: There is an alternative route at the next road to the right
answer_text_b: The road turns to the right only
answer_text_c: They must turn right at the next road
correct_answer: A. There is an alternative route at the next road to the right
answer_information_text: This sign indicates that an alternative route is available at the next road on the right. It does not instruct the driver to turn right, and it does not show that the main road itself turns right; it gives route-choice information.

question_text: When approaching this sign...?
answer_text_a: Keep left
answer_text_b: It shows a one way roadway to the left
answer_text_c: Turn left
correct_answer: B. It shows a one way roadway to the left
answer_information_text: This sign indicates a one-way roadway to the left. It gives information about the direction of traffic on that roadway, rather than ordering you to keep left or turn left at the sign.

question_text: This sign shows...?
answer_text_a: How much toll you have to pay if you drive on the toll road
answer_text_b: Which speed all vehicles must travel
answer_text_c: A toll road and an alternative to the toll road
correct_answer: C. A toll road and an alternative to the toll road
answer_information_text: This sign identifies a toll road and shows that an alternative route is available for drivers who do not want to use the toll road. It does not state the toll amount or prescribe a speed.

question_text: This road marking indicates...?
answer_text_a: An area is set aside for disabled persons
answer_text_b: No disabled persons allowed there
answer_text_c: Look out for persons in wheelchairs
correct_answer: A. An area is set aside for disabled persons
answer_information_text: This road marking reserves the area for vehicles used by disabled persons, normally where the required disabled-person parking permission is displayed. Other drivers must not use or park in the reserved area.

question_text: This type of sign is known as...?
answer_text_a: A warning sign
answer_text_b: An information sign
answer_text_c: A regulatory sign
correct_answer: B. An information sign
answer_information_text: This is an information sign because it gives road or route information to the driver. Information signs guide or inform road users; they do not impose a prohibition, obligation or warning of danger.

question_text: What does this road marking indicate?
answer_text_a: Only Two lanes may be used
answer_text_b: Vehicles on the Left can overtake
answer_text_c: The left lane is reducing
correct_answer: C. The left lane is reducing
answer_information_text: This road marking shows that the left lane is reducing and will end or merge into the remaining lane. Drivers in that lane must prepare to merge safely, while other drivers should allow sufficient space where necessary.

question_text: This Sign shows you that....
answer_text_a: A sequence of turnoffs to various centres
answer_text_b: A route to the city hall
answer_text_c: A road block ahead
correct_answer: A. A sequence of turnoffs to various centres
answer_information_text: This sign shows a sequence of turn-offs leading to different centres or destinations. It helps drivers plan which exit or turn-off to use; it is not limited to a route to the city hall and does not indicate a roadblock.

question_text: What does this sign mean?
answer_text_a: An additional traffic lane opens on the left ahead.
answer_text_b: The left-hand traffic lane ends ahead.
answer_text_c: An additional traffic lane opens on the right ahead.
correct_answer: A. An additional traffic lane opens on the left ahead.
answer_information_text: This sign indicates that an additional traffic lane opens on the left ahead, increasing the number of lanes in your direction of travel.

question_text: This sign shows you
answer_text_a: Keep left
answer_text_b: Proceed left at the next intersection
answer_text_c: The road you may use to exit a freeway
correct_answer: C. The road you may use to exit a freeway
answer_information_text: This is a freeway exit sign showing the road or ramp used to leave the freeway. It gives exit information; it does not mean you must turn left at the next intersection or simply keep left.

question_text: This road sign prohibits...
answer_text_a: all motor cycle riders to ride there
answer_text_b: motor cycles with an engine capacity of 125 cc and less to be there
answer_text_c: motor cycles with an engine capacity of more than 125 cc to be there
correct_answer: B. motor cycles with an engine capacity of 125 cc and less to be there
answer_information_text: The restriction applies to motorcycles with an engine capacity of 125 cc or less. It does not prohibit every motorcycle, and this particular restriction does not apply to motorcycles above 125 cc.

question_text: This road sign shows to motor cycle riders that...
answer_text_a: They can ride to the left of this sign if they wish
answer_text_b: They must ride to the left of this sign
answer_text_c: The freeway ends ahead to the left
correct_answer: B. They must ride to the left of this sign

question_text: Which of the following is used to change gears?

answer_text_b: Steering wheel

answer_text_c: Indicators

question_text: Which of the following is used to prevent your car from stalling?
answer_text_a: Clutch Pedal
answer_text_b: Steering Wheel
answer_text_c: Brake Pedal
correct_answer: A. Clutch Pedal
answer_information_text: The clutch pedal helps prevent stalling by disconnecting the engine from the wheels while you select a gear or bring the vehicle to a stop. Release it smoothly and coordinate it with the accelerator when moving off.

question_text: Which of the following do you use to check the right side of your vehicle?

answer_text_b: Right side mirror
answer_text_c: Steering Wheel
correct_answer: B. Right side mirror
answer_information_text: The right side mirror lets you check the area alongside and behind the right side of your vehicle. Use it together with the rearview mirror and a blind-spot check before moving or changing lanes.

question_text: Which of the following do you use to clear your windscreen?

answer_information_text: The windscreen wiper clears rain, water and dirt from the windscreen so that you can see properly. Good visibility is essential before and while driving.

question_text: Which of the following do you use to engage a gear?
answer_text_a: Clutch Pedal

answer_text_c: Brake Pedal
correct_answer: A. Clutch Pedal
answer_information_text: Pressing the clutch pedal disengages the engine from the gearbox so that a gear can be selected and engaged without damaging the transmission. Release the clutch smoothly after selecting the gear to transfer power to the wheels.

question_text: Which of the following do you use to stop your vehicle?
answer_text_a: Accelerator

answer_text_c: Clutch Pedal
correct_answer: B. Brake Pedal
answer_information_text: The brake pedal operates the vehicle’s braking system and reduces the vehicle’s speed until it stops. Apply it progressively and keep the clutch in mind when stopping a manual vehicle so that the engine does not stall.

question_text: Which of the following is used to increase your speed?

answer_information_text: Pressing the accelerator increases the engine's power and makes the vehicle speed up. Apply it smoothly so that you remain in control and do not exceed the speed limit.

question_text: Which of the following is not found in an automatic vehicle?
