correct_answer: B. C
answer_information_text: Use control C to accelerate the vehicle. Apply pressure smoothly so that the vehicle increases speed under control and remains within the applicable speed limit.

question_text: To turn your vehicle you must use control..
answer_text_a: B
answer_text_b: G
answer_text_c: A
correct_answer: C. A
answer_information_text: Use control A to turn the vehicle by steering. Steer smoothly and keep both hands ready to maintain control while checking the road and mirrors.

question_text: What do you use to put your vehicle in to drive?
answer_text_a: F
answer_text_b: B
answer_text_c: C
correct_answer: B. B
answer_information_text: Use control B to put the vehicle into drive. Keep your foot on the brake while selecting drive, then move off only after checking that it is safe.

question_text: What do you use to turn your vehicle?
answer_text_a: E
answer_text_b: A
answer_text_c: B
correct_answer: B. A
answer_information_text: You use the steering wheel to turn the vehicle because it changes the direction of the front wheels. Smooth steering helps keep the vehicle on the intended path through the turn.

question_text: What do you use to slow your vehicle down?
answer_text_a: E
answer_text_b: A
answer_text_c: D
correct_answer: C. D
answer_information_text: The footbrake applies the service brakes and is used to slow the vehicle. The marked option identifies that control in the vehicle-controls diagram.

question_text: What do you use to accelerate?
answer_text_a: C
answer_text_b: G
answer_text_c: F
correct_answer: A. C
answer_information_text: The accelerator increases engine power and is used to make the vehicle speed up. The marked option identifies that control in the vehicle-controls diagram.

question_text: Which instrument is used to look at vehicles behind you?
answer_text_a: B
answer_text_b: E
answer_text_c: D
correct_answer: B. E
answer_information_text: The rear-view mirror gives the driver a view of vehicles behind the vehicle. The marked option identifies the instrument with that function in the vehicle-controls diagram.

question_text: What is the blind spot?
answer_text_a: The left side of your vehicle
answer_text_b: The area that you can't see in your mirror
answer_text_c: A specific area on your body
correct_answer: B. The area that you can't see in your mirror
answer_information_text: A blind spot is an area around the vehicle that cannot be seen in the mirrors. Because a vehicle or road user may be hidden there, turn your head to check the blind spot before moving, changing lanes or turning.

question_text: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum distance from which your hooter must be clearly audible to a person of normal hearing?
answer_text_a: 80 metres
answer_text_b: 100 metres
answer_text_c: 90 metres
correct_answer: C. 90 metres
answer_information_text: Under normal conditions, a motor vehicle's hooter must be clearly audible from at least 90 metres to someone with normal hearing.

question_text: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
answer_text_a: Every 30 minutes
answer_text_b: Every 5 to 8 seconds
answer_text_c: Every 10 minutes
correct_answer: B. Every 5 to 8 seconds
answer_information_text: K53 requires regular rear-view mirror checks every 5 to 8 seconds. Also check the mirrors before hazards and before changing speed, stopping, turning or changing lanes, while keeping your eyes mainly on the road ahead.

question_text: When the oil pressure warning light comes on while driving, you should:
answer_text_a: Increase speed to reach your destination faster
answer_text_b: Stop as soon as safely possible and check the oil level
answer_text_c: Continue driving to the nearest garage
correct_answer: B. Stop as soon as safely possible and check the oil level
answer_information_text: Stop the vehicle as soon as it is safe to do so and check the oil level. Continuing to drive with low oil pressure can destroy the engine.

question_text: When should you use hazard lights?
answer_text_a: When looking for parking
answer_text_b: When your vehicle is stationary in a hazardous position, or moving in an emergency situation
answer_text_c: When driving in rain
correct_answer: B. When your vehicle is stationary in a hazardous position, or moving in an emergency situation
answer_information_text: Use hazard lights when your vehicle is stopped in a dangerous position or moving during an emergency. They must not be used in other circumstances.

question_text: The ABS warning light on the dashboard indicates:
answer_text_a: The battery is low
answer_text_b: A fault in the anti-lock braking system
answer_text_c: The airbags need servicing
correct_answer: B. A fault in the anti-lock braking system
answer_information_text: The ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) warning light indicates a fault in the ABS system. Normal brakes still work, but the anti-lock function is disabled.

question_text: The temperature gauge on your dashboard shows the engine is overheating. You should:
answer_text_a: Drive faster to get more airflow
answer_text_b: Immediately open the radiator cap to release pressure
answer_text_c: Turn the heater on full to help cool the engine, then stop safely
correct_answer: C. Turn the heater on full to help cool the engine, then stop safely
answer_information_text: Stop the vehicle safely, turn off the engine, and wait for it to cool before checking the coolant level. Never open a hot radiator cap.

question_text: What is the purpose of an accelerator?
answer_text_a: It is used to increase or decrease the speed of a vehicle
answer_text_b: It is used to change gears
answer_text_c: It is used to stop the vehicle
correct_answer: A. It is used to increase or decrease the speed of a vehicle
answer_information_text: The accelerator controls the power delivered by the engine and changes the vehicle’s speed. Pressing it increases speed, while releasing it allows the vehicle to slow down.

question_text: Which control is used to change the direction of the vehicle?
answer_text_a: The accelerator
answer_text_b: The steering wheel
answer_text_c: The clutch
correct_answer: B. The steering wheel
answer_information_text: The steering wheel changes the direction in which the vehicle travels by turning the steering wheels. The accelerator controls speed, while the clutch connects or disconnects the engine from the transmission.

question_text: When the footbrake is used, the distance it takes to stop a motor vehicle is: (i) longer on a wet road than on a dry road; (ii) longer if the vehicle is travelling at a higher speed; (iii) longer if the vehicle is loaded. SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
answer_text_a: All of the above are correct
answer_text_b: None of the above are correct
answer_text_c: Only (i) is correct
correct_answer: A. All of the above are correct
answer_information_text: All three statements are correct: stopping distance is longer on a wet road, at a higher speed, and when the vehicle is loaded. Wet conditions reduce tyre grip, higher speed increases the distance travelled during braking, and extra load increases the work the brakes must do.

question_text: In a vehicle with a manual transmission, what must you use to shift from one gear to another?
answer_text_a: Foot brake and gear lever
answer_text_b: Parking brake and the clutch
answer_text_c: Gear lever and the clutch
correct_answer: C. Gear lever and the clutch
answer_information_text: In a manual vehicle, use the clutch while selecting the next gear with the gear lever.

question_text: What is the function of a clutch?
answer_text_a: It is used to disconnect the engine from the transmission
answer_text_b: It is used to freewheel down a hill
answer_text_c: It is used to reduce the speed of a vehicle
correct_answer: A. It is used to disconnect the engine from the transmission
answer_information_text: The clutch temporarily disconnects the engine from the transmission. This allows you to change gear or stop without the engine continuing to drive the wheels.

question_text: To select a gear you must use numbers...
answer_information_text: Selecting a gear in a manual light motor vehicle requires the clutch to disengage the engine from the gearbox while the gear lever selects the required gear. Numbers 6 and 8 represent these two controls. Using them together allows a gear change without damaging the transmission or stalling the engine.

question_text: To stop your vehicle, you must use number...
answer_information_text: Number 9 is the foot-brake pedal, which is used to reduce speed and bring the vehicle to a stop. Apply it smoothly and progressively so that the vehicle remains stable and the wheels do not lock. The parking brake is used to hold a stationary vehicle, not as the normal control for stopping while driving.

question_text: Number...is not found in an automatic vehicle
answer_information_text: Number 8 is the clutch pedal in the standard K53 light-motor-vehicle control diagram. An automatic vehicle changes gears without a driver-operated clutch, so it has no clutch pedal. The driver uses the brake and accelerator pedals and selects the required automatic transmission position instead.

question_text: To turn, number...is used
answer_information_text: Turning requires the steering control, which changes the direction of the front wheels. In this diagram, that steering control is numbered 4.

question_text: To ensure that your parked vehicle, does not move you must use number..
answer_information_text: Number 7 is used to keep a parked vehicle from moving. Apply the parking brake when the vehicle is parked, and select a suitable gear or Park as an additional safeguard.

question_text: To accelerate your vehicle you must use number
answer_information_text: Control 10 is the accelerator, which increases engine speed and makes the vehicle accelerate. Press it smoothly so the vehicle gains speed without losing control.

question_text: What controls must you use when you are going to negotiate a sharp bend in the road?
answer_text_c: 3,4,5,9 and 10 only
answer_information_text: When negotiating a sharp bend, check the mirrors, steer correctly, select a suitable gear and control the vehicle with the pedals. The indicator is not necessarily required unless turning at a junction or changing direction.

question_text: How far must a vehicle's indicator lights be visible to a person of normal eyesight in normal daylight?
answer_information_text: Direction-indicator lamps must be clearly visible in normal daylight from at least 30 m. This requirement appears in Regulation 194.

question_text: Which sequence is correct when moving off in a manual light motor vehicle?
answer_text_a: Select neutral, press the brake pedal, and use the hooter before releasing the clutch.
answer_text_b: Release the parking brake, select first gear, and release the clutch quickly before using the accelerator.
answer_text_c: Depress the clutch (8), select first gear with the gear lever (6), bring the clutch to its biting point while applying the accelerator (10), release the parking brake (7), then release the clutch smoothly.
correct_answer: C. Depress the clutch (8), select first gear with the gear lever (6), bring the clutch to its biting point while applying the accelerator (10), release the parking brake (7), then release the clutch smoothly.
answer_information_text: The image labels 8 as the clutch, 6 as the gear lever, 10 as the accelerator and 7 as the parking brake. Sequence A correctly describes moving off smoothly in a manual light vehicle.

question_text: To change gear smoothly while moving, which sequence should you follow?
answer_text_a: Release the accelerator, depress the clutch fully, move the gear lever to the next gear, then release the clutch progressively while reapplying the accelerator.
answer_text_b: Press the accelerator fully, move the gear lever without using the clutch, and then apply the brake.
answer_text_c: Apply the parking brake, keep the accelerator pressed, and move the gear lever into neutral.
correct_answer: A. Release the accelerator, depress the clutch fully, move the gear lever to the next gear, then release the clutch progressively while reapplying the accelerator.
answer_information_text: The correct smooth gear-changing sequence is to release the accelerator, fully depress the clutch, select the next gear, then progressively release the clutch while reapplying the accelerator. The picture shows the relevant controls but not the sequence itself.

question_text: What is likely to happen if the clutch pedal is held partly down while driving for a long distance?
answer_text_a: The parking brake will release itself.
answer_text_b: The clutch may slip, overheat and wear prematurely.
answer_text_c: The steering wheel will automatically turn the vehicle.
correct_answer: B. The clutch may slip, overheat and wear prematurely.
answer_information_text: Holding the clutch partly down over a long distance causes clutch slip, generating heat and accelerating wear. The other options are unrelated to clutch operation.

question_text: What may happen if the parking brake lever is left partly applied while the vehicle is moving?
answer_text_a: The direction indicators will stop working.
answer_text_b: The accelerator will become more effective.
answer_text_c: The brakes may overheat and wear unnecessarily.
correct_answer: C. The brakes may overheat and wear unnecessarily.
answer_information_text: Leaving the parking brake partly applied while driving can cause the brakes to overheat and wear unnecessarily.

question_text: If Number 5 is still indicating after you have completed a turn, what should you do?
answer_text_a: Cancel the direction indicator when it is safe, so that other road users are not misled.
answer_text_b: Press the accelerator to cancel it automatically.
answer_text_c: Leave it on until the next intersection so that vehicles behind keep their distance.
correct_answer: A. Cancel the direction indicator when it is safe, so that other road users are not misled.
answer_information_text: Cancel the direction indicator when safe after completing the turn, so other road users are not misled.

question_text: When is it appropriate to use the hooter?
answer_text_a: To replace the direction indicator when changing direction.
answer_text_b: To warn another road user of your presence or of an immediate danger when necessary to avoid a collision.
answer_text_c: To show impatience when a vehicle ahead is travelling slowly.
correct_answer: B. To warn another road user of your presence or of an immediate danger when necessary to avoid a collision.
answer_information_text: The hooter may be used when necessary for safety, such as warning another road user of your presence or an immediate danger to avoid a collision. It must not be used to show impatience or replace an indicator.

question_text: When bringing a manual vehicle to a controlled stop, which combination is appropriate as the vehicle comes to rest?
answer_text_a: Press the accelerator and parking brake together while leaving the clutch fully released.
answer_text_b: Switch on the windscreen wiper and move the gear lever without using the clutch.
answer_text_c: Ease off the accelerator, use the foot brake, depress the clutch before the engine labours, and select neutral after stopping.
correct_answer: C. Ease off the accelerator, use the foot brake, depress the clutch before the engine labours, and select neutral after stopping.
answer_information_text: A correctly describes stopping a manual vehicle: use the foot brake, depress the clutch before the engine labours or stalls, and select neutral after stopping.

question_text: Before selecting reverse with Number 6, what should the driver do?
answer_text_a: Bring the vehicle to a complete stop, depress the clutch, and select reverse only after checking that it is safe.
answer_text_b: Apply the accelerator fully before moving the gear lever into reverse.
answer_text_c: Select reverse while the vehicle is still moving forward and release the clutch quickly.
correct_answer: A. Bring the vehicle to a complete stop, depress the clutch, and select reverse only after checking that it is safe.
answer_information_text: The vehicle must be stationary before reverse is selected. Depress the clutch and check that it is safe before engaging reverse.

question_text: What happens when the accelerator is pressed while the clutch pedal is fully depressed?
answer_text_a: The parking brake is automatically applied.
answer_text_b: The engine speed may increase without transferring drive to the wheels.
answer_text_c: The steering wheel becomes locked in a straight position.
correct_answer: B. The engine speed may increase without transferring drive to the wheels.
answer_information_text: With the clutch fully depressed, the engine is disconnected from the drivetrain. Pressing the accelerator can raise engine speed without transferring drive to the wheels.

question_text: When rain begins to reduce forward visibility, how should the windscreen wiper be used?
answer_text_a: Use the direction-indicator lever repeatedly instead of the wiper.
answer_text_b: Apply the parking brake briefly whenever the windscreen becomes wet.
answer_text_c: Switch it on early and select a speed that keeps the windscreen clear for the conditions.
correct_answer: C. Switch it on early and select a speed that keeps the windscreen clear for the conditions.
answer_information_text: The wipers should be switched on as soon as rain reduces visibility, using the speed needed to keep the windscreen clear. The proposed answer is correct.

question_text: Why should the interior and exterior rear-view mirrors be adjusted before moving off?
answer_text_a: To provide useful views behind and to the sides of the vehicle before moving or manoeuvring.
answer_text_b: To increase the engine speed before selecting a gear.
answer_text_c: To make the steering wheel return to the straight-ahead position.
correct_answer: A. To provide useful views behind and to the sides of the vehicle before moving or manoeuvring.
answer_information_text: Mirrors should be adjusted to give useful views behind and alongside the vehicle before moving or manoeuvring. The illustration does not clearly show the exterior mirrors, but the question itself is clear.

question_text: While driving, what is the main purpose of Number 1?
answer_text_a: To show the engine speed
answer_text_b: To see traffic directly behind through the rear window
answer_text_c: To illuminate the road ahead
correct_answer: B. To see traffic directly behind through the rear window
answer_information_text: Number 1 is the rear-view mirror, used to see traffic behind through the rear window.

question_text: What can result from operating the windscreen wiper on a dry, dusty windscreen for a long time?
answer_text_a: The brake pedal may become harder
answer_text_b: The engine may overheat
answer_text_c: The blade and glass may wear, and the view may become smeared
correct_answer: C. The blade and glass may wear, and the view may become smeared
answer_information_text: Using a wiper on a dry, dusty windscreen can wear the blade and scratch or smear the glass, reducing visibility. The other options are unrelated.

question_text: When setting Number 3, which view is most useful?
answer_text_a: A small part of the vehicle and as much adjacent road as possible
answer_text_b: The area directly above the bonnet
answer_text_c: Only the rear seat of the vehicle
correct_answer: A. A small part of the vehicle and as much adjacent road as possible
answer_information_text: Number 3 refers to the side mirrors. They should show a small part of the vehicle and as much adjacent road as possible.

question_text: Why should the steering wheel not be turned hard while the vehicle is stationary unless necessary?
answer_text_a: To stop the direction indicators from flashing
answer_text_b: To avoid unnecessary strain on the tyres and steering system
answer_text_c: To prevent the hooter from sounding
correct_answer: B. To avoid unnecessary strain on the tyres and steering system
answer_information_text: Turning the steering wheel hard while stationary causes unnecessary strain and wear on the tyres and steering system.

question_text: What does an activated direction indicator tell other road users?
answer_text_a: That the driver intends to change direction or position; indicating does not itself give the driver right of way
answer_text_b: That the manoeuvre has already been completed
answer_text_c: That the driver may ignore mirrors and blind spots
correct_answer: A. That the driver intends to change direction or position; indicating does not itself give the driver right of way
answer_information_text: An activated direction indicator communicates the driver's intention to change direction or position. Indicating does not itself give the driver right of way.

question_text: Before starting a manual vehicle, why should Number 6 normally be in neutral?
answer_text_a: To prevent the vehicle from lurching when the starter is operated
answer_text_b: To lock the steering wheel
answer_text_c: To switch off the fuel supply
correct_answer: A. To prevent the vehicle from lurching when the starter is operated
answer_information_text: Number 6 is the gear lever. Selecting neutral prevents the vehicle from moving or lurching when the starter is operated.

question_text: During a lengthy stop in a manual vehicle, which combination reduces unnecessary clutch wear while keeping the vehicle secure?
answer_text_a: Select a low gear, release the foot brake, and partly engage the clutch
answer_text_b: Select neutral, release the clutch, and keep the foot brake applied
answer_text_c: Keep the clutch fully depressed and press the accelerator
correct_answer: B. Select neutral, release the clutch, and keep the foot brake applied
answer_information_text: For a lengthy stop, select neutral and release the clutch to avoid unnecessary clutch wear. Keep the vehicle secured with the brake; the other options either load the clutch or encourage clutch slipping.

question_text: What may happen if the clutch pedal is released too quickly after selecting a gear?
answer_text_a: The mirrors may adjust automatically
answer_text_b: The hooter may sound automatically
answer_text_c: The vehicle may jerk and stall
correct_answer: C. The vehicle may jerk and stall
answer_information_text: Releasing the clutch too quickly can make the vehicle jerk and cause the engine to stall.

question_text: If the gear lever is forced while the clutch is not fully depressed, what is likely to happen?
answer_text_a: The gears may grind and the transmission may be damaged
answer_text_b: The windscreen wiper may change speed
answer_text_c: The steering will become lighter
correct_answer: A. The gears may grind and the transmission may be damaged
answer_information_text: If the clutch is not fully depressed, the gears may not disengage properly. Forcing the gear lever can cause grinding and damage the transmission.

question_text: What is a likely result of resting your foot on the foot brake while driving when braking is not needed?
answer_text_a: The exterior mirrors may fold in
answer_text_b: The brakes may overheat and wear unnecessarily
answer_text_c: The engine oil level may rise
correct_answer: B. The brakes may overheat and wear unnecessarily
answer_information_text: Resting a foot on the brake can apply it slightly, causing unnecessary friction, overheating and wear. The other options are unrelated.

question_text: When descending a steep hill, which control combination helps maintain control?
answer_text_a: Apply the parking brake continuously while steering one-handed
answer_text_b: Select neutral and use the accelerator
answer_text_c: Select a suitable lower gear and use the foot brake as necessary
correct_answer: C. Select a suitable lower gear and use the foot brake as necessary
answer_information_text: A suitable lower gear helps control speed on a steep descent, while the foot brake can be used as necessary. Neutral and continuous parking-brake use are unsafe choices.

question_text: On a slippery surface, how should the accelerator be applied?
answer_text_a: Smoothly and gently to reduce wheel spin
answer_text_b: Fully and suddenly to gain maximum speed
answer_text_c: Repeatedly and rapidly to maintain traction
correct_answer: A. Smoothly and gently to reduce wheel spin
answer_information_text: On a slippery surface, apply the accelerator smoothly and gently to avoid wheel spin and loss of traction.

question_text: When may you use the hooter (Number 11)?
answer_text_a: Whenever you want a slower driver to move aside
answer_text_b: When necessary to warn another road user of your presence
answer_text_c: To greet someone next to the road
correct_answer: B. When necessary to warn another road user of your presence
answer_information_text: The hooter may be used when necessary to warn another road user of your presence. It must not be used merely to hurry, greet, or inconvenience someone.

question_text: What should you do with the parking brake before moving off?
answer_text_a: Pull it up further while pressing the accelerator
answer_text_b: Leave it partly applied to prevent sudden acceleration
answer_text_c: Release it fully after securing the vehicle with the foot brake
correct_answer: C. Release it fully after securing the vehicle with the foot brake
answer_information_text: Before moving off, secure the vehicle with the foot brake and release the parking brake fully. Driving with it applied can reduce control and damage the braking system.

question_text: Why should you avoid resting your foot on the clutch pedal while driving?
answer_text_a: It can partly disengage the clutch and cause unnecessary wear
answer_text_b: It makes the direction indicators flash continuously
answer_text_c: It keeps the brakes applied and overheats them
correct_answer: A. It can partly disengage the clutch and cause unnecessary wear
answer_information_text: Resting a foot on the clutch can partly disengage it, causing clutch slip and unnecessary wear. It should be kept off the pedal unless the clutch is being operated.

question_text: While travelling downhill, why should you not keep Number 8 depressed for longer than necessary?
answer_text_a: It makes the engine increase the vehicle's braking automatically
answer_text_b: It disconnects the engine from the driving wheels and reduces control
answer_text_c: It applies the parking brake to the rear wheels
correct_answer: B. It disconnects the engine from the driving wheels and reduces control
answer_information_text: Number 8 is the clutch pedal. Holding it down disconnects the engine from the driving wheels, removing engine braking and reducing vehicle control while travelling downhill.

question_text: Once a gear has been selected, which controls should be coordinated to move off smoothly in a manual vehicle?
answer_text_a: The hooter and direction-indicator lever
answer_text_b: The foot brake and parking brake only
answer_text_c: The clutch and accelerator pedals
correct_answer: C. The clutch and accelerator pedals
answer_information_text: Moving off smoothly in a manual vehicle requires coordinating clutch release with accelerator application. The other controls are not used for normal coordinated take-off.

question_text: What is the correct general sequence when bringing a manual vehicle to a normal stop?
answer_text_a: Release the accelerator, apply the foot brake and depress the clutch before the engine begins to labour
answer_text_b: Increase accelerator pressure, select a higher gear and then brake
answer_text_c: Depress the clutch first and coast, then use the parking brake
correct_answer: A. Release the accelerator, apply the foot brake and depress the clutch before the engine begins to labour
answer_information_text: For a normal stop, release the accelerator, apply the foot brake, and depress the clutch before the engine begins to labour or stall. Depressing the clutch first would cause unnecessary coasting.

question_text: What can happen if you select a gear that is too high for the vehicle's speed?
answer_text_a: The windscreen wipers will operate more slowly
answer_text_b: The engine may labour and the vehicle may respond poorly to acceleration
answer_text_c: The parking brake will apply automatically
correct_answer: B. The engine may labour and the vehicle may respond poorly to acceleration
answer_information_text: Selecting a gear that is too high can make the engine labour, reducing the vehicle’s ability to accelerate and respond properly.

question_text: When rain begins to restrict your view through the windscreen, what should you do with Number 2?
answer_text_a: Operate it only while the vehicle is stationary
answer_text_b: Leave it off until the windscreen is completely obscured
answer_text_c: Operate it at a suitable speed to maintain a clear view
correct_answer: C. Operate it at a suitable speed to maintain a clear view
answer_information_text: The windscreen wipers should be operated at a suitable speed whenever rain restricts visibility, keeping the windscreen clear.

question_text: Why should sudden movements of Number 4 be avoided when travelling at speed?
answer_text_a: They can cause an abrupt change of direction and loss of control
answer_text_b: They disconnect the engine from the driving wheels
answer_text_c: They automatically engage the parking brake
correct_answer: A. They can cause an abrupt change of direction and loss of control
answer_information_text: Sudden steering-wheel movements can cause an abrupt change of direction, making the vehicle unstable and causing loss of control at speed.

question_text: Before moving off, how should the interior and exterior rear-view mirrors be set?
answer_text_a: They should be adjusted only after the vehicle has reached normal road speed
answer_text_b: They should provide the best possible view behind and alongside without requiring major head movement
answer_text_c: They should mainly show the sides of your own vehicle
correct_answer: B. They should provide the best possible view behind and alongside without requiring major head movement
answer_information_text: Mirrors should be adjusted before moving off to give the best possible view behind and alongside, with minimal head movement. The illustration does not show the mirrors but is unnecessary for answering this general question.

question_text: After completing a turn, what should you check about Number 5?
answer_text_a: That it has applied the foot brake
answer_text_b: That it remains on until the next intersection
answer_text_c: That it has cancelled and is no longer giving a misleading signal
correct_answer: C. That it has cancelled and is no longer giving a misleading signal
answer_information_text: After completing a turn, check that the direction indicator has cancelled and is no longer giving a misleading signal.

question_text: If danger develops ahead, why should Number 11 not be used instead of the foot brake?
answer_text_a: The hooter warns others but does not reduce the vehicle's speed
answer_text_b: The hooter disengages the clutch rather than slowing the vehicle
answer_text_c: The hooter causes the accelerator to remain pressed
correct_answer: A. The hooter warns others but does not reduce the vehicle's speed
answer_information_text: Number 11 is the hooter. It warns other road users but does not slow or stop the vehicle, so the foot brake must be used.

question_text: If luggage blocks the view through the interior rear-view mirror, which controls should you use to observe traffic behind and alongside the vehicle?
answer_text_a: The windscreen wiper, Number 2
answer_text_b: Both exterior rear-view mirrors, Number 3
answer_text_c: The direction-indicator lever, Number 5
correct_answer: B. Both exterior rear-view mirrors, Number 3
answer_information_text: If luggage blocks the interior rear-view mirror, use both exterior rear-view mirrors to observe traffic behind and alongside the vehicle. Number 3 identifies the exterior mirrors.

question_text: What normally happens outside the vehicle when you press Number 9?
answer_text_a: The direction indicators begin flashing
answer_text_b: The exterior mirrors move outward
answer_text_c: The stop lamps illuminate to warn traffic behind
correct_answer: C. The stop lamps illuminate to warn traffic behind
answer_information_text: Number 9 is the brake pedal. Pressing it normally activates the stop lamps, warning traffic behind that the vehicle is slowing or stopping.

question_text: What does operating Number 5 before changing direction tell other road users?
answer_text_a: It shows your intention, but does not give you right of way
answer_text_b: It requires other road users to stop and let you turn
answer_text_c: It confirms that the road you are entering is clear
correct_answer: A. It shows your intention, but does not give you right of way
answer_information_text: Operating number 5 signals your intention to change direction. It does not give you right of way; you must still yield where required.

question_text: Why is it unsafe to place the gear lever in neutral while travelling downhill?
answer_text_a: It prevents the steering wheel from turning
answer_text_b: It removes engine braking and reduces control of the vehicle
answer_text_c: It causes the parking brake to engage automatically
correct_answer: B. It removes engine braking and reduces control of the vehicle
answer_information_text: Selecting neutral while travelling downhill removes engine braking and reduces the driver's control of the vehicle. A suitable lower gear should be selected instead.

question_text: What is likely to happen if Number 8 is released too quickly while moving off?
answer_text_a: The steering may lock in the straight-ahead position
answer_text_b: The stop lamps may remain on
answer_text_c: The vehicle may jerk or the engine may stall
correct_answer: C. The vehicle may jerk or the engine may stall
answer_information_text: Releasing the clutch too quickly while moving off can make the vehicle jerk or cause the engine to stall.

question_text: What can happen if you press the accelerator strongly while keeping the clutch pedal fully depressed?
answer_text_a: The engine may race because drive to the wheels is disconnected
answer_text_b: The parking brake will release automatically
answer_text_c: The vehicle will receive maximum engine braking
correct_answer: A. The engine may race because drive to the wheels is disconnected
answer_information_text: With the clutch fully depressed, the engine is disconnected from the wheels. Pressing the accelerator can therefore make the engine rev or race without driving the vehicle forward.

question_text: What danger can arise if Number 7 is applied suddenly and unnecessarily while the vehicle is moving?
answer_text_a: The engine speed will increase sharply
answer_text_b: The rear wheels may lock and the vehicle may skid
answer_text_c: The windscreen wiper will stop working
correct_answer: B. The rear wheels may lock and the vehicle may skid
answer_information_text: Number 7 is the handbrake. Applying it suddenly while moving can lock the rear wheels and cause the vehicle to skid.

question_text: What is the likely effect of pressing Numbers 9 and 10 at the same time while trying to stop?
answer_text_a: The parking brake automatically holds the vehicle
answer_text_b: The clutch automatically disengages and shortens the stopping distance
answer_text_c: The controls oppose each other and may increase stopping distance or brake strain
correct_answer: C. The controls oppose each other and may increase stopping distance or brake strain
answer_information_text: Pressing the brake and accelerator together makes the controls oppose each other. This can reduce braking effectiveness, increase stopping distance, and place strain on the braking system.

question_text: While changing gear in a moving vehicle, how should you maintain steering control?
answer_text_a: Keep one hand controlling the steering wheel and return the other hand promptly after changing gear
answer_text_b: Release the steering wheel with both hands until the gear is selected
answer_text_c: Hold the gear lever with both hands and steer with your knees
correct_answer: A. Keep one hand controlling the steering wheel and return the other hand promptly after changing gear
answer_information_text: While changing gear, one hand operates the gear lever while the other maintains steering control. The hand used for changing gear should return to the steering wheel promptly.

question_text: Why should you avoid looking down at Number 6 while the vehicle is moving?
answer_text_a: It causes the selected gear to disengage
answer_text_b: It takes your attention and vision away from the road
answer_text_c: It prevents the foot brake from operating
correct_answer: B. It takes your attention and vision away from the road
answer_information_text: Looking down at the gear lever takes your eyes and attention away from the road, reducing control and awareness while driving.

question_text: Which vehicle control is used to warn other road users of immediate danger?
answer_text_a: The hooter or horn.
answer_text_b: The direction indicator.
answer_text_c: The parking brake.
correct_answer: A. The hooter or horn.
answer_information_text: The hooter or horn is used to warn other road users when necessary for safety or to signal immediate danger.

question_text: Which control should be used to keep the windscreen clear when rain reduces visibility?
answer_text_a: The parking brake.
answer_text_b: The windscreen wipers.
answer_text_c: The hazard warning lights.
correct_answer: B. The windscreen wipers.
answer_information_text: Windscreen wipers clear rain from the windscreen and maintain visibility.

question_text: In a manual motor vehicle, which control should be depressed shortly before the vehicle stops to prevent the engine from stalling?
answer_text_a: The parking brake
answer_text_b: The accelerator pedal
answer_text_c: The clutch pedal
correct_answer: C. The clutch pedal
answer_information_text: Depressing the clutch shortly before stopping disengages the engine from the drivetrain and prevents stalling.

question_text: In a manual vehicle, which control assists when a gear is engaged or disengaged?
answer_text_a: The clutch control
answer_text_b: The parking brake
answer_text_c: The accelerator
correct_answer: A. The clutch control
answer_information_text: The clutch temporarily disconnects the engine from the transmission, allowing a gear to be engaged or disengaged.

question_text: Which control is used to bring a moving motor vehicle to a complete standstill?
answer_text_a: The clutch pedal
answer_text_b: The parking brake
answer_text_c: The service brake or foot brake
correct_answer: C. The service brake or foot brake
answer_information_text: The service or foot brake is used to slow and stop a moving vehicle. The parking brake is mainly for holding a stationary vehicle.

question_text: Which numbered control in the picture is the footbrake?
answer_information_text: Control 9 is the footbrake, the middle pedal between the clutch and accelerator. Press it with your right foot to slow down or stop the vehicle.

question_text: Which numbered items would you use to check traffic beside and behind your vehicle?
answer_text_b: 3 and 1
correct_answer: B. 3 and 1
answer_information_text: Use the side mirrors (3) to check traffic beside your vehicle and the rear-view mirror (1) to check traffic behind you.
